The server runs in the lane and writes only `ask/`. It rejects a bad `command`/`path`/`port`
(`bad_request`: one line, at most `LINE_MAX` 4096; a path absolute; a port 1-65535 in digits) or an empty `question`
(`NO_QUESTION`, the runner's `_judge` text), and past a budget refuses (a courtesy, counted as the
runner counts: status `asks` plus unjudged ask files, #831). Else it writes `ask/<id>.json` (`{id,
ts, round, question, context, command?, path?, port?}`) and blocks (a `Watcher`) until `ask/<id>.answer`
or `--ask-timeout` (20 min), then returns the answer or `NO_ANSWER`. Both sides' waits use
`ask_mcp.Waited` (monotonic, less steps over `FROZEN_SECS` 60 s; the server looks every `STEP_SECS`
30 s), so a suspend doesn't expire a question (#453). A failing call returns `isError: true`,
`ask_reviewer failed: <why>; carry on without an answer and say so in your summary.`; a failing
request gets `-32603` with its own id, never `null` (OpenCode drops those and the call hung, #525).
Requests and ask files parse with `store.loads` (lone surrogates become U+FFFD). `tools/call` runs
on its own thread, so `ping` is answered while a question waits; the silence guard ignores the wait.

The runner relays (`ask_mcp.relay`, each tick, woken by the steer bell). Outside the lane it reads
new ask files (no links, at most `FILE_MAX` 256 KiB, `NEW_MAX` a tick, `ASKS_MAX` in all) and
counts each in status `asks` (`{id: "q" | "p" | "x"}`, out of the agent's reach, so deleting files
returns no budget): questions up to `--ask-budget` (2) across all steps, command/path/port requests up to
`PERMISSION_BUDGET` (8) apart. A refused one (`x`) is answered with why, without waking Claude.
Otherwise an `ask` event and a `question` notice: `Q: …`, or `PERMISSION to run: `cmd`` /
`PERMISSION to use the directory D (outside its lane)` / `PERMISSION to connect to TCP port N
(outside its lane)` (a `port` of digits, 1-65535, else refused: `bad_request`) with the `wb allow`
that grants it. The
question is clipped at `QUESTION_CHARS` (2,000), context at `CONTEXT_CHARS` (4,000); continuation
lines are marked `> ` so none passes for workbench's own; `command` and `path` are never clipped.
The phase is `asking` while any question of the round is open (`status.asking` the oldest), set
before the notice is raised; an answer (an `answer` event) or the timeout closes one, and with none
open the phase is `running` again. Each open question's notice gets its own mark (two in one tick
shared one, and acking the first acked both). A question dropped
(timeout, round over) is closed with `NO_ANSWER` as its answer (`ask_mcp.close`; lessons skip it).
However a round ends, `_end_agent` closes every open question (`ask_mcp.close_all`) and clears
`asking`, as `cli.reap` does for a dead runner, and closes never-relayed ask files as `x` (#680:
left, the next round raised one live and held `asking`, pausing every guard). The `wb next` prompt
names the questions left (`ask_mcp.used`).
`wb answer <task> --text|--file` refuses a closed question (`ask_mcp.is_open`); `wb allow` answers
the oldest open permission request (`_permission_asked`), else the question. Every answer goes
through `ask_mcp.answer_once`: the open check and `write_answer` in one step under
`locks/<task>.ask.lock`, as do the runner's `close`, its refusals and the bench's; the loser gets
"<id> was already answered (or closed with NO_ANSWER)", exit 1, status `answered` untouched (#938:
apart, a late answer overwrote `NO_ANSWER` and counted as answered).

**Granting.** `wb allow <task> "<pattern>"… [--path DIR…] [--port N…] [--always]` adds to
`rules/<task>/grants.json` (`context.grant`), and with `--always` to `commands.json`
(`context.allow_always` via `store.edit_config`: locked, through a symlink, mode kept, #495;
refuses a malformed file). It answers a pending question "Claude allowed … Run it again now and
carry on." and, if the agent runs, queues it as a `--now` note: rules are read when OpenCode starts.

**Notes.** `wb steer <task> --text "…"` (queued, running, testing or asking, live runner) is
delivered when the current run ends, before the tests. `--now` wakes the runner (`_steer_bell`),
stops the agent and starts the next round with the note first, marked overriding. During tests it
waits; while waiting for the GPU (or a provider or server, to run the round again: after `RERUN`) it rides the round's prompt (`runner._early_notes`), or after the
tests under `--unload-for-tests`; `cli._when_delivered` says which (an API task's: a provider slot, #1112). An undelivered note goes to the
stuck report; `wb resume` carries it, `wb feedback`/`wb next` drop it and say so.

**Check-ins.** `--checkin MIN` raises a `checkin` notice every MIN minutes of a round with a digest
(*The runner, inside*); Claude reports briefly, logs with `wb note` (a `captain` event), steers if
needed. Off by default: each wake re-reads Claude's whole context (the 10-minute default cost 500K
of a task's 1.2M tokens, 2026-11-17). A cut-short base check raises one regardless; a nudge is a
report line, "nudged once", and so is a session that fills up reading (#1322).

**Progress checks** (`workbench/progress.py`, #95): opt-in, `wb progress on [--after MIN]` / `off`,
`$WB_HOME/progress.json` `{on, after?, ts}`; `after` survives a bare `on`/`off` (`set_enabled`,
#578), `--after 0` clears it; any other `--after` but a finite positive number is refused, and a
stored one that isn't (progress.json by hand) is ignored (`progress.user_after`, #1401).
- **Active work**: each round adds its time less answers and frozen time (`_Clock.ran`) to status
  `active_s`, on or off; GPU waits never count; results carry `active_minutes`. Per step: `wb next`
  stores `step_active_s` and resets `progress_checks`; checks and the ETA use
  `runner.active_so_far` (#815).
- **The check** fires once at the threshold, twice it, four times… (`progress.due`,
  `progress.passed`, status `progress_checks`), never while asking. Threshold: `--after`, else the
  median `active_minutes` a step for size and model (`progress.typical`, `progress.threshold`,
  `tuning._step_minutes`, as `router.expected`) once `TYPICAL_MIN` (3) are timed, at least
  `FLOOR_MIN` (10); before that `DEFAULT_MIN` (20 trivial, 45 significant) (#724: with no history
no check came, and a 1.5-minute typical made every 1.5 minutes a wake). The web app's
  Progress row (`settings._progress_stops`; the pane's until #1283) repeats `DEFAULT_MIN` and `TYPICAL_MIN`: change them together. It is a `checkin` notice
  (`progress: true`): the digest, then `progress.text`, two lines (#1322): `progress check: Nm of
  active work, past the typical Nm` (or `the Nm the user set`) with files changed and whether any
  since the last check, status `progress_mark`, failed tool calls, last tests; then `recommended:`,
  one recommendation: a hint (`wb steer --text`) or a smaller step (`wb steer --now --step --text`,
  opening with `runner.STEP_NOTE`: no auto-fix or self-review after it, status `step_note`, #1300).
- **The recommendation**: after `MIN_TRIES` (2) of each kind on the model, whichever helped more
  (`progress.recommend`); before, a smaller step if nothing changed since the last check, else a
  hint.
- It never authorizes an edit: nothing in it touches `coding.json`.
- **Learning**: the first `wb steer` after a check (status `progress_open`) goes in status
  `interventions` `[{kind: hint|smaller, ts, round, step}]` and the results row, without a line
  of its own in `wb steer`'s output (#1322); `progress.helped(model)` / `helped_by_model(rows)` (over `tuning.judged` rows) count tries and
  landings without a takeover (`tuning.agent_landed`); the next check cites them.

**Stats recording** (`workbench/stats.py`, #404) keeps what only the Stats read (the web app's, #1283),
always: it costs nothing, and the `recording` switch that could turn it off guarded nothing (#1322; a
`recording` key in stats.json is ignored). A `round_end {secs, how, guard?}` event (`how`:
`done`, `stuck`, `handover`, `interrupted`, `failed`; `runner._round_end`); the stopping guard named
(`repeat`, `errors`, `no_edit`, `round`, `silence`, `think`, `handovers`, `spend`) and counted in status
`guards`; speed samples with time to first token (`router.speed_samples`) in status `speeds`; and
`results.for_stats` in the row (`started_at`, `load_secs`, `setup_secs`, `nudges`, `asks` by kind,
`answered`, `guards`, median `speed`, `gpu_w` `{mean, peak}` from status `gpu_w_*`, each only when
measured); the `how` is shown by no reader. `live` and `every`, the settings left, drive the live
view (`wb top`).

**The Stats feed** (`stats.feed`, `wb stats --json`, #405): one object of what was learned. Rows:
`store.results()` kept by `tuning.judged`. An empty section is left out, never zeros (a new install:
`{ts, until, settings, tasks: 0}`); `until` is the next local midnight (`_midnight`), when its counts
from today go stale (#575: the pane re-read at it; since #1283 the web app's Stats view refetches past
it). Keys: `periods` (`week`, `month`, `all`, `savings.PERIODS`: tasks, landed, `accepted_pct`,
`active_minutes`, `api`, below), `models` (the `wb stats` columns, `speed`, `write_trend`, and from `TREND_MIN` 6 rows `write_change_pct`),
`model_lines` (#638: `{lines: [{model, variants, windows, last, …}], more, older}`: models OpenCode
has now, `wb optimize` variants under their source via `variant_of`, renamed ids under the current
one via `renamed_from` or the Ollama digest, #818; at most `stats.STATS_MODEL_LINES` 3, the rest in
`more`, idle past `stats.OLD_DAYS` 90 or unconfigured in `older`, each only when nonzero; the most
recently used first; `models` keeps every id split), `sizes`, `stacks` `{tasks, accepted_pct}`,
`guards`, `helps` (`progress.helped_by_model`), `bench` (each model's newest finished run `{run,
day, passed, of}`, a newer one beside it, never in its place, as `partial` `{…, planned, running}`,
#570; a run is finished once every replay in its plan.json, times `repeat`, is graded or failed to
start; one with no plan is finished), `optimized` (optimize.json's `{window, fits, spill, ts}`).
results.jsonl is read once and the snapshot passed down (#565: 16 reads a feed, 3 s at 20,000 rows). `feed(only=...)` builds just those sections; plain `wb stats` uses `stats.SUMMARY`, `("periods",)`: `stats.summary` prints each period's tasks and landings, no saving, no score, no API line (`wb savings` has them) and none of the tab's other sections (#1322).
Gone (#1322: precision nobody acted on): each period's `savings` and `score`, `spec_gaps` and `energy`
`{wh, cost?}`, `streak`, `bests`, `milestones`, `absorbed`, `questions`, `days` and each model's
`claude`; `wb savings` still says the saving and its energy.

**API tasks in the feed** (#1022). `periods[*].api` is `{tasks, cost, unknown, plan, by_provider:
{p: {tasks, cost, unknown, plan?}}}` (`stats._api_period`, from `savings.api_totals` over every
row, trials in: money spent is spent), only when the period has API rows; `plan` is there so a
plan-only week never reads `API $0`. `model_lines` and `models` take an API model from its rows'
`kind` (discover() lists none) and group by kind as well as by id, so an id run as a GPU model and
then as an API one (an Ollama `:cloud` id, #1013) gives two lines; each has `kind`, an API one
`paid`, its mean dollars a task over the known costs (none known: no `paid`; a task that sent
nothing is none, `results.task_cost`, #1106). The trial-free rows
(`tuning.judged`) give those lines. The web app's Stats view (the pane's Stats tab until #1283): each
period adds `API ≈$1.27 (DeepSeek ≈$0.84 · Anthropic ≈$0.43)` (`apiPeriod`, each provider by its
name, `providerWord`; `API plan usage` or `API no known cost` with no known dollars, `apiMoney`; `+ N
with no known cost` beside known ones), and an API model's line (`API DeepSeek deepseek-flash: …`)
says `paid ~$0.12/task` in place of its write speed.

**Taking over.** `wb takeover <task>` stops the agent and sets `review` ("Claude took over"):
Claude finishes in the worktree uncommitted (accept adds the trailers; a commit made by hand is
kept as is), then accepts or hands back with `wb feedback`. `wb stop` sets `stuck` ("stopped by the
reviewer", worktree kept); `wb resume` continues a stuck or failed task in a fresh session with
`RESUME` and the step's asks, not counted as a review round.

## Context, on both sides

Local models work in a small context window, and so, in its own way, does Claude.

**The agent's.** Rounds continue one OpenCode session until the runner hands it to a fresh one
(*The runner, inside*); OpenCode's compaction sits at least a step's growth past the handover
point (#644). Reports show the fill (`agent context: 19.4K of 32K (60%)`). `--fresh` (on `wb
feedback`/`wb next`) forces a fresh session; `--keep-context` keeps it. Context carries over only
within a task's worktree.

**The slice** (`router.slice`). The first guess is three files and about 150 new lines on 32K,
scaled with the window up to `GUESS_MAX` (4) times. Each closing step records its files and added
lines (`results.step`): bad when compacted, filled up reading first, stuck, or `BAD_REVIEWS` (2)
agent-caused review rounds (a `--spec-gap` round is Claude's); a handover isn't held against it.
The latest steps decide: the smallest bad one lowers the slice, the size most good ones reached
raises it unless steps that big mostly went badly (#720: the biggest good step ever set it for good). `wb models`, `wb start`, `wb scout` show
it. Reports name changed files the spec never mentions (`not in the spec: src/util.c`, `outside_spec`:
path or basename not in the step's prompt, silent when it names none; `src/io.{h,c}` names each file).
The window is what the server serves (*Managing the set*): `wb model add` writes it with an
eighth as output budget; `wb doctor` flags a mismatch or none.

**Claude's record as a spec writer.** `--spec-gap "what it missed"` (`feedback`, `next`, `accept`,
`discard`) marks a round as the spec's fault: `status.spec_gaps` `{round, text}`, counted in the
row (`wb stats` leaves those discards out), a `spec` lesson for Claude's checklist (not an agent
skill), counted by `wb stats` and the web app's Stats view (`wb start`'s `your specs:` line,
`results.spec_gap_line`, went in #1322).

**Self-tuning** (`workbench/tuning.py`). Model-dependent settings are learned per model and window.
`KNOBS`: `fresh_at`, the handover point (default 0.6, candidates 0.4–0.8), and `self_review`
(default 1, candidates 0 and 1; the agent's own review round, *6. The tests gate the round*). A per-task `--self-review`/`--no-self-review`
wins over record and pin (`tune`'s `fixed`) and is evidence for the value it ran. `tune(task,
ceilings)` picks once per task (`status.tuned`, `status.explored`, `status.tuned_max`): the best so
far, or one time in five (`EXPLORE`) its neighbour. `reward`, per step: 1 if accepted
(`agent_landed`; a takeover scores 0, #647), divided by one plus agent-caused review rounds a step,
less `COMPACT_PENALTY` 0.25 if OpenCode compacted, ± up to `SPEED_WEIGHT` 0.15 against the model's
median active minutes a step of the same kind of work (`tuning.work`: the row's `role`, else its size; #543, #721, #1025). Discards score 0; a `--spec-gap`
discard counts nowhere (`judged`), nor one after a stop that wasn't the step's with no step kept
(`tuning.stopped_outside`: the row's `infra`, #1245), nor a compare attempt discarded once another attempt at its item was accepted (the row's `not_chosen`, #1473). `Knob.fills` (`fresh_at`) counts a task only if a session
reached the smallest allowed value (`tuning.acted`, row `peak_share`; older rows count; #721: most
tasks never fill 40%, and one fast trivial task flipped the pick); `Knob.passed` (`self_review`)
only if a round's tests passed (`self_review_due`, set whether or not self-review ran; older rows
`tests_ok`; #816: a task without passing tests ran alike under 0 and 1, and its noise could turn
self-review off), and never a writing task's (row `role: writing`: off by its role, not chosen;
#1025). `probe_aggressive` is gone
(#857): an old pin, row `tuned` value or `status.tuned` entry is never read; only `KNOBS` count.
Means are smoothed toward the pool (`PRIOR`, two tasks' worth); a non-default value needs `TRY_MIN`
(3) tasks before it can be picked (an untried value sits at the pooled mean, so one task above it
won); the pick moves one step at a time. Values past
`runner.fresh_ceiling` (a step's growth, at least `tuning.CEILING_MARGIN` 0.05, before compaction)
are never tried; a window under `models.MIN_WINDOW` (16K) is refused. An output cap that puts the
ceiling under every value makes the ceiling the only value, or the smallest when the ceiling isn't
positive (#595: the smallest stood, past compaction, so every long step compacted); `runner.handover_warning` says
so for a GPU entry in `wb doctor` ("its output cap … puts OpenCode's compaction at N% of the
window…", or "no handover fits" at `HANDOVER_ROOM` or under; until #1322 at every `wb start` too,
and for an API model, whose catalog limits neither wb nor the user can change, #1073), and `optimize.budget` cuts such a
cap to a quarter of the window. Trials aren't evidence. `wb tune` shows the record;
`$WB_HOME/tuning.json` pins (`{"fresh_at": 0.6}`, used as given). A new knob: add it to `KNOBS`,
read it with `tuning.value(task, name)`.

**API self-review** (#1017). Without `--self-review`/`--no-self-review`, an API task's
`self_review` is fixed 0 (`runner.fixed_knobs`, passed as `tune`'s `fixed`): a round Claude never
sees costs money there, so neither the record nor the explore turns it on. `--self-review` is
Claude's word and runs it, and so does a task.json `review_model` (fixed 1: the role's
`thinking_review`, #1059), which `--no-self-review` still turns off.

**Claude's.** `wb` holds the delegation state. Whenever Claude's conversation compacts with this
session's tasks open in a session that delegated, the mod tells the summary to keep goals,
decisions and each task's next need, and drop finished tasks' diffs and reports. At a task boundary
in workbench mode (one just closed, none waiting) it compacts early once halfway to the
engine's own compaction (`WB_COMPACT_AT`, a percentage; 0 off). A session that never delegated is never
compacted for a task (2026-11-16 audit: a task closing compacted every session). After a compaction or `/clear`, a context block lists the
open tasks from `wb status --repo <its directory> --session <id>…`. An OpenCode driver gets the
same from the plugin (`upkeep.ts`, *The OpenCode plugin*): the blocks as session instruction
entries OpenCode sends again after each compaction, KEEP_ON_COMPACT through the `compaction` hook,
and the boundary compaction at `WB_COMPACT_AT` of the way to OpenCode's own (#1315).

**What Claude learns about the user** (`wb notes`): cross-project preferences, `wb notes add "…"`
(at most 300 characters, 20 notes) in `$WB_HOME/notes.md` (`- ` lines, `notes.lock`), handed to
every workbench-mode session in a `user-notes` block (#540: `NOTES_NOTE`, `The user's delegation notes
(\`wb notes\`):` and the notes; when to add or drop one is the skill's, no longer said with them, #1322);
`wb notes drop N…`. One repo's facts go in its CLAUDE.md.

## Waking Claude, exactly once

A run's notices (#1278, *Deep workflows*) are rows `{ts, run, kind, text}` in the same file, no
`task`: `store.notices()` leaves them out (its callers index `task`), `store.notices(runs=True)`
keeps them, `_rotate_notices` moves one once its run's `acked` passes it or the run is closed. An
open run's item (task.json `run`, `runs.item_open`: the run open and its driver alive) notifies its
driver instead (`runs/<run>/notify.jsonl`, with its `noticed` mark, which the driver's ack covers), except
`question` and `checkin` (`store.RUN_GLOBAL`), which only Claude can answer.

Notices go to `$WB_HOME/notify.jsonl` (`Task.notify`: `{ts, task, kind, text, round?, id?, cause?,
guard?, tasks?}`; `guard` `agents` on a `spend` stop for the Agents switch, #1213). Kinds: `review` (report and `review_diff`), `stuck`, `failed`, `question` (with `id`),
`checkin` (periodic, a base check cut short
or whose command wasn't found).
`cause` (`stuck`/`failed` with a round): `guard`, `agent`, `server` (#657), `provider` (an API provider's
`rate_limited`/`outage` after its one revive, `quota`, `auth`: #1020; `refused`: #1082, #1084; the
keyhole's `setup`, this machine's, #1080), `spend` (the day's API spend
cap, #1019: `runner.SPEND`; Agents on GPU, `guard` `agents`, #1213), `updated`
(runners before #1322's `_updated`), `opencode` (`runner.opencode_moved`, OpenCode below 2.0), `local_only` (an API task's repo marked local-only since it started:
`runner.LOCAL_ONLY`, #1215), `signal` (`SIGNAL_STOP`), `died`
(`reap`), `update` (`wb update --stop`). A failure whose text names its own remedy has a cause too, with no round:
`checkout` (`_checkout_failed`), `setup` (`_prepare`), `repo` (`_repo_gone`), `catalog` (`_left_catalog`, both of
`left_catalog`'s lines), `model` (`_load_failed`, not `Damaged`), `disk` (the crash handler's full disk; a crash has
none), so the mod's wake is `OUTSIDE_NEXT`'s (#1247). `tasks` names a batch (restart, shutdown, `wb update
--stop`), or the one task `opencode_moved` stopped, so its wake is an interruption's
(`BATCH_NEXT`, #1176). `wb` itself writes only `reap`'s `failed` and `cli._stop_for_update`'s `stuck`, one per
owner (#694). The file is out of the agent's lane (2026-11-16 audit: it could forge or wipe wakes).
Read through `store.notices()`, whole rows only (a `NAME_RE` task, a kind, a numeric ts: one row
without a task made every acknowledging command raise). A task's
`acked` file is the time up to which Claude has its news; `noticed` its newest notice's ts (for
every task a batch names; #844). A `ts` is later than every earlier notice and the task's `acked`,
under the lock (`append_jsonl(…, after=)`, `store.newest_ts`; #473: a backward clock hid notices).
A batch's other tasks are acked up to the row's stamp as written, never below their mark
(`store.ack_batch`, #874).

- **Ears.** The mod runs `wb events` (*Waiting without polling*) and re-reads tasks on each line.
- **Still true.** The newest notice under an hour old past `acked` (and every open question) is
  delivered only while true: a check-in while queued, running or testing; a question while
  `asking` with no `ask/<id>.answer`; else while the phase matches the kind. A stale one is acked
  and dropped.
- **Held mid-turn.** While Claude is mid-turn (`mem.busy`, set by `turn.start` or the model's own
  `tool.call`) the wake waits (a prompt submitted then would queue and arrive stale) and is
  rechecked each poll and after the turn. A question doesn't wait (its agent is blocked): it goes into the running turn
  (`session.send`, `MIDTURN_NOTE`); if refused and then closed with `NO_ANSWER`, it wakes Claude
  after the turn with `MISSED_NOTE` (#542). Otherwise the mod writes `acked`, toasts, and submits
  `[workbench] Task <n> <headline>.`, the text and the next commands (`NEXT[kind]` in
  `register.tsx`; a `cause` outside the step's, `OUTSIDE_NEXT`, #1247; a question names `wb answer <n> --id <id>`, a PERMISSION one its `wb allow`); a batch wakes as `[workbench] Tasks <a>, <b> were interrupted.` with
  `BATCH_NEXT` (#544). A prompt the engine drops puts `acked` back (unless something acted since)
  and the safety net retries.
- **Acting acknowledges.** `feedback`, `next`, `answer`, `allow`, `note`, `resume`, `takeover`,
  `accept`, `discard`, `stop` ack the task (`cli._ack_all`), stopping just before the oldest unacked
  notice of the kind the phase stands for (`question` while asking, `checkin` while queued, running
  or testing, else the phase's name), else at now; never backwards (a note seconds after a failure
  once swallowed its notice for an hour). `answer`, `allow` (answering), `feedback`, `next`,
  `resume` move it to when they acted (an answered question came back from `wb wait`), but while
  asking still stop before another open question's notice.
- **The safety net** (`rewake`): a task waiting on Claude (review, asking, stuck, failed) a minute after its last status change,
  newest notice unacked (by notify.jsonl's tail or `noticed`, #844), wakes Claude once with `wb
  report <n>`, and the headline and next step deliver's wake would have given its newest notice
  (`headlineOf`, `nextOf`: from the phase alone a provider's, a day-cap, an Agents-GPU or a
  local-only stop woke as "got stuck … Steer it with wb feedback", #1384); none in the tail, the
  phase's.
- **Without the mod.** `wb wait [task]` blocks for news past `acked`, prints `[kind] task` and the
  text, and acks it, skipping what the mod would (`_stale`; of a task's questions only the oldest
  open, `_oldest_open`, judged by the answer files), partial rows and gone tasks; it reaps first.
  Exit 2 for a named closed task, a bare wait with nothing open, or `--timeout`. A notice taken
  elsewhere is reprinted "(already delivered once)"; a task stopped by hand prints `[<phase>]
  <task> (no notice: <last>)`; one failed as dead under 10 s ago waits for its notice.
- **Off switch.** The plugin's `wake` setting stops prompts, keeping pane and toasts; a
  `workbench-wake` context block (#540) tells Claude no wake will come.

The state directory is global, so a session wakes, rewakes and compacts only for its own tasks
(`mine`). `wb start` records `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` (task.json `session`), `CLAUDE_PID`
(`claude_pid`), its start (`claude_start`, `models._started`) and `claude_machine`; the mod keeps
every session id its process had (`$.session.id()` at start and each poll, since /clear and a
resume change it: the `sessions` atom), and a task with a `session` is the session's whose ids hold
it, wherever it ran (0.90 review: by directory alone, a task started from `~` was every session's
there). Once the process is gone (`cli._gone`, `models._alive`: no `/proc/<pid>`, else `kill -0`
fails, #700; or a recycled pid, #532; never judged for another machine's pid, #922; the mod's
`noteClaude`, a live one rechecked at most every 30 s, a gone one final), the task is also claimed
by directory, so a new `claude` in the repo adopts it (0.90 review: after a crash or an update it
was woken for none). The first claimer wins (#687): the mod, knowing its process from `wb events`'s
hello (`parent`, `parent_start`, `machine`), runs, for an open task whose process is gone and that
it would own, `wb adopt <task> --pid <its process> --session <ids…>` (`claim`), which under the
command lock rewrites `session` (kept when one of the given ids), `claude_pid`, `claude_start`,
`claude_machine`, and refuses (exit 1) while the recorded process lives; the mod re-reads task.json
either way, so every other session sees a live process and drops the task.
The wake is a compare-and-set: `wb ack <task> <ts>` raises `acked` under the `ack` lock only if below
`ts` (`cli.claim_ack`, shared with `wb wait`); exit 3 wakes no one. An undelivered wake is released
by `wb ack <task> <prev> --if <ts>` (`cli.release_ack`), only while the mark is still that `ts`
(#786). A `wb` that can't run leaves the mod's own write, which only raises the mark (`raiseAck`).
A run's own notices (`run`, no `task`: *Deep workflows*) take the same path through `deliverRuns`, with `--run`
on each `wb ack`; read as a task named `''` before #1278's S9, they woke no one.
Two live sessions in one repo keep their own; a task with a `session` but no `claude_pid` stays its
session's. One without a `session` goes by
directory: its `repo` is or is inside the session's directory, or the session's directory is inside
the task's spot (`repo`/`subdir`, else a `cwd` inside the repo, else the repo: the kernel's `owns`, `_scope`;
#695), or its `cwd` is or is inside the session's directory; by whole components of real paths,
case-folded where the file system ignores case (`mem.fold`, `store.folds_case`: any component of the path found
in its parent with its case swapped, WSL2's `/mnt/c` too, #1217; 2026-11-19 audit). A
session in `~` or `/` claims none by directory, but for a gone session's task whose `cwd` is
exactly there (`owns`, `_scope`: plain `claude` restarted in `~` after a `wb start --repo
~/proj` there was woken for none, #1403); a task with neither key is everyone's. Another
session's notice is at most toasted. `wb status`, a bare `wait`, and `stop`/`takeover`/`resume
--all` from Claude Code's Bash take the caller's scope (`cli._caller`: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`,
`claude-sessions/<CLAUDE_PID>` under this process's start, #787, the directory; `--all-sessions`
for all; #693; an OpenCode driver's: *The OpenCode driver* below). Among owners the first to deliver wins. A session with no person (`claude -p`) does
nothing until a surface attaches.

### The OpenCode driver: whose task it is
On the OpenCode path (2.2, #1296) the driver (the model with the final say) is an OpenCode
session, and its identity is `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (#1309): the workbench plugin's tools set it on
their `wb` child, and OpenCode sets it in every shell, the agents' own shells included. So
`WB_TASK` outranks it (an agent is never a driver: `store.opencode_session` is "" under it), and
`CLAUDECODE=1` outranks the session id, so Claude Code's path reads exactly what it read before 2.2.
`store.caller_kind` ranks `WB_TASK` first of all: `agent`, a model's call at the gates whatever
else its shell holds (#1310), then `claude`, `opencode`, `terminal`. No flag
and no variable of the plugin's marks a driver, and the plugin stamps nothing on a shell: a missing
plugin can only fail to ask, never open a gate (`store.under_model`, *The gate*).
- **task.json.** `wb start` records the session as `session`, as a Claude Code task's, and `driver`
  `{tool: "opencode", machine, pid?, start?, store?, seen?, model?, variant?}` (`store.driver_record`):
  the session's server is the beating OpenCode server `wb` runs under (`store._lineage`: its tool's
  child, or its shell's), whose store holds the session even before a listing caught it, `seen`
  now; else the running server whose beat lists the session, a fresh beat first, a stale one too
  (a busy service: the #1309 third review), `seen` that beat's `ts`. From it: `pid`, `start` that
  process's start as wb reads it (`models._started`, never the beat's), `store` (the beat's), the
  model and variant. No beat (no plugin yet, or none listing the session): none of those, and the
  task reads `unknown` until a later beat lists its session: `cli._scope` fills them in then
  (`store.driver_fill`: that beat's server, `store`, `seen` its `ts`; under the task's command lock,
  never waited for), so a task started before the plugin beat can still be gone, and adopted, one
  day (the #1309 re-review). No `claude_pid`: OpenCode's shells run in a long-lived server, which outlives the
  session. The mod's `mine` takes no OpenCode task once it has its own session ids (`mem.ids`):
  its `session` is none the mod's process had, and with no `claude_pid` it is never gone to the
  mod. Before the mod has an id, its directory rule could match one (a check of `driver.tool` in
  `mine` is for later).
- **The heartbeat.** The workbench plugin's server part writes it (#1316: `opencode-plugin/driver.ts`
  lists its store every `BEAT_MS` 30 s and hands the listing to `wb driver beat`, `driver.write_beat`,
  which writes the file: *The driver*); wb reads it for the tasks' owners and the web chat's OpenCode
  listener (`store.beat_of(pid)`, one server's fresh beat, `chat._server_listens`, #1319). One file per OpenCode server, `drivers/opencode-<machine_tag>-<pid>.json`
  (`store.beat_path`), never one for them all: the background service, every
  `opencode --standalone` TUI and wb's own `--standalone` helpers (`models._opencode_json`,
  `keyhole._opencode`, the runner's export, which load the user's global plugin too) are each a
  server, and with one shared file any of them, beating its own pid and none of the service's
  sessions, made a live session's task read as gone, so another session nearby took it, its
  notice and `wb adopt` (the #1309 review, 2026-11-25; #693/#696's kind). Each beat, rewritten
  every 30 s, is `{tool: "opencode", pid, machine?, store?, ts, sessions: {<id>: {model?, variant?, dir?, used?}}}`
  (`pid` the name's; a file not of that shape, or of another machine's tag or `machine`, is left
  out; one of this machine's whose pid has exited is removed: `store.heartbeats`). **Which sessions
  are live** (#1296 row 3, "the session no longer exists"): `store` is the server's database (an
  absolute path: OpenCode's data dir and `opencode.db`, or `OPENCODE_DB`), and `sessions` every
  session in it (the plugin's `session.list`, unfiltered, every page), whether any server serves
  it or not; `ts` is when that listing began. A beat that can't list its whole store (a failed or
  partial listing, an `OPENCODE_DB` of `:memory:`) names no `store`: its `sessions` can then say
  live, never gone. A session outlives its server, so a server's exit says nothing of it.
  `store.driver_server(session, driver)`: `live` (a fresh beat, `store.HEARTBEAT_FRESH` 120 s, of a
  running server lists the session; the recorded server's beat first, else the newest, is
  returned), `gone` (a fresh beat of a running server of the store the task recorded, its listing
  begun after the task's `seen`, leaves the session out: deleted), `unknown` (no store recorded,
  no plugin having beaten at `wb start`; no fresh beat of that store: a laptop asleep, a stopped,
  restarting or busy service, a stalled timer; another machine's task, #922's rule). Only positive
  evidence makes a task `gone`: never another store's beat, never a stale beat, never a server's
  exit (the #1309 reviews, 2026-11-25: each read as gone, and another session nearby took its
  tasks, their notices and `wb adopt`; the third, a service restart whose new beat didn't list the
  session yet), as `cli._gone` never says gone while Claude Code's process lives; and only `gone`
  hands a task on (`store.driver_state`).
- **Scope.** `cli._caller` from an OpenCode driver is the session's one id (an OpenCode session keeps
  it; no `claude-sessions/` ledger) and the directory, with the driver's kind; `cli._scope`'s
  directory rule claims a gone owner's task only for the same driver (`store.driver_of`), so neither
  host's sessions take the other's tasks by directory. `wb status`, a bare `wb wait` (a notice
  goes to the session that owns its task), `stop`/`takeover`/`resume --all` follow it.
- **Adoption.** `wb adopt <task>` from an OpenCode driver (`cli._adopt_opencode`) takes a task
  whose owner is gone, from either driver: an OpenCode session `gone` by its store's heartbeat, a
  Claude Code process gone (`cli._gone`; one with no `claude_pid` is not known gone); a user moving
  a project between the two hands its tasks over with it, and the task records the adopting
  session's server (`store.driver_record`). wb permits `wb adopt --session … --pid` of an OpenCode
  task once its session is `gone`, but the unchanged Claude Code mod never calls it for one: its
  `claim` needs the task's `claude_pid` in `mem.deadPids`, and `noteClaude` never notes a task
  without a `claude_pid`.
- **Agents.** Under `WB_TASK` the agent's own shells carry OpenCode's id for their session, which
  is never a driver's; `wb bench run` and `wb optimize` drop it from their replays' environment, as
  they drop Claude Code's.

### The driver
Which model has the final say on the OpenCode path (#1316, by the host-shape decision): whatever
the OpenCode session runs on, picked in OpenCode's own `/models` (variants included) or set by the
`workbench` agent's `model`. wb doesn't own the choice; it records it and says what it means.
Under Claude Code the driver is Claude Code, fixed (`driver.CLAUDE_CODE`, "Claude Code (fixed)"),
and nothing here changes that path.

- **Recorded.** The plugin's server part (`opencode-plugin/driver.ts`, `startDriver`) keeps, per
  session, the model of its last `primary` request (OpenCode's `model.request` hook; a `title`,
  `compaction` or `generate` request may use a small model and is never the driver) and of a
  `session.model.selected` event (a `/models` pick, before its first request). Every `BEAT_MS` 30
  s (the first after `FIRST_BEAT_MS` 1 s) it lists its store's sessions (`session.list`, every page:
  `listAll`), each with that model or, before any request, its selection, its directory and
  `used` (the last primary request, epoch seconds), and pipes the listing to `wb driver beat`
  (`driver.write_beat`): wb checks it (the `pid` must be a process the call runs under,
  `store._lineage`, so no other process's beat is written; `ts` a time; each row's `model` an id
  `routes.driver_ref` parses, `dir` absolute) and writes the heartbeat, `machine` added (*The
  heartbeat*). `store` is OpenCode's database path as its CLI resolves it (`storePath`:
  `OPENCODE_DB`, else `opencode.db` on the release channels or with
  `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB`, else `opencode-<channel>.db`, under `XDG_DATA_HOME`'s
  `opencode/`; `cli/src/database-path.ts`), and only for a whole listing: a failed page leaves it
  out, so its sessions can say live, never gone. The pages are newest-updated first (50 a page), so
  a session updated while they are read moves ahead of the cursor: `listAll` reads the first page
  again at the end, adds its rows not yet seen, and calls the listing whole only when that page's
  oldest `time.updated` is before the listing began (or it is empty); else no `store` (the review of
  #1316). Nothing listed at all writes no beat. A hook or
  event stream the server refuses costs only its piece. wb's own OpenCode calls remove the plugin
  (`models.plugin_off`), so they never beat.
- **The pin.** routes.json's top-level `driver` (`routes.normalize`; absent, `session`, or a hand
  edit that isn't an id `routes.driver_ref` parses: each session's own choice, never an unreadable
  file, as the mod's `routesValid` doesn't read the key) is an optional standing default, not a fourth role: nothing routes a task
  by it. `wb route driver <provider/model>[#variant]|session` sets it (`routes.driver_change`): a GPU
  model's (`models.gpu_side`) needs no yes; any other id is taken for an API model, failing closed,
  and from a model's call takes the host's dialog (`route-ok.json`, as a role's API change),
  since the session's whole conversation, the code in it, would go to its provider. The plugin's
  RPC `pin` method (`applyPin`) reads `wb route driver --json` and switches the session to it
  (`session.switchModel`) unless it is `session` or the session's already; `/workbench` (`pane.ts`)
  applies it before it switches the session to the Workbench agent, so the notes said at that switch
  are the pinned model's.
- **What wb says** (`driver.info`, `wb driver`, the RPC's `driver` method): the session's model, its
  beat's, or with `--model` the TUI's selection (`driver.selected`: OpenCode commits a `/models` pick,
  and a new session's model, to the session only at its next prompt, so no beat has it before; its
  `dir` kept, its `used` only for the same model; the live check, 2026-11-26)
  (`label`: `provider/id#variant`, or `not known yet …` before its first request), `kind` (`gpu`:
  `discover()` finds it; `api`: OpenCode's catalog lists it, `models.lookup`, cached first;
  `unknown`), its `window` (`limit.context`), the pin, and three notes, each never a refusal (wb
  can't make a weak model hold the bar) and said once per key with `--once` (`driver.once`,
  `drivers/said.json`, the newest `SAID_KEEP` 400 kept):
  - `own:<id>`: the driver is the agents' own model (`driver.agents_models`: each role's API model,
    GPU pin or the router's pick; the same id or `models.identity`): its review isn't independent
    and the handoff saves nothing. `wb doctor` says it every time for each live driver
    (`driver.doctor_lines`).
  - `local:<id>:<place>`: an API (or unknown) driver in a `local_only` repo
    (`privacy.local_only_place`): local_only keeps API models off the agents only, so the code
    reaches the API through the driver.
  - `small:<id>`: the `/workbench` procedure (`skill/workbench/SKILL.md`, about a token per
    `BYTES_PER_TOKEN` 4 bytes) takes `context.FIXED_SHARE` 40% of the window or more.
- **The pane** (`pane.tsx`, `pane-view.ts`'s `driverRow`): the panel's first row, `driver:
  <provider/id#variant> (GPU|API)`, ` · pin <id>` when the pin names another model, and ` · change`:
  the row's press dispatches the TUI's `model.list` (`MODELS`, OpenCode's own `/models`), as the
  choice is OpenCode's. It is wb's answer for the TUI's selection (`ui.model.current()`, reactive,
  handed in as `model`), asked again at each change of it, an older answer dropped. The notes are
  toasted when the session on screen becomes Workbench's (`driver` with `once` and the selection,
  `SETTLE_MS` 0.5 s after, as the TUI's selection follows the new agent), and only then: `--once`
  records a note as said. A beat's variant `default` (OpenCode's word for the model's own) is none
  (`variantOf`).
- **The web app's Settings** row `driver` (*The admin table (settings.py)*); `wb doctor`'s `--`
  line for a live driver that is the agents' own model, after the OpenCode plugin's lines.

### A local driver on the GPU
A driver on this machine's GPU (#1317) is held like a running task's model. `store.driver_models()`:
the models of the sessions in this machine's fresh beats (`HEARTBEAT_FRESH`, the server running)
that drove within `store.DRIVER_HOLD` 1800 s (`used`). `models.keep_loaded()` adds them, so a
round's `free_gpu` never unloads the driver's model and its next turn doesn't reload it and evict
the agent's. Only against coding loads: a job that takes the GPU to itself (`wb image`, `wb audio`,
`--unload-for-tests`, `wb optimize`: `free_gpu` with no `of`, `media.settle`'s `models.freed`, a
box's turn, `optimize.candidates`) reads `keep_loaded(drivers=False)` and unloads the driver's
model as before, its next turn reloading it; no exclusive lease waits for a driver, which may be
the one waiting on its own `wb image`. `models.driver_holders(m)`: each such model `discover()` finds on `m`'s GPU, not `m`
itself (the same model shares), and resident, as an admission-only holder
(`driver:<id>`, `models.DRIVER_HOLDER`, never written to gpu.json): `GpuLease` admits `m` beside
it only when `admits` says both fit, else the task queues, `waiting for the GPU (held by the
driver's <id> (<GB> GB))`, re-checked each `QUEUE_POLL` while queued (`_driver_waits`), and
`load()`'s `_fits_beside` counts it as kept. `wb start` names it (`the GPU is busy with the
driver's …`, `cli._gpu_wait`) and the way out (`cli._driver_way_out`: it leaves only once Ollama
unloads it or its session idles `DRIVER_HOLD`; a smaller model for either side, an API role or an
API driver runs it sooner; a server engine's model `stays loaded on its server (it never unloads)`
until the session idles, and only the driver's own model, an API role or an API driver runs it
sooner, #1476; `this session's own <id>`, `so it waits on this session`, when the
caller's `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` drives on it, `store.driver_models(session)`); a bench never
preempts it (`_preempt_bench`). The router ranks a model that would wait on it (`Score.waits_on`)
after those that run now (*Found, loaded, chosen*). An API driver, a
stale beat or a session idle past `DRIVER_HOLD` holds nothing (`DriverLease`).

## Seeing what the agent does

**Which model, and why** (#1016): `wb start`'s `model:` line (an API task's
`model: <id> · API (<provider>) · trivial role · thinking off`, `routes.model_line`, no `set by you` stamp, #1322;
its thinking `thinking_shown`, what the task does, never only the role's setting, #1237;
a GPU task's as before), `wb status`'s `via` column, `wb watch`'s `routed:` line (`transcript.routed_text`:
an API task's `API <id> (<provider>) · <role> role · thinking off` from task.json,
else task.json `route`, the router's why), the pane's row (`API DeepSeek  deepseek-flash`: the place and the model, tasks.ts's `placeOf`, #1048)
and its `routed` line under the task line, and the web chat's strip over the thread (`Running:
fix-auth · API deepseek-flash (DeepSeek)`, from `chat.open_tasks`): while away, the chat is all the
user sees.

- **The terminal is primary; the web chat is a second lane** (the owner, 2026-11-24: "the terminal
  stays the primary method of doing things with claude, the chat app only a secondary lane. the
  settings of the app are authoritative though, but Claude should retain the ability to help the
  user with the settings when requested"). The work is asked for and reviewed in the terminal; the
  settings and the Stats are the web app's (*The web chat*), and what the web app's Settings hold is
  what wb runs by. Claude still helps with a setting when the user asks, through the `wb` command
  that owns it, on their yes; the API-provider consent dialog stays as it is (*The roles' consent
  gate*).
- **The pane** (opened by `/workbench`, or once per load when a task runs) is the Tasks view alone
  (#1283: no tabs, no `1`-`3` keys, no Stats or Settings). Its last row is the modeline (`modeline`,
  `mod/hooks/modeline.ts`): `[•_•] Claude's Workbench - <the web app's link>` (`FACE.rest`,
  `MODELINE`) on the theme's `claude` colour with bold `inverseText`, from the `chat` atom's `link`
  (`chat-5`): `up` or `started` the link; `checking` `… - starting the web app…`; `off` `… - web app
  off (wb chat on)`; `blocked` or `failed` `… - web app down: <why>`, the why cut to the room with
  `…`. The room is the pane's `bodyColumns` less its padding of 1 each side. Too narrow for the whole
  line it reads `[•_•] <link>`; narrower still the bar says `[•_•] Claude's Workbench` and the link
  goes on bar-coloured rows of its own under it (key `modeline-url-<n>`), cut by characters, never
  by words, so it stays one link to copy. The link comes from `chatLink`: `wb chat url --json`
  (its `state`, `url`, `why`; `linkOf` reads it whole or not at all) at `session.start`, every
  `CHAT_CHECK_MS` (60 s), at once when chat/switch.json changes (`readSwitch`, a `wb chat on|off`),
  and again `CHAT_RECHECK_MS` (3 s) after a newly `started`, `failed` or `blocked`, once: one that
  stays down waits the minute. A url is taken only whole (`/^https?:\/\/\S+#token=\S+$/`), and
  `off` shows none. A wb older than `--json` (a nonzero exit or output that isn't JSON): plain `wb
  chat url`, a link read as `up`, anything else `failed` with wb's line. The web chat counts as on
  (`webOn`: away, the listener, the phone's dialogs) unless the link says `off`.
  **The opening animation** (#963, `mod/hooks/splash.ts`; the owner, 2026-11-21: about five
  seconds, no cost after startup) plays at the `/workbench` that turns the mode on (`skill.prompt`,
  before `showPane`): a body-sized Raster (key `splash`) at `SPLASH_MS` (80 ms), its words landing
  in the modeline's bar on the row from `pageShape`/`splashTarget` (recomputed each draw: the
  modeline's own row, above the link's rows when it wraps, #1283), or rising away when no row is
  exact (`NARROW`), never on a guessed row. A key skips it and still acts; a close, a small pane,
  no Raster or a refused blit end it; a resize replans it (ending there killed it in every real
  session, 2026-11-21). Typing doesn't skip it: a `prompt.edit` hook can't be removed and would
  slow every keystroke. The `splash` atom (`splash-1`) is set at that `/workbench` and cleared by
  `workbenchMode` when the mode goes off, so reloads and bring-backs never replay it. Whether it
  plays is the web app's Settings' (`splash.json`, `splashOn`; `wb splash on|off`). Big at 56×24
  up, small at 40-55 columns or 20-23 rows, none below. Frames are computed as they play from font
  tables and apprentice.ts's `pixels(pose, over)`, nothing at module load, no file read;
  non-apprentice colours go through `atLum` (WCAG luminance 0.105-0.295). It ports forge.py, the
  reference generator, exactly (hash, arithmetic order, half-to-even rounding): the tests hold
  frames 0-41 at 60x26 and 40x22. Its words are `plan`'s `lines`, `LINES` (CLAUDE'S WORKBENCH)
  unless given: the last line cool, any above it warm, the title's rows from their count. The
  OpenCode plugin plays the same frames with `['WORKBENCH']`, drawn as spans (*The OpenCode
  plugin*, `spans.ts`), and paints apprentice.ts's `LAMP` colours in its theme's.
  Closed by the user (mark, Esc), the pane is minimized to a strip above the prompt (one
  `▸ Workbench` Button, key `restore`, and `STRIP_HINT`) while workbench mode is on or tasks exist;
  a press or `/workbench` brings it back, a quit clears it, a reload doesn't reopen it.
  The Tasks view lists every task and follows one as a live transcript: the followed one while live,
  else the newest started running/testing/asking, then queued, else the newest waiting for Claude
  (never by latest status write, which flipped on every tool call). At its foot the apprentice
  shows the phase and says what it does and the time left, or who acts next ("Claude reviews
  next.", #103), as do the transcript's last line and status `last`; then the API day cap's line
  while an API task works (*The Tasks view*), then the modeline. The week's saving and API dollars
  are the web app's Stats (#1283: the pane runs no `wb savings`, `wb stats` or `wb top`).
  **Settings changed on the web app** (#1283's addendum). The web app's Settings write wb's own
  files through wb, and append each change to `$WB_HOME/settings-changes.jsonl` (`{ts, key, label?,
  from, to, said, help?, by: "web"}`). `settingsTurns` reads its tail (64 KB) at each poll when its
  size or mtime moved, in the session that listens (chat/listener.json) or any while none does (a claim stands as
  `listen` reads it, `claimStands`: a session ended in workbench mode leaves its claim), and
  takes each `by: "web"` row newer than `$.store`'s `settingsSeen` mark (every session's, so a
  reload or a second session says it never again; no older than `OLDEST_WAKE_MS`). A row with
  `help` (a setting on but not working yet, such as Agent code navigation with no probe) toasts
  `workbench: <label> changed on the web app: Claude will offer to set it up` and queues a
  `[workbench]` turn (`mem.queued`): `The user changed <label> from <from> to <to> on the web app.
  wb said: <said>`, the help, and `Offer to help with it, and install or change nothing without
  their yes.` (`SETTING_HELP`, `settingSaid`). One without goes in as one quiet `[workbench]` row
  (no turn); the roles, the busy row, the cap, Claude coding and Dynamic workflows (`SAID_ELSEWHERE`)
  are left out of it, as `unsaid` says them already (*The roles in the conversation*, *The rules
  said later*).
- **The status line**: `⚒ wb · add-scores running r2 · fix-typo asks · 1 awaiting review · 1 stuck`, or `⚒
  wb · workbench mode`. Outside workbench mode it counts only `mine`, and is empty without one
  (2026-11-17).
- **`wb watch [task]`** (`workbench/transcript.py`): the transcript in a terminal. It re-exports
  only when the task directory or status `session`/`updated_at` changed, or `EXPORT_EVERY` (30 s)
  passed while live (#555); it calls `cli.reap` every `REAP_EVERY` (60 s) while live.
- **`wb status`**, **`wb log [-f]`**, **`wb report [--round N]`**, **`wb diff [--stat] [--all]
  [paths]`**: Claude's compact views. `wb status` reaps a silently dead runner (`failed`) and marks
  one dead within `REAP_GRACE` with `?`.

**The transcript** (`transcript.follow`) merges the exports of the current and earlier sessions
(`status.sessions`) with the task's events, by time, each entry once (keyed by message and part).
`opencode session export <id> --standalone` runs from `/` (30 s); with no id yet, `opencode session
list --standalone` in the worktree finds `wb: <task>`. Standalone so they never need the background
service's port (2026-11-16 audit); a failure is said once per process (`opencode session export
failed: …`). The same export feeds the runner (`transcript.export`). Everything printed for a
person passes `transcript.plain`: control characters but newline and tab (C1 too) become `\xNN`,
so an escape (OSC 52) never reaches the terminal; `wb log` and `wb report` do the same on a
terminal.
Drawn in Claude Code's grammar (results under `  ⎿  `). Prompt labels match the prompt's first
words (`Claude → agent · spec`, `· review feedback`, `· next step`, `· INTERRUPT, high priority`,
`· note`; `workbench → agent · tests failed, sent back automatically`, `· fresh session: the task,
the work so far, what's next`, `· the round again, after its provider or server stopped it`); the protocol folds to `(+ the workbench protocol; -v shows it)`.
`ask_reviewer` calls are left out for their `ask`/`answer` events. Each model call gets `⏱ N tokens
in (M cached), read in Xs · K out in Ys · R tok/s`. `-v` raises the caps. Under it: `activity`
(queued: `status.last`, #869, else `Waiting for the GPU…`, an API task's `Starting…`, and its
phase line `■ waiting to start` (`transcript.API_QUEUED_LINE`), never the GPU's, #1112; testing, asking; running: the server's `GET
<root>/metrics` `live` object `{state, phase, prompt_tokens, generated, tok_s}`, which
`models._server_idle` reads too; without one, a rotating verb) and the clock (`⏲ task T · round N t
· model load t`, the ETA from `router.expected_minutes`, the median active minutes a step on the
task's `weights_id` from the files alone, never the server (#819), against `runner.active_so_far`
(#543), then `context U of WK (P%)`).

**`wb watch <task> --json`** (hidden) is the mod's feed: one pass, `{"s": style, "t": text}` per
line: `meta`, the transcript (styles `claude`, `agent`, `think`, `tool`, `out`, `ok`, `bad`, `sys`,
`add`, `del`, `head`, `""`), `activity` if any, `clock`, the phase line. Text is cut to
`JSON_LINE_CHARS` 2000; `--last N` (hidden) keeps the newest N transcript lines (the engine keeps
only a command's first 4 MiB). Earlier sessions are exported once ever into
`tasks/<t>/.export-<sid>.json` (`transcript.finished_export`, #691). The mod runs it with `--last
2000` while the pane is shown, every 5 s while the followed task is active (#691), at once when the
followed task changes; past 4 MiB it keeps its lines and adds `transcript too long for the pane`;
it cuts to `LINE_CHARS` 2000 and uses `activity` as the apprentice's speech, the pose `work` when it
starts `Writing` or `Running`, else `think` (reword those and update the mod). A new style needs an
entry in the mod's `LINE_STYLE`; changing the shape needs a new `live-1` tag.

**`wb watch <task> --export`** (hidden) is the OpenCode plugin's (`children.ts`, #1331): one JSON
object, `{"task", "sessions": [{"session", "current", "messages"}], "missing"}`, each of the
task's sessions earlier ones first (status `sessions`, then the current one), its messages as
OpenCode exported them and nothing of the export's `info` (`transcript.exports`); an earlier
session through `finished_export`, the current one exported again; one that holds no messages is
left out, and one whose export failed (a busy store) is in `missing`, which the plugin asks for
again.

### wb top

`workbench/top.py` (#407): the machine's live view, and a feed (`--json`). One long-lived process
ticking every `--every S` (0.2 to 3600, `cli.TOP_EVERY`, #611; default stats.json `every`, else
`EVERY` 2). It exits with its parent, and quietly (0) on SIGTERM, SIGHUP, a closed pipe, `q` or
Ctrl-C, killing its nvidia-smi. Never a model call, a load or a session export.

Each tick reads:
- **GPUs**: sysfs per card (`hardware.drm_cards`): busy, VRAM (an APU, `hardware.apu`, adds GTT,
  `unified`), watts (`hardware.card_watts`); names from lspci once (`card_name`). NVIDIA: one
  streaming `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=… -lms <ms>` (`SmiStream`, `hardware.smi_path`); rows older than
  three intervals drop out, cards named at start stay as `stale`, a dead stream restarts with
  backoff to `SMI_RETRY_MAX` 60 s (#547). An ARM card with `[N/A]` memory (`hardware.shares_ram`)
  shows shared RAM (#572); x86 `[N/A]` stays unknown. macOS: system_profiler once; an Apple GPU's
  `total`/`used` are RAM (`hardware.mac_free`) and `limit` the wired ceiling (`wired_limit`, else
  `models.unified_default`; #574, #701). WSL without nvidia-smi cards: Windows' adapters once. A
  card reporting nothing is no row; with no row giving `total` and none `stale`, a RAM row (#551).
- **Tasks**: task.json, status.json (`_Files`, by mtime and size), a running task's last 64 KiB of
  events.jsonl.
- **The lease**: gpu.json and each remote pool's `gpu-<host>.json` (`models.holders`, dead pids
  dropped); `router.speed`.
- **Every `PROBE_EVERY` (5 s)**: `models.discover()`, Ollama's `/api/tags` and `/api/ps`,
  `models.status` (`/v1/models` once per base URL and key, `models._catalog`, #561), non-Ollama
  `/metrics`; never another machine's model; proxies skipped (`models._open`). The loop probes on a
  thread (`Top._probe_bg`) so a stalled server never holds the tick. Also `cli.reap` for each live
  task (#571).
- **Typical load** (every `LOAD_EVERY` 300 s): the median single load (`models.single_loads`: status
  `loads`, else `load_secs`), not task totals (#577).

`--json`, one object a tick (bytes; a field the platform can't give is left out, never 0):
- `ts`, `every`;
- `gpus`: `[{index, name, driver, used, total, busy (%), watts, unified?, limit?, stale?}]`, then
  `{name: "RAM (no GPU)" (or "RAM"), ram: true, used, total}` when no GPU row gives its memory;
- `running` (queued, running, testing, asking): `[{task, model, label, phase, round, round_s,
  tok_s, tok_s_from, read_tok_s, read_from, context_used, context_window, context_pct, last,
  remote?, server?, via?, provider?, spend?, waits?}]` (the last four an API task's, below); `tok_s_from` is `live` only for the one task in phase `running` on that
  server (#548), else `last call` (the newest step's output over the time since the step before: a
floor); `read_from: "median"`. No first-token time: OpenCode's events carry none.
- `rack`: `[{model, label, state, why?, gpu_bytes?, cpu_bytes?, write_tok_s?, read_tok_s?, load_s?,
  tasks?, server?}]`, `state` `resident`, `split`, `cpu` (`size_vram` 0 with no GPU memory row),
  `idle`, `can't run`, `remote`; `server` a busy server's `live` no task claimed.
- `queue`: `[{task, model, since, waited_s, pool?}]` by `since`; `waited_s` from gpu.json
  `waiting_since`, not the task's age (#573).
- `runs` (#1278, *Deep workflows*; `runs.snapshot`): each run not closed, by its start, from its files alone
  (no reap, no state rebuilt): `[{run, flow, phase, why, alive (its driver), stages {<id>: {done, running,
  null, filtered, not_run}}, spent_usd, budget_usd, budget_min, gpu_min, session, cwd, created}]`: the
  pane's and the web's seam.

**API tasks** (#1022, `Top._api`): an API task (task.json `via: "api"`) is under RUNNING with
`via: "api"`, its `provider`, `spend` (dollars so far, `results.live_spend`: the runner's meter,
else the steps' `cost` over all of events.jsonl, which `_Files.step_cost` sums on from the offset
the last tick reached, again from the start when the file is replaced or cut; the 64 KB
`EVENTS_TAIL` held a fraction of a long task's; absent when unknown, never 0 for a missing
price; `prices`, `results.live_basis`, #1135) and, queued for one of its provider's slots, `waits: "a <provider> slot"`. No live server
rate (no server of ours: the last call's rate still works). It is never in the rack, which stays
`discover()`'s GPU models, nor the queue, the lease's waiters: an API task takes no lease. The text
row ends `  API deepseek · ≈$0.12`.

On a terminal: the alternate screen, redrawn each tick, bars in eighths, the card's short name
(`top.short`, #576), cbreak stdin for `q`. Ctrl-Z restores the
terminal before stopping and SIGCONT retakes it and redraws (a wake pipe, #607); the handlers write
straight to the fd (`os.write`), never `sys.stdout` (#950: a reentrant write quit wb top). Too tall,
it folds idle, `can't run` and `remote` models (`top.FOLD`) into `+N more`, then cuts the middle with `… N more
lines`, keeping the QUEUE (`top.lines(snap, rows)`, #608). Not on a terminal: one pass, then exit.

## Models: found, loaded, chosen

Code: `workbench/models.py` (discovery, status, residency, the GPU lease, adding and retiring),
`workbench/router.py` (choice, slice, budgets, speeds), `workbench/hardware.py` (the machine),
`cli.cmd_models`, `cmd_model`, `cmd_scout`.

### Running your own server
What each server needs set (from the README's old FAQ, #102). Ollama is where wb automates most
(pulls, deletes, each model's window, two tasks sharing the GPU); any OpenAI-compatible server
works, with size and window read from llama-server, LM Studio and vLLM too, and tasks there take
turns on the GPU. No provider yet: `wb model add <provider>/<model> --url <baseURL>` (`--context
N` when it doesn't say its window).
- Window: at least 16K (`models.MIN_WINDOW`; the README says so, `tests/test_docs.py` checks),
  32K recommended; OpenCode's own prompt is about 10K. Ollama: `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (its small
  default cuts prompts silently), or a model's `num_ctx` (read first; on macOS the one that lasts
  past a reboot, as `launchctl setenv` doesn't). llama.cpp: `-c`, split across `--parallel N`
  slots unless `--kv-unified`; one agent uses one slot. LM Studio: the length at load (`lms load <model>
  --context-length 32768`), loaded before registering. vLLM: `--max-model-len`. Too big for the
  card spills to RAM at about half speed (`wb optimize` measures Ollama's).
- Tool calls: vLLM needs `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser <parser>`; llama.cpp may
  need `--chat-template-file`; LM Studio's untrained-for-tools model is `tool_call: false`.
- An API key: the provider's `options.apiKey`; a `{env:NAME}` there needs `NAME` in commands.json
  `env` (agents get no secrets by default); else the key `opencode auth login` (or `/connect`)
  stored: OpenCode 2.x keeps it in its database (`opencode auth export`), 1.x in `auth.json`. The
  task's config layer carries such a key for the task's provider (agents' OpenCode has no stored
  credentials, #1010).

#### A server on Windows, from WSL2
WSL2's NAT forwards Windows to WSL's `localhost`, not back, so a server on Windows' 127.0.0.1
never answers from WSL: use `networkingMode=mirrored`, or listen on 0.0.0.0 and `wb remote` /
`wb model add --url` with `local: true`. When nothing answers here, `models.servers_here` (first
run, scout) probes the usual ports at `models.windows_host` (the default gateway in
`/proc/net/route`, else `/etc/resolv.conf`'s nameserver), calls a hit "on Windows", and with
nothing prints `models.WSL_NAT` (#663: Claude proposed a second server inside WSL). A provider
there is `remote` but on the same GPU (`models.same_gpu`): this machine's pool, and `free_gpu`
unloads it (#750: as its own pool it ran beside WSL's tasks on the one card); LM Studio for
Windows's instances too, through its REST API (`models._shared_servers`, never stopped: #1248,
each switch stacked one more model in VRAM). NAT gives Windows a
new address when the WSL VM restarts, so `wb remote <Windows' address>` writes provider
`models.WSL_PID` (`ollama-windows`, models.json `wsl_host: true`), and `discover()` follows it
(`follow_windows_host`): a provider wb remote made there, still at its `remote` mark, whose host
isn't `windows_host()` now, once `models._moved_to` finds Ollama silent at the mark and answering
at the new address (both probed at once, 1 s, only when the addresses differ), has its baseURL
(port kept) and mark rewritten through `own_config`, one `wb: Windows' address moved …` line on
stderr; one the user repointed (baseURL off its mark) stays theirs (#242). The probe because
`windows_host()` is only the default gateway: under `networkingMode=mirrored` or a VPN in WSL it
is the router, and a working provider was rewritten to it, every `wb start` then saying to start
Ollama at the router (#1159's review). A mark still answering is kept that way (`models._STAYED`,
per mark and new address) for `DOWN_SECS`, in-process: where the router drops packets every
`discover()` paid a second, about 5 s a `wb models` (#1397); a silent mark is asked each time, as
a runner waiting after a reboot needs. At Windows' address `wb remote` and `--remove` take the
provider marked `wsl_host` whatever its id (`models._remote_pid_for`), and `wb remote <new>`
repoints it if discovery hasn't yet (it probes the new address first, as every `wb remote` does).
One wb can't rewrite stays, and `remedy` (`windows_moved`) names the new address where it said to
start Ollama: for a `wsl_host` one, when Ollama answers at `windows_host()`, `wb remote <new>` (it
repoints it), or `networkingMode=mirrored`; when nothing answers there, "start Ollama on Windows",
never that NAT moved it, and under mirrored `wb remote 127.0.0.1 --port N` (Windows' Ollama is on
127.0.0.1 there); for any other wb remote provider, or remote Ollama, gone from an address
that isn't Windows' now ("if <host> was Windows' address"), `wb remote <new>` adds `ollama-windows`
beside it (new ids) and `wb remote <old> --remove` drops it (#1159's review: it said `wb remote
<new>` repointed it). A provider `ollama-<address>` from before stays its own (`wb remote` again at
that address, while it's Windows', marks it `wsl_host`, its ids kept). #1159: after a reboot every
`wb start` said to start a running Ollama, and `wb remote <new>` made a second provider whose new
ids started the router's history over. Any other server there (LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, Jan)
is one `wb model add <p>/<m> --url http://<Windows' address>:PORT/v1` made, marked `wsl_url`
(its baseURL, never `remote`: `wb remote` would adopt it, `--remove` delete it), and followed
the same way: `_moved_to` probes `<baseURL>/models` (`_answers`) rather than Ollama's
`/api/version`, the new baseURL is the old with only the host swapped (`_at_host`), and
`_repoint` writes it and the mark. Its "not running, and no start command" gets `windows_moved`
too: marked, "set <p>'s baseURL to <new>" when it answers at Windows' new address (wb couldn't
rewrite it), else "start its server on Windows: it answers neither at …", under mirrored a
`wb model add … --url http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1` of its own; unmarked (one `wb model add` made before
the mark), "if <host> was Windows' address", its baseURL there by hand, then `wb model add <p>/<m>
--url <new>`, which marks it (the adopt branch) so the next reboot is followed: the hand edit alone
left it unmarked, broken again by the next reboot (#1167's review). `may_come_up` stays true: a waiting runner re-reads the
model (`runner._wait_up`). #1167: such a server read "start its server" after every reboot, and
wb setup's and scout's line said `local: true` after the `wb model add` it has to precede.

#### A model on another machine
Ollama there with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`, reachable only from the client (no login; plain `http://`
carries the code: a firewall or Tailscale), then `wb remote <host>` (`--context N`, since that
Ollama says no window until a model loads; `--remove` undoes it). It adds
a model, never splits one; its energy isn't measured. Another server there: models.json `"local":
true` on its provider, then `wb model add … --url`.

Each client's lease is its own (`gpu-<host>-<port>.*`): nothing of wb runs on the box, and Ollama
shows only `/api/ps` (what is loaded, each `expires_at`, which a finished request moves and a
running one doesn't). So clients coordinate through it (`models.box_others`, `box_quiet`,
`BOX_SHARED`, #812): before loading, wait up to `BOX_WAIT` 2400 s while a model there its task
doesn't run had a request within `BOX_QUIET` 150 s. Not counted: `keep_loaded`, and what this
machine loaded there in the last week (`box_mine`, `boxes.json` `{root: {name: ts}}` in
`store.machine_dir()`), though such a model is watched `INFLIGHT_WATCH` and a request on it now
drops its mark (`_forget_mine`, #893). Last use is `expires_at` less `BOX_KEEP_ALIVE` 300 s; a stamp
standing still may be a long request and is waited out, so `make_resident` loads a box's model for
`BOX_KEEP_ALIVE`, not 30 min (#899: a 30 min stamp read as quiet through the first prefill); box
stamps may be past only by `BOX_SKEW` 10 s (`_past(remote=True)`). Clients thus take the box a round
at a time. Evictions and the task's own model found gone are `gpu` events (`GpuLease.load`,
`box_others(own=True)`); `wb start` notes the box's foreign models. Not stopped: a tool running
past `BOX_QUIET`, a box keeping models longer, a cut-off wait, clients that don't look.

### Found, loaded, chosen
**OpenCode's config.** `models.opencode_config_files()`: `$WB_OPENCODE_CONFIG` alone, else in
order the system directory's `opencode.json`/`.jsonc` (`_system_dir`: `/etc/opencode`, macOS
`/Library/Application Support/opencode`; never written), the global one's (`_config_dir`:
`$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`; #370), then `$OPENCODE_CONFIG`
(`_users_config`; never under the state directory: a task's layer). `read_config` merges them as
OpenCode does (later wins, dicts recursively, `_strip_jsonc`), then `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`
(`users_config_content`; ignored beside `$WB_OPENCODE_CONFIG`; doctor names it set, never its
keys, #347); a real-OpenCode test compares with `opencode debug config`. A relative `{file:}` is
its defining file's (`_provider_dirs`). `opencode_config_path()`: `opencode.json` if it exists,
else `.jsonc` if it exists, else `opencode.json`. An unparseable file is a `RuntimeError` naming it.

Writes (`write_entry`, `_add_provider`, `remove_remote`, `set_default`) go through
`own_config(change)`: one file's own contents under its lock (`store.edit_config`), never the merge
(#421: that copied the admin's file and a session's `apiKey` into the user's). `set_elsewhere`
refuses removing what another layer also sets, or changing what a later one sets ("… is set in
<layer>, which wb doesn't write: …"). A model for a system-only provider is an overlay in the user's
file; for an `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`-only one, refused. `own_config` refuses while two files are
layered (one merged file would undo the layering), a file that isn't strict JSON (a rewrite would
lose its comments) and one that isn't writable (Nix) (`models.config_target`), printing only `change`,
never the config (it may hold an `apiKey`). `store.write_through` (shared with models.json,
commands.json, savings.json, #495): atomic, indent 2, through a symlink, keeping the mode (0600 new).

The agent's `OPENCODE_CONFIG` is the task's layer, so `models.agent_providers()` copies
`PROVIDER_KEYS` from `$WB_OPENCODE_CONFIG` and `$OPENCODE_CONFIG` into it, templates kept, `{file:}`
made absolute, the layer 0600 (the 2026-11-19 audit: such a provider was "Model unavailable"); a
file's V2 `providers` is folded into the layer's `provider`, beside its V1 block too.

A layer's providers are both shapes' (`_providers_of`: `provider` and `providers`, V2's entry
winning for an id in both, as OpenCode keeps it): read as one or the other, an older `provider`
block beside a hand-written `providers` one hid every V2 model from discovery, `gpu_side` and the
layer, though OpenCode 2.4.1 loads both (#1508).

**Discovery** (`discover`, `_scan`) lists GPU models only (`kind == "gpu"`): about 60 call sites
(the lease, residency, `free_gpu`, media, the router's `choose`/`rank`/`unproven`/`_cheaper`) read
it, so none needs to ask a model its kind, and exploring can never reach an API model (#1013; a test
pins that `discover()` never returns `kind == "api"`). A candidate is an entry under a provider (`provider`/`providers`,
`options`/`settings` `baseURL`) that OpenCode loads (`disabled_providers`, `enabled_providers`) on
this machine (`_this_host`): `localhost`, `0.0.0.0`, `host.docker.internal`, loopback, the host
name, its first label, `<label>.local`, an own address (`_own_addresses`: `getaddrinfo`, `ip -o
addr`, else `ifconfig -a`; reread after `ADDR_SECS` 60 s), or a name for it (`_named_here`: FQDN,
or resolving to loopback or an own address within `RESOLVE_WAIT` 1 s; failures retried after
`DOWN_SECS`, results rechecked against current addresses; #807, #900). Elsewhere it counts only
with models.json `"local": true`, as `remote`. A baseURL's `{env:}`/`{file:}` resolve first
(`_expand`; empty when unset, unreadable, or dropped from the agent's environment by
`runner.SECRET_ENV`). Skipped providers and why: `skipped_providers()`, `why_none()` (in `wb
models`, doctor, `wb model add`, `resolve`, the router's "no GPU models"; an Ollama with only cloud
models: "<id> is an Ollama cloud model, an API model now (set a role to use it)…",
`ollama_cloud_ids`); one with no baseURL is a catalog provider, `hosted()`'s. `resolve()`: the GPU
side first, as before: exact id, exact model or provider name, or a unique case-insensitive
substring; then an API model by its exact id only (`hosted()[wanted]`, asked only for a miss with a
`/` that isn't the GPU side's, `gpu_side`; an exact miss reads the catalog again once, `hosted(fresh=True)`,
when the cache is older than `AUTH_FRESH_SECS` and its read didn't fail (`miss_rereads`), `_hosted_exact`: the catalog
lists only providers that can authenticate and `/connect` changes no stamp, so a just-connected
provider's ids were unknown for `HOSTED_TTL`). A fragment matching nothing raises `unknown model '<x>'; known: <GPU ids>; API models are
named by their exact id, as OpenCode lists them (opencode models)` (`EXACT_ONLY`), never listing
catalog ids (#1013: with 40 or more, `--model flash` could have landed on a paid model nobody
chose). An id with a `/` that isn't the GPU side's, while the catalog read failed (`hosted_error`),
says so after the id: `unknown model '<id>' (OpenCode's catalog read failed: <error>); …` (#1108:
read as a wrong id, Claude hunted for the "right" one).

**API models** (`hosted`, `lookup`, #1013). `models.hosted() -> {id: Model}` with `kind == "api"`:
- *Where from.* OpenCode's model.list (JSON `{location, data}`: only providers that
  can authenticate, plus OpenCode's free models; the spike's facts, *API models through OpenCode*),
  read by `models.model_list` from a private `opencode serve --stdio --port 0 --hostname 127.0.0.1`
  (the server `--standalone` starts; it prints `{"url"}`, takes a password of wb's from
  `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` as HTTP Basic `opencode:<password>`, and ends when its stdin closes; its group is
  killed after): `GET /api/plugin` every `PLUGIN_POLL` (25 ms) until it lists a plugin, then `GET
  /api/model`, both with `location[directory]`, through `_DIRECT` (no proxy; never `_open`'s stored keys), within `CATALOG_TIMEOUT` (past it,
  `opencode model.list took over 30 s`: never a partial list; a server that exits before it listens gives its stderr's first line, its exit awaited after its stdout closes, as a loaded runner's lagged: #1370). Not `opencode api model.list
  --standalone`: from OpenCode 2.4.0 the server answers model.list with what has loaded so far, and
  the catalog and every provider are plugins that load after it starts (#63814 upstream), so 2.4.1
  printed no model, or 14 of 93, and wb saw no API model (the opencode workflow, 2026-11-23);
  OpenCode's own `models` waits on plugin.list the same way. And `opencode auth list --format json
  --standalone` for each provider's key source (it never
  prints a secret, and waits for the plugins itself; `auth export` is never run: only the keyhole reads keys, for a task). Both run in
  the state directory with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1` (a repo's opencode.json under the
  caller's cwd must not add providers) and `OPENCODE_CONFIG=$WB_OPENCODE_CONFIG` when set
  (`_opencode_env`). OpenCode's own catalog fetch is left alone. Ids split at the first `/` only
  (`deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`: provider `deepinfra`, name the rest).
- *Which.* Every catalog model whose provider has no configured entry on this machine (one that
  `_scan` lists and isn't off it: those are `discover()`'s); the models of a configured provider
  whose baseURL is off this machine and not `local: true` (`_off_machine`: `_scan` still skips it
  with its `local: true` hint); the Ollama cloud models of an Ollama provider on this machine
  (`:cloud`/`-cloud` by name, whatever their `local: true`: key `ollama`, label `Ollama cloud
  (ollama.com)`, `cloud`; Ollama by `_ollama_ish`: probed as Ollama, on its port or named for it,
  never the probe alone, #1074: one behind a proxy hiding `/api/version`, or `engine: server`, fell
  out of both lists and was the router's largest GPU model). `disabled_providers`/`enabled_providers` and models.json `skip` are
  followed. A catalog entry whose `settings.baseURL` is this machine (`_this_host` without its DNS
  lookup: a catalog names dozens of hosts) is left out: a server OpenCode found by itself (2.3.2
  lists a running Ollama at 127.0.0.1 with no config) is `wb model add`'s, not an API model told to
  `/connect`. `gpu_side(id)`: the id's provider is one of the GPU side's (`_sides`: configured, on
  this machine or opted in, skipped or not) and its name no cloud name, so `hosted()` can't hold it
  whether or not `discover()` still does (a renamed or retired model, an old task's id, `wb model
  rename OLD`, a typo): `resolve`, `lookup` and `cli._api_id` ask no catalog for one (it cost two
  OpenCode starts on every `wb watch --json` the pane polls).
- *The model.* `base_url` the model's catalog base (`catalog_base`: `settings.baseURL`, its `${AWS_REGION}`
  filled as 2.3.2's `prepareProviderURL` fills it when it resolves the model (model.list prints every Mantle row's
  base as `https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION}.api.aws/openai/v1` or `/v1`: passed on as it was, the keyhole's
  upstream host was the template and every request failed, #1192's review) and any other `${...}` refused (no
  base: OpenCode fills it from its own environment); else what its package builds from the settings, as 2.3.2
  does: Azure's `https://<resourceName>.openai.azure.com/openai`, Bedrock Converse's
  `https://bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com`, Mantle's `https://bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws/v1` or
  `/anthropic/v1` (a Mantle row with no baseURL); the region `settings.region`, else `AWS_REGION`,
  `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, `us-east-1`, a host label or no base; the upstream; an off-machine or Ollama provider's
  own baseURL), `engine` `api`, `name` the id at the provider (the entry's `modelID`, which
  an alias's differs from, else its `id`), `label` `<Provider name>
  (API)` (the auth list's name, else the id), `remote` true, `package` the model's own catalog package (or the
  config's `npm`; one provider's models post through several, Azure's and Google's, and the first model seen set
  both for all, #1192), `config` the catalog entry (`limit`, `cost`, `variants` as the catalog's list,
  `capabilities`, `tool_call` from `capabilities.tools`, `reasoning`, `family`, `status`; values
  unchanged, a field of the wrong shape dropped; never `settings`, where 2.3.2 prints the key it
  holds for a layer or a free model, `settings.apiKey`), `free` (`opencode/*-free`, or every price 0; only marked here). `key`, the source
  (never the key): a config `apiKey` first (`env:<NAME>` for a lone `{env:NAME}`, else `config`;
  a lone `{env:NAME}` in `options` beside a stored key is `stored`, #1075: OpenCode sends the stored
