  kind)`: the named one (refused when of another kind), else `--kind`'s default (`default_of`:
  `default_<kind>`, else its first; *The default engines*), else the first non-listener's kind's.
- `generate` refuses before anything runs a voice not in `voices` and any option the engine has no
  slot for (refused, not dropped). Its lease is `media.turns("wb audio", …)`: none when both engine
  and listener are off this GPU, pinned only when both are, `free_gpu` keeping either's own server. An API task takes no lease
  (#1015), so audio runs beside it (not beside its `--unload-for-tests` tests).
  Each clip is made in `.wb-audio-*`, checked (`inspect`), then published with its sidecar and
  spectrogram as the first free `<slug>-<seed>.wav` (`media.free`). The `unload` URLs of engine and
  listener are each POSTed once at the batch's end (`_unload`, #594).
- `inspect`: with ffmpeg, a 16-bit PCM copy at the clip's rate and channels (`_plain_tag`, since
  `wave` reads WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE only from 3.12), `ebur128` loudness, a `showspectrumpic`
  picture, and a 16 kHz mono copy for the listener alone. Without ffmpeg, `wave` alone ("loudness:
  no ffmpeg"; a float WAV noted "unreadable: …"). What isn't audio (`MAGIC`) fails: "audio engine
  <name> wrote no audio (it starts '…')", nothing published (#592). Levels come from each frame's
  loudest channel at the clip's own rate (the mono copy hid one-channel clipping and an inverted
  channel, #586), streamed in 50 ms blocks (`_measure`, `_Meter`: memory doesn't grow, #599).
  Silence is below `SILENT_DB` (-50 dBFS), a gap `GAP_SECS` (1 s), clipped ≥ 0.999 of full scale.
- Scoring (`score`): `_align` finds the fewest word edits (Levenshtein, banded from `ALIGN_BAND` 32
  and widened until exact; past `ALIGN_CELLS` 64M cells "too long to score", a listener failure,
  #947; `difflib` misscored repeated words, #593); `wer` is edits over the script's words,
  uncapped; `differences` the first four spans `script → heard`, ignoring spacing and apostrophes, both from
  one alignment (`inspect` calls `score` once, #947). `words` NFC-normalizes (#747), keeps letters,
  digits, apostrophes and their combining marks (`\w` split Hindi and Thai at vowel signs), and
  splits scripts written without spaces (`UNSPACED`: Thai, Lao, Myanmar, Khmer, kana, CJK; not
  Hangul) into characters; mostly such a script scores CER (`cer: true`, #598). The line shows what
  was heard too, since a WER alone misled (#396: "2026" for "Twenty twenty-six" read 30%). A failing
  listener is reported on the line, not raised.
- **Dictation** (#1203, the web chat's mic, *The web chat*): `dictation()` is the first listener when
  its entry can run (a command's program found; a url only well-formed, never probed, as it is on
  every chat state); `hear(clip, ctype)` gives it a 16 kHz mono WAV when ffmpeg makes one, else the
  clip as it is, sent to a url listener as its own type (`_multipart`'s `ctype`: every clip went
  as `audio/wav`, so a phone's webm or m4a reached a server mislabelled), under
  `media.turns("wb chat dictation", …, wait=False)`: a GPU listener is `Busy` at once while a task
  holds the GPU, its `unload` URL POSTed before the turn ends. A url listener nothing answers at
  (`ready`'s probe, or a `URLError` on the clip's POST) is `Down`, for now; any other failure is
  the listener's (`RuntimeError`).
- The line: `3.4 s (asked 3) · peak -1.2 dBFS · -16 LUFS · lead 0.1 s, tail 0.3 s · gaps … · heard
  "…" WER 30% (twenty twenty six → 2026)` and the spectrogram's path; under 80% of the asked length,
  "cut short". `lines()` (`wb audio --list`, `wb scout`) shows kind, readiness, voices and `notes`
  ("licence: not noted"); `coverage()` is scout's summary.
- **Listening by ear** (#397, `chat.listen`, `wb chat listen <clip>… [--text]`): up to `LISTEN_MAX`
  (8) takes of `AUDIO_TYPES` (what a browser plays), each at most `AUDIO_MAX` (64 MiB), are copied
  into `chat/audio/<batch>/` as `<n>.<ext>` with `audio.json` (names, paths, types, `audio.summary`
  check lines) and sent as a Claude message carrying `audio` (`chat.audio_batch`: `{batch, clips:
  [{n, name, line}]}`); the page plays wb's copy, so a clip changed since plays as sent.
  Links, missing or unplayable clips, too many or too big are refused before any copy; a failed copy
  removes the batch; the newest `LISTEN_KEPT` (20) batches are kept. The pick returns as the user's
  `Keep take <n>: <name>` with `about: {audio, n, name, path}`, name and path from the batch, not
  the page (*The web chat*).
- The sidecar: `{text, kind, seed, seconds, voice, lyrics, refs, engine, secs, ts, duration, peak_db,
  clipped, lead, tail, gaps, silent?, lufs?, transcript?, wer?, differences?, listener?,
  listen_error?, unreadable?}`. `--out` defaults to `$WB_HOME/audio/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>/`.

## Git, commits and projects

- **How workbench reads git** (`gitops.git`): `-c color.ui=never` (and `color.diff|status|branch`),
  `core.quotePath=false`, `log.showSignature=false` (signed commits broke a `%h` read and accept
  exited 1), `submodule.recurse=false` (#888); diffs `--no-ext-diff --no-color`; changed files from
  `status --porcelain` (the user's `diff.external` and colours once changed the review diff: the
  2026-11-16 audit). Output is UTF-8 with U+FFFD for bad bytes. `gitops.mark`, the runner's edit
  fingerprint, streams git's raw bytes into the hash (`git_hash`, #678) and takes untracked files
  with `lstat` (past `MARK_READ_MAX`, 1 MiB, by size and time), so a FIFO or a link to `/dev/zero`
  can't hang it.
- **Pinned to the task's git dir** (`gitops._pinned`). The worktree's `.git` file is the agent's to
  rewrite; pointed at its own git dir, that config (`core.fsmonitor`, hooks) ran from `mark()`
  outside the lane (the 2026-11-16 audit). So `create_worktree` records the real git dir and the
  `.git` text in `rules/<task>/gitdir.json` (rewritten only by `wb relocate`), and every call on a
  task's worktree runs with `--git-dir`/`--work-tree` from it, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`,
  `core.fsmonitor=false`, and `core.filemode`/`core.ignorecase` set to what the state dir's file
  system does (`gitops._modes_hold`, `_case_folds`, probe files; unknown pins nothing): the repo's
  values committed a 0755 script as 100644 (#323), flipped every file to 100755 on exFAT (#683) and
  hid case-only renames (#492). The agent's reads in the task's repo get the same pins from the shim
  where the repo differs (`gitops.fs_pins`, `differing=True`; #796). On a case-folding file system
  `add -A` misses case-only renames (#656): `gitops.case_renames`/`record_case_renames` stage them
  before the review diff, the snapshot and `commit_all`; `mark` hashes them. A `.git` not holding
  the recorded text is a `GitError` ("the worktree's .git was rewritten"): the runner fails the
  task, accept refuses. Tasks from before the record run unpinned.
- **No git hooks from the worktree.** A relative `core.hooksPath` (husky's `.husky/_`) runs
  agent-written hooks as the user. `commit_all`, `worktree add|remove`, `--merge`'s merge,
  fast-forward and squash (with `--no-verify`, #499) and `wb init`'s commits run with `gitops.NO_HOOKS`
  (`core.hooksPath=/dev/null`): no hook runs, the user's included. Signing is kept. Checks belong in
  `--test`, in the lane.
- **Git LFS** (#382). A `--shared` scratch clone has no local config, so it checked out pointers:
  `gitops.share_lfs` gives it the repo's `filter.lfs.*` (`lfs_filter`) and `lfs.storage` at the
  repo's LFS directory. `wb start`'s disk check counts each pointer at its `size`
  (`gitops.checkout_size`, `LFS_POINTER*`). The suite's LFS test skips without git-lfs.
- **Checkout settings** (#426). A scratch clone must check out the task's bytes (`core.autocrlf`
  gave the task CRLF and the base check LF). `verify.checkout_settings` copies the repo's
  `CHECKOUT_KEYS` (`core.eol`, `autocrlf`, `safecrlf`, `symlinks`, `filemode`, `ignorecase`,
  `checkRoundtripEncoding`), its non-LFS `filter.<driver>.*` (`verify.local_filters`, #932) and
  `info/attributes`. A filter keeping state in the git dir (git-crypt) still fails: up to
  `FILTER_SAMPLE` (50) unedited filtered files are compared with the worktree (`verify.filter_gap`),
  and a difference or a failed `required` filter makes the run `"filtered"`: the base check says the
  base wasn't checked, `wb verify` is `inconclusive` (`filtered`), `wb shot`'s side `exit filtered`.
  bench's clones (`bench._clone_base`, #736) compare with what the repo smudges
  (`verify.smudge_gap`, git 2.40+), and a gap is a `RuntimeError` (`bench._filtered`): `bench add`
  refuses, a replay is an `error` row, never graded on other bytes.
- **The split of roles.** The agent writes code and reads git. Everything that leaves its working
  tree is Claude's: commits, branches, merges, pushes, PRs, CI/CD, deploys, infrastructure, and the
  project's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`; the agent asks through `ask_reviewer` or says so in its summary.
- **Git is read-only for the agent, enforced** (`workbench/gitguard.py`). `install` writes
  `rules/<task>/bin/git` every round, a `/bin/sh` wrapper `exec '<python>' -I -c '<code>' "$@"`
  (a shebang splits at a space in the Python's path) calling `gitguard.main(<real git>, <common
  dir>, argv, <temp roots>, [<worktree>, <lane's writable dirs>], <pins>)`, first on the agent's
  `PATH`. `split` skips global options and their values; `reads`: none or `READ` (41) reads;
  `branch`/`tag` only listing (`TAG_LISTS`, #443); `apply` without `APPLY_INDEX` (#890);
  `hash-object` without `-w`; `fsck` without `--lost-found`; `config` reading (`CONFIG_VALUED`,
  #794); `stash list|show`; `worktree list`; `remote` bare, `remote get-url|show`; read forms of
  `reflog`, `notes`, `submodule`, `symbolic-ref`; anything else (aliases, `lfs`) writes. `git
  submodule update|init|sync` in the worktree or a scratch checkout of it is not run: on submodules
  workbench filled (`filled_submodules`) it exits 0 with `FILLED`, an empty one `UNFILLED` and 1
  (builds that init their own submodules went red, #885). Reads run with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` (no
  index refresh while Claude diffs) and the pins. A write is refused with `REFUSAL` in the task's
  repository (`protected`; a `config --global|--system|-f` write judged by its file,
  `config_files`, the one git writes, so `--global` is `~/.gitconfig` unless only the XDG file
  exists: refused on the user's own `~/.gitconfig`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` or system file, `user_configs` as the environment named them at install,
  which only the lane kept out of reach: without one (then macOS's), `git config --global user.name` rewrote
  the user's, #1120; a fixture's temp `HOME` still writes, #794, with the user's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
  exported too, #1120's review) or any repository outside the temp roots, the worktree and the lane's writable
  dirs; outside any repository it passes, and throwaway repos there pass (test suites, #444;
  pre-commit, uv, Go, Bazel caches, #665). The roots are fixed at install, so `TMPDIR` can't make a
  project scratch. `init`/`clone` are judged by where the repo lands (`new_repo`, `nested`, else
  `destination`). Git by full path is denied (`context.denied_shell()`) and the task repo's refs are
  outside the lane. Standard library only: it runs on every git call.
- **Claude's files.** OpenCode's `edit` rules refuse `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `.claude/`; a shell change is named in the round report (`runner.claude_files_changed`).
- **The agent never commits.** `wb diff` shows its work against the base, or the last `wb next` step
  (`--all`: the branch), new files through intent-to-add in a scratch index copied from the
  worktree's (`gitops.with_new_files`: its index and locks untouched, skip-worktree entries not
  deletions), and the ignored files `--include` commits through `add -f` (`force=`, #1259). `gitops.add_all` reruns `add -A` with `--sparse` only after a sparse refusal (an older
  git has neither, #493). A git error in the diffstat costs only that line (`(no diffstat: …)`).
- **Nested repositories** (`gitops.nested_repos`) are left out of the diff, noted (`NOTE: <dir>: a
  git repository of its own, …`, `gitops.nested_line`) and refused by name by `commit_all`, so accept
  and next stop in review (a gitlink to nowhere was committed).
- **Edits in a filled submodule** (`gitops.submodule_edits`, `submodule_check`). Filled files are
  read-only, but `sed -i` replaces through the directory (#419). Each filled submodule, nested ones
  too, is recorded in `rules/<task>/submodules.json` with a copy of its index taken after the fill,
  kept with its time (`shutil.copy2`: a fresh mtime hid same-second rewrites, CI, 2026-11-21);
  `diff-files` against the user's submodule checkout finds changes: a NOTE and `commit_all` refuses
  ("not committed: edits in submodule <path> can't land: …"), reached even when they are a step's
  only change past a wb next (`cli._to_commit`: there git status saw nothing, and next said "had
  no changes" and accept removed the edit with the worktree, #1307). New files (`ls-files --others
  --exclude-standard`) are only noted ("new files in submodule <path> won't be committed: …"; build
  objects refused every accept, #889); an uncheckable one says "… can't be checked: … wb relocate"
  (#682), never skipped. The directories stay writable: in-tree builds write there.
- **Commits are the user's** (`gitops.commit_all`: `add -A`; refused with nothing staged, a nested
  repo, or, without `--include`, a file git ignores). `wb accept` commits under the user's identity,
  no AI co-author line, only provenance:
  ```
  feat: CSV export for reports

  Delegated to <model> via OpenCode: 3 round(s), 1 automatic test-fix, 1 review round(s).

  Workbench-Task: csv-export
  OpenCode-Session: ses_…
  ```
  `<model>` is task.json's `model_label` (`models.task_label`): a GPU model's label (`MiMo-V2.6 9B
  Q8 (Ollama)`), an API model's exact id and provider (`deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (DeepInfra, API)`;
  `<id> (Ollama cloud)`; a `label` the user set, as set), never the provider alone, which two roles
  on one provider share (#1078); the round reports, wakes and `wb watch` lead with it too.
  Rounds count every runner round (auto-fixes, notes, handovers); review rounds the last step's. `wb next` commits with
  `Workbench-Task: <task> (step N)`. A clean worktree accepts the branch's commits past the base;
  none is refused. An accept that committed then died finishes on retry by its trailer
  (`cli._landed`). `delegate/<task>` is made the commit (`gitops.put_on_branch`), refused when it
  holds commits the accepted one lacks (#417).

  **`--merge`** runs `merge --no-ff --commit --no-squash --no-log` in the user's checkout with git's
  own message (`gitops.merge_message`, #471), no hooks, refused unless the checkout is on a branch
  (`base_branch`, else any) holding the base (#418), has no tracked changes (`gitops._uncommitted`;
  a submodule only if the merge changes its gitlink, #505), no merge under way, and no untracked or
  ignored file where the merge writes (`gitops._overwritten`: ort silently replaces ignored files,
  #189; a file-to-directory change is the merge's, #343; an untracked link is in the way, #367; a
  case twin counts as the tracked file only on the same inode, `gitops._same_file`, #470, #640).
  Those paths come from the merge done first (`git merge-tree --write-tree`, 2.38+; else
  `gitops._trial_merge` in a `--no-checkout` scratch worktree with `NO_SMUDGE`, #469, whose failure
  refuses the merge), compared as raw bytes (#241, #320). `--commit --no-squash` outrank `mergeOptions` (#430), the squash passes
  `--ff` (#429) and commits with the tip's message (`-C`), or accept's when it made no commit (#1393). Success is the branch in HEAD and no `MERGE_HEAD`; a conflict, a signature past
  `COMMIT_SECS`, or SIGTERM/SIGHUP (`cli._ends_cleanly`) is backed out (`gitops._back_out`, only its
  own merge: `_made_by`; #420, #190). A SIGKILL runs no backout: a retry with `closing`'s
  `merge_from` first clears what that merge of the tip left (`gitops.clear_killed_merge`:
  `MERGE_HEAD` at the tip is quit when HEAD holds it, else backed out; a squash's staged tree
  backed out when `SQUASH_MSG` names the tip; #1231: it was refused as uncommitted changes, or
  said merged mid-merge). Before reading any of it, it ends the killed try's signing git if it
  still runs (`closing`'s `merge_git`, `[pid, start]`, which `gitops.merge`'s `started` records:
  `gitops.end_session`, checked with `models._alive`; a pid with no start is left alone): backed
  out under it, that git landed the merge once its signer was answered, over the unmerged index
  and files, with the task's changes staged as reverted and wb saying not merged (#1246). Merges into one checkout take turns (`gitops.merge_lock`, a
  flock on `workbench-merge.lock` in its git dir, held from `merge_from` through the merge, since
  the command lock is per task and two accepts interleaved, #639; refused past `MERGE_WAIT`,
  `COMMIT_SECS` + 15 s, never forced, since an agent can hold it; a flock the file system refuses
  is a `GitError`, #892). Without `--merge`, or with it refused, it prints `merge into <branch> with:`
  (`cli._merge_line`, `gitops.merge_by_hand`, in the repo's mode: `--merge-as` or commands.json
  `merge`, #471): into `closing`'s `merge_into`, else the task's `base_branch`, else the checkout's
  branch, led by `git -C <repo> switch <branch> &&` when another branch or a detached HEAD is out
  (it merged into whatever was out, #1154); no branch known on a detached HEAD prints no command.
  `wb discard` prints the same line for the approved steps it keeps (#1174: its plain `git merge`
  landed them on whatever was out, in no mode or signing of the repo's). A colocated Jujutsu repo
  (`gitops.jj_colocated`) has a detached HEAD: the refusal (`gitops.detached`) and `merge with:`
  give `jj -R <repo> new @- delegate/<task>` (`gitops.jj_merge`, #385). A task from a tag or commit has a null `base_branch` (`cli._merge_into`, #87).
- **The worktree** (`gitops.create_worktree`): `worktree add -b delegate/<task> <task dir>/worktree
  <base sha>` (peeled to its commit, never an annotated tag's id), refused when the branch exists; sparse (`gitops.sparse_of`, `apply_sparse`) when the
  repo is, as are the scratch clones (#263; verify's candidate uses `--ignore-skip-worktree-bits`,
  #493). A failed add removes all it made. `remove_worktree` is `--force`, falling back to deleting
  by hand and `gitops.drop_registration` (#793); nothing runs `git worktree prune` (it dropped a
  worktree on an unmounted drive, #641).

  A task outlives its checkout (#498): repo-level git runs where `gitops.repo_of` says, task.json
  `repo` while it is a checkout of the repository, else the main worktree (from task.json
  `git_common`). A git dir gone (the repo moved): `_pinned`, accept (`cli._repo`), feedback, next,
  resume (`cli._worktree_problem`) and the runner (`runner._repo_gone`, a notice with `cause` `repo`, #1247) say "the repo moved or was
  deleted … wb relocate <task> --repo <its new path>" before changing anything; the shim and lane
  (`context.repo_dirs`, #776) and `wb bench add` (`bench._repo`, #909; a case's siblings from
  case.json `checkout`) follow `repo_of` too; commands.json `repos` matches a linked worktree by git
  dir (`context.repo_conf`). `wb
  relocate` (`gitops.relocate`) checks the base is there, finds the worktree's admin dir (relative
  links too, #682), refuses a `.git` naming another existing git dir, runs `git worktree repair`, and
  rewrites gitdir.json, task.json `repo`, `git_common`, `cwd` and `submodules.json`'s `src`.

  `wb discard` records status `tip` and deletes the branch (`delete_branch`, `(was <sha>)`) unless
  `--keep-branch`, the repo moved, or it has commits past the base (kept unless `--drop-steps`,
  #494; it prints accept's `merge into <branch> with:` line for them, `cli._merge_line`, #1174,
  and `to drop them: git -C <repo> branch -D <branch>`). Accept records `tip` and after `--merge` runs `drop_merged_branch` (`branch -d`). Once the
  branch is gone, `gitops.step_commit`, `cli._landed` and `wb gc` (`_merged_branches`) read `tip`.
- **One command per task at a time** (`cli.one_at_a_time`): accept, discard, next, feedback, resume,
  takeover and stop hold `locks/<task>.cmd.lock` (`store.task_lock`, outside every lane: an agent's
  flock would wedge them), so a second waits and sees what the first did (an accept racing a
  discard deleted the accepted commit). `stop --all` takes each in turn, skipping one closed since.
  The runner never takes it.
- **The repo's stack** (`gitops.stack`, for the router and the skill records): the top two
  `LANGUAGES` by extension over `git ls-files`, each at least 20% of sources; a `.h` counts as the
  most common of `HEADERS`, C with none (#908).
- **`wb init <dir>`**: a repo on `init.defaultBranch` with an initial commit and `AGENTS.md` a
  symlink to `CLAUDE.md` (an `AGENTS.md` becomes `CLAUDE.md`; the reverse link is swapped). A
  gitignored `CLAUDE.md` gets no link (it would dangle in every clone). It refuses home or above, inside another repo, no git
  identity, and adds no remote. Its commits run no hooks (`gitops.NO_HOOKS`: a global
  `core.hooksPath` commit-msg policy failed `wb try` on every retry, #1254) and sign as accept's do (`gitops.commit`, *Signing the
  user's commits*): a key that can't sign unattended refuses at once with `UNLOCK`, the files left
  staged and a link in the working tree, and `wb init --no-sign` (or again once unlocked) commits
  them; a rerun commits a link to `CLAUDE.md` HEAD lacks (#1226). Before a first commit it refuses, changing nothing, uncovered or
  staged `cli.SECRET_FILES` and `cli.VENDORED` (#80: an `.env` was committed). In a repo with
  commits it commits only its own change, "chore: AGENTS.md links to CLAUDE.md" (`cli._commit_link`,
  a scratch index from HEAD, `_md_entries`, no hooks), leaving the user's edits (#931), and nothing
  ("not committed: …") for an already-staged path, an uncommitted `CLAUDE.md`, a gitignored target,
  or an operation under way (`gitops.under_way`, `UNDER_WAY`: it once consumed `MERGE_HEAD`).
- **CLAUDE.md stays true.** It goes into every prompt, so the skill has Claude update it after an
  accepted task that changes what it describes. `wb accept` says only when the repo has none
  (`the repo has no CLAUDE.md: write one (wb init)`, `cli.claude_md_status` at `tip`, #269; a
  `subdir` task's package CLAUDE.md first, #783; never when an AGENTS.md is committed there or at
  the root, `cli._agents_md_at`, as `wb start` said the agent gets it, #1513); how many code commits it is behind went (#1322:
  every accept said it, and "keep it current"); `wb init` still says it.

## Claude coding: when Claude writes a task's code

The user chooses (`wb coding`, #92; the web app's Settings, #1283) in `$WB_HOME/coding.json` `{mode,
ts}`, read fresh, default `decide`. The agent always gets the first shot.
- **Let Claude decide** (`decide`): nothing added, nothing gated.
- **Ask me first** (`ask`): Claude's first edit in a task's worktree asks the user in a dialog (`Let Claude edit
  <task>'s code now?`, `Allow`/`Don't`, through `consent`: the terminal's, the user away or not); `Allow` runs `wb coding
  allow <task> --said="Allow, in the workbench dialog"` and lets it through, `Don't` denies (`NOT_EDITED`). `--edit`
  (default `its code`) and `--said` are optional (#1322: Claude once had to ask in chat and record both itself).
- **Only when I say** (`only`): Claude reports the blocker and keeps the work until the user says.

An allowance (`tasks/<task>/coding.json` `{allowed: [{edit, said, ts, used, when?, started?,
did?}]}`, a `coding` event) is spent when work goes back to the agent (`spawn_runner` marks it
`used`). A **one-task exception** (#94, `--when "<condition>"`) is spent only once Claude has
started (the mod stamps `started`); Claude records `wb coding used <task> --did "…"` and hands back
with `wb feedback`. It is the task's alone: the setting never moves. The pane shows it
(`allowedLine`: `Claude may, once, if <when>: <edit>`). Enforced: `wb takeover` exits 3 without one
(`_coding_gate`) unless `--user` (the mod's hand-back, which records an allowance per task); the mod denies Edit, MultiEdit, Write and
NotebookEdit under `$WB_HOME/tasks/<task>/worktree/` without one (`codingRefusal`, `taskOfPath`; the rules are the kernel's
`codingGate`, its verdict `pass`, `start`, `ask` or `refuse`, *The kernel*; the unmatched
`tool.call` hook, which also keeps Claude's calls there for `wb accept`, `rules/<task>/claude-calls/`, #1211), and outside `decide` adds a `claude-coding` block (`CODING_RULES`), a mid-session
change arriving as a row (`sayRules`, #540). Shell edits aren't seen: the block covers them.

**Dynamic workflows (deepmode)** (#1041, named deepmode by #1278: `cli.WORKFLOWS_LABEL`; `wb deepmode` and,
its name before, `wb workflows`, one command; on, a substantive request runs as a deep workflow, *Deep
workflows*; `/deepmode [on|off]` in both hosts, and `deepmode on|off` typed, *The keywords* below).
Whether Claude may split one request into several tasks that run at once:
the user's choice, `wb deepmode on|off` (the web app's Settings), kept beside the coding choice in `$WB_HOME/workflows.json` `{deepmode, ts}`
(`cli.WORKFLOWS`, `DEEPMODE_KEY`, `workflows_mode`), read fresh, default `off` (no file, unreadable JSON, an unknown mode).
**2.1's key** (#1507, 2026-11-26): 2.1 kept it as `{mode, ts}`, where on meant Claude may start several tasks
at once for a request; read as 2.2's deepmode, a 2.1 on made every substantive request a deep workflow,
unasked. 2.2 reads `deepmode` alone, so a 2.1 on starts off, and `wb deepmode --moved`
(`cli.deepmode_moved`, under `locks/workflows.lock`) writes `{deepmode: off}` and prints the story's
`moved.deepmode` once (what deepmode is now, `/deepmode on` to turn it on): the mod (`deepmodeMoved`, at a
session's start with a person there) and the OpenCode plugin (`Jobs.tick`, once a load) run it only while the
file holds 2.1's `mode: on` and no `deepmode`, and toast its line; any other file prints nothing. Like
`wb coding` it is the user's: Claude runs it only on their yes, and wb gates neither (no dialog: nothing it
starts could not start anyway). **Off**: the skill's rule, one task at a time, as before there was a choice.
**On**: the mod adds a `dynamic-workflows` block (`WORKFLOWS_RULE`, from `workflowsMode`, said with
`/workbench`'s text when that comes first) while delegating or with a task open, as `wanted` reads;
a change either way reaches the conversation as one `[workbench]` row (`sayRules`: the rule, or
`WORKFLOWS_OFF`), however made. The rule (#1278): a substantive request is a deep workflow, the skill's *Deep
workflows*: a flow picked (`wb run flows`) and said in at most three lines, `wb run start` once, then the turn
ends and the run's notices wake Claude as a task's do (the mod's `deliverRuns`, #1278's S9; before it the wake was
a background `wb wait <run>`: told only "don't poll", Claude was never woken, the review of #1278); never several tasks Claude starts at once itself (the run's driver
starts its items, each `--group <run>`: task.json `group`, #1048, the pane draws a group's tasks under one header;
nothing is guessed from names, which would join `fix-crash` and `fix-menu`); each result reviewed on its own,
merged logic first, then tests, then UI or docs. Each task runs on its own role's model;
nothing new decides what runs together: the GPU lease (`models.apart` cards together, the rest queued)
and the provider slots (#1015). No cap on tasks at once (the owner's call, not asked for). Its Settings
row is the web app's (#1283; the pane's until then, #1023).

**The keywords** (#1278; `mod/hooks/keywords.ts`, both hosts' one copy, held to `tests/fixtures/keywords.json`
as `runs.keywords` is; text, so never the kernel's: kernel/BOUNDARY.md): `deepcode`, a whole word outside
backticks and fences, and a line of its own `deepmode on|off` (the last wins; `onlyToggles`: nothing else in
the text), read as Python reads it (`\w` Unicode, `\s` as `str.isspace`, a line ending at `\n` alone: a seeded
run of the two agreed on 300,000 texts, #1325). Only the user's own words: in the terminal (the mod's `prompt.submit`, `byUser` and none of `[web
chat]`, `[agent `, `[workbench]` nor a slash command) or the user's web message (never an agent's), never
Claude's `ultracode`. `deepcode` adds `wb deepmode --rule` (`runs.DEEPCODE_RULE`, read once a load;
`DEEPCODE_FALLBACK` from a wb without it) to that prompt: the hidden `context` entry in the terminal, the text
(`chatPrompt`'s `about`) for a web message, as a plugin's prompt has no context. `deepmode on|off` is the user's
yes: the mod runs `wb deepmode on|off`, toasts its line, and a prompt of toggles alone is dropped with that
line (no turn; `sayRules`' row tells Claude); else the rest goes on. `/deepmode [on|off]` (the mod's
`DEEPMODE`, the one command not named `workbench-*`: the user's word) sets or shows it. In OpenCode
(`opencode-plugin/deep.ts`, its prompt hook registered before upkeep's so that a toggle is in workflows.json
when upkeep reads it): the session `prompt` hook reads a typed prompt (no metadata) or the chat's delivery of
the user's (`chat.SOURCE`, `[web chat]`), never a subagent's (a session with a `parentID`: OpenCode's
subagent prompt comes unmarked too, #1325), runs wb as the session, and the `context` hook adds the rule, or the
toggle's `TOGGLED` line, as system parts to that prompt's requests (while it is the newest user message, by
the requests' message ids; to the next prompt without them); `/deepmode` is a server command (`command.transform`),
said with a `synthetic` message that starts no turn.

## Experiments

An experiment changes what the agent may do before it is measured enough: it ships off, the bench
(`--label`) and results rows' `experiments` decide it, and one that doesn't earn its place is
removed. `context.EXPERIMENTS` names each. `wb experiment <name> on|off` (or the pane) sets
`$WB_HOME/experiments.json`; `wb start` records task.json `experiments`
(`context.task_experiments`), so a flip affects only later tasks. Off, unable to work or unable to
help, the agent's prompt and rules are exactly those without it.

**probe** (`probe-code`, an outside program the user installs): the agent outlines a file (`probe
symbols`) or extracts one function (`probe extract <file>#<name>`) instead of reading it whole (half
the measured steps compacted or handed over, 2026-11-20). It needs a probe on the agent's PATH
(`context.probe_bin`) whose `--help` lists `symbols` (crates.io's 0.6.0 doesn't); `wb experiment`,
`wb doctor` and the web app's Settings say when it's missing (`PROBE_HOME`, `PROBE_RELEASES`); turned on there
without it, the change's `help` row has Claude offer to set it up (*Settings changed on the web app*).
Off, it isn't run at all (a non-UTF-8 `--help` failed a start, #518; read with `errors="replace"`).
On:
- shell rules allow only `context.PROBE_READS` (`symbols`, `extract`, `search`, `grep`, `query`) and
  refuse `--lsp`: `probe *` let the agent start `lsp` and change `config` (2026-11-21);
- the handbook copy ends with `EXPERIMENT_NOTES["probe"]`, after `spec_note` (`agent/HANDBOOK.md` unchanged): extract
  from `PROBE_FILE_LINES` (1500) lines, `--allow-tests`, search `--dry-run -o plain`, never re-spell
  a search, `grep -n` after two misses, never pipe into `head` (0.6.0 aborts on EPIPE), what "File
  too large" means, how to page a long `read`;
- the protocol carries `EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL["probe"]` (`context.experiment_protocol`), a condition,
  not an order: "When you need one function from a file over 1500 lines, `probe extract
  <file>#<name>` it instead of reading the whole file.";
- `PROBE_MAX_TOKENS` (the user's, else 2000) in its environment (`runner.agent_env`; one search
  printed 169 KB, #857); it caps matched code, not output, hence the note's `--dry-run -o plain`;
- **a read cap**: the layer's `tool_output` at a tenth of the window (`runner.output_cap`), which
  bounds shell output but not `read` (2,000 lines or 50 KB; OpenCode 2.3.2, 2026-11-21);
- **an outline in round 1** (`runner.add_outline`, once, a restarted runner adds nothing; before the
  GPU lease, since a hanging probe would hold the GPU, the review, 2026-11-21; status `outline`, `[]`
  when none): `probe symbols --allow-tests -o json` (`runner.probe_symbols`, `OUTLINE_TIMEOUT` 20 s;
  JSON, since the text's signatures span lines) on each long file in a probe language the spec names
  (`context.long_files`, lines counted by `context._Lines`, never read whole), as `OUTLINE_HEAD` and
  one `<first>-<last> <signature>` line per symbol, longest first, `OUTLINE_MORE` when cut, named
  from `task.workdir`, within `PROBE_OUTLINE_TOKENS` (1000) shared evenly. A failing probe adds
  nothing and never fails a round.

task.json `experiments.probe` is `"on"` or `false` (an old task's level or `true` reads as on),
`probe_files` the spec's long files (`context.long_files` at the base: `spec_paths`, `brace_names`,
the package first); the results row's `probe_long` says whether there were any. `wb status`: `probe: 2 call(s); whole reads of files
over 300 lines: 1` (`LONG_FILE_LINES`). The pane says "recommended" only when
`context.PROBE_RECOMMENDED` (`wb experiment`'s line then ends `; on is recommended`), which Claude
sets once a measurement finds on at least as good as off (#857's step 6): false, after the third
A/B.

**On (large files only)** (the owner, 2026-11-22, #857): off (default) or on, in `wb experiment probe`
and the pane. It had levels from 2026-11-21 (moderate, today's on; aggressive, an order that cost
more; adaptable, via a `probe_aggressive` knob, which always chose moderate), so they went. An old
level or `true` still reads as on (`context.setting`, `context.OLD_LEVELS`; a running A/B calls `wb
experiment probe adaptable`), hidden from help.

**Only where probe can help** (the owner, 2026-11-21, #857: "No sense in clogging up the subagents
with irrelevant information"). Set on and installed, probe is off for a task whose repo has no file
in a probe language over `PROBE_FILE_LINES` (`context.probe_off`, at `wb start`): task.json
`experiments: {probe: false}`, `experiments_off: {probe: "<why>"}`, everything byte for byte a
probe-off task's, and no `experiments` or `probe_*` in its results row. Reasons: `PROBE_OFF_SHORT`,
`PROBE_OFF_GAVE_UP` (`PROBE_SCAN_BYTES`, 64 MiB, ran out), `PROBE_OFF_PARTIAL` (a partial clone, git
before 2.44), `PROBE_OFF_HELP`, `PROBE_OFF_WRITING` (a writing task: no repo scan; *The writing role*).
Not installed: `{probe: false}`, no `experiments_off`.
- **Which files count**: the base's blobs (a `subdir` task's package) plus files the spec names,
  probe languages only, counted largest first through `gitops.feed_blobs` a chunk at a time, never
  whole; a blob of at most `PROBE_FILE_LINES` bytes isn't read; generated blobs (over
  `PROBE_SPARSE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, per `PROBE_FILE_LINES` lines in the first `PROBE_SPARSE_AFTER`,
  64 KiB) skipped (`gitops.SKIP_BLOB`), so a minified bundle can't eat the budget;
  only what the sparse patterns keep (`gitops.sparse_keeps`); in a partial clone with
  `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` (#436). Submodules and symlinks don't count.
- **Which languages**: the installed probe's `probe search --help` `--language` values
  (`context.probe_language_names`, read from that option only) mapped by `context.PROBE_LANGUAGES`
  (made by trying 0.6.0's values; `yaml` and `swift` map to nothing on purpose; a new language needs
  only its row), cached per path and version in `probe-languages.json` (`context.probe_languages`;
  a probe with no version is asked each time). Unreadable, or no value with a row: off, uncached.
- **The outline** and `probe_files` take only those languages (`runner.outline_section`).
- **Image and audio generation** start no runner, so no experiment (`ProbeWhereItHelps`).

**Measured** on one 27B at Q3, a 40K window, a 16 GB card, with cases from workbench's commits on
1,500–3,000-line files, paired off/on replays (`wb bench run --label`, `wb experiment probe on|off`
between arms; `wb bench report --label <arm>` prints the use per arm, `bench.use_lines`):
- **the first A/B** (2026-11-21): probe never used in 14 replays with the note in the handbook only:
  hence the protocol line.
- **the second A/B** (2026-11-21, the order "before you read a file over 300 lines, run probe
  symbols"): used in every on replay, halved time and tokens on the 2,700-line file, but explored
  2–3× more elsewhere and handed over (median tokens 55K → 134K): hence the condition, the 1500-line
  threshold and `--dry-run -o plain`.
- **the quick A/B** (2026-11-21): the harder the wording pushed probe the worse it did; the condition
  alone was never worse than off. OpenCode's `read` filled the window in every arm: hence the cap
  and the note's paging sentence. A `probe` shim is the lever left untried.
- **the third A/B** (2026-11-22, #857's step 6, the condition with the cap and outline, 18 pairs,
  rule fixed before the run: used, at most one fewer pass, P(faster or fewer tokens) ≥ 0.8 by a
  Bayesian bootstrap, handovers not up): passed 15 off, 13 on; P(faster) 0.39, P(fewer tokens) 0.50;
  handovers 15 → 11; long whole reads 5 → 0. So `PROBE_RECOMMENDED` stays false and on stays
  opt-in. Another model or window may differ; the same replays check it.

## Verifying a fix against the base

`wb verify <task> [--test CMD] [--files PATH…] [--expect TEXT] [--timeout N]` (`workbench/verify.py`,
#96) runs one test twice at review, in scratch checkouts in the task's lane and environment
(`runner.run_in_lane` on a `verify._At`), set up like the worktree (`runner.prepare`), never in the
user's checkout or the worktree:
- **The base**: a `--shared` clone (`gitops.scratch_clone`, `bundle_steps`'s too; in a shallow repo,
  where git ignores `--shared`, made by hand in its object format with the repo's objects as
  alternates, #884) at the task's base, or the previous approved step (`step_base`, #252, #652),
  with the candidate's test files copied in (`--files`, else the changed files `TEST_PATH`/`looks_like_test` matches:
  `tests/`, `fixtures/`, `testdata/`, `test_*`, `*.test.*` and the like, test data included, #500,
  #731; paths as `:(literal)`, #194) and its deleted tests deleted
  (`verify.removed_tests`, #643). No test file: refused. A non-test `--files` path is
  `code_copied`, said in the report.
- **The candidate**: that clone with the tree accept would commit (`verify.candidate_tree`:
  `gitops.snapshot_left(landing=True)`, also `wb shot`'s and the staleness check's, not the review
  snapshot, #431): only what accept refuses without `--include` (a new binary of `BINARY_MAX` or
  more, directories past `NEW_FILES_MAX`) is `left_out`, a big text file is in (the review's
  `SNAPSHOT_MAX` dropped one and verify said proven, #642), and so are the ignored files the agent
  wrote, which `--include` commits (`force=runner.ignored_to_commit`, #1275); a check with anything
  left out is never `proven`.

The verdict: `proven` (the base fails on an assertion, the candidate passes), `base-passes`,
`candidate-fails`, or `inconclusive` (a timeout, overrun, failed setup, left-out files, a run whose
lane was refused, exit 126 and `lane.REFUSED`, said as `no test ran: …` and kept as `refused`, #1308,
or a base failure that isn't proof). Proof is positive only: `--expect TEXT` in the base's output, else an
`ASSERTION` line or `FAILED_TEST` header (#730), unless first a `SETUP` error (#326) or a `MISSING`
file the candidate adds (#500). Never proof: `MISSING_API` (an API the candidate adds; a command
not found in bash's words or dash's), or pytest
whose first `E` line (`PYTEST_E`) isn't `PYTEST_PROOF` (#729); a bare "expected" matched
`SyntaxError: expected ':'` (#193). `assertion` is the line shown (pytest's first `E` line, else
the first assertion line, never a `>` line, else the header). Runs are kept in
`tasks/<task>/verify/<n>/` (`base.txt`, `candidate.txt`, `result.json` `{cmd, files, tree, ts, base:
{rev, exit, assertion}, candidate: {…}, verdict, dir, expect?, uncopied?, removed, missing,
code_copied, left_out?, filtered?, refused?}`); `verify.last` adds `stale`. `wb report` ends with the newest
check (#97); `wb accept` prints `verify.note` when it isn't `proven` or is stale.
An API task's checks are the same, with no model call: with `--unload-for-tests`, `wb verify`, `wb
shot` and the runner's tests (`_tests_gpu`, for a lease with no pool) take this machine's pool alone
(`verify.gpu`), whatever the model's (#1026).

### Screenshots of the base and the candidate

`wb shot <task> --capture CMD [--viewport WxH] [--files PATH…] [--timeout N]` (`verify.shot`, #98)
runs the project's capture command on both sides, with verify's checkouts and base (`gitops.step_base`,
#501), in the agent's shell (`runner.test_shell`, #517), writing a PNG to `$WB_SHOT_OUT` (absolute,
a fresh `.wb-shot-<random>.png`: #344, #433) at `$WB_SHOT_VIEWPORT` (1280x800). workbench ships no
browser. Pairs are kept in `tasks/<task>/shots/<n>/` (`base.png`, `candidate.png`, `base.txt`,
`candidate.txt`, `shots.json` `{task, step, round, cmd, viewport, files, ts, base: {rev, exit, ok,
image, error?, pruned?}, candidate: {…}, left_out?}`; `pruned` by `store.slim_archive`, #821;
`left_out` from `gitops.snapshot_left` adds `verify.LEFT_OUT`, #836). A side is `ok` only on exit 0
with a PNG (checked by signature, never through a link: `verify.shot_ok`; #268); else its `error`
names the exit and output file, even with a PNG ("the PNG it wrote anyway"). A failed capture never
blocks or passes a review.

`--chat` posts the pair (#99; `chat.shots`, *Files* under *The web chat*). "Reply about these" sends
`about: {task, n}` (`localStorage` `wb-chat-about`); the server fills step and round, and the mod
gives Claude `[web chat] (about <task>, step <s>, screenshots <n>) <their words>`, for `wb feedback`.
**Audio takes** (#397, `wb chat listen`, *Audio*, *Listening by ear*) come the same way: "Keep this
one" sends `Keep take <n>: <name>` with `about: {audio, n}`, and Claude gets `[web chat] (keeps take
<n> of the shortlist: <path>) Keep take <n>: <name>`.

## The web chat

`wb chat serve` (`workbench/chat.py`, `chat_static/`) serves a page on port 1337 that reaches the
Claude session in workbench mode while the user is away: messages both ways, Claude Code's
dialogs, push notifications (installable and notifying over https only: `tailscale serve --bg
1337`). On by default (the owner, 2026-11-24, #1281, reversing 2026-11-19's off until `wb chat
on`): `chat.ensure` brings it up, `wb setup` installs its service, `wb doctor` says whether it
answers; `wb chat off` turns it off, and that choice is kept. The pane's modeline shows its link, or
why it is down (*Seeing what the agent does*).

**What it's for** (#1341; the owner, 2026-11-24): message the driver from anywhere, and most work
can run from here; a prompt the driver raises waits in its terminal (ssh + tmux) unless the driver
runs with permissions granted, and the settings live here too. The empty state (`#intro`) says so,
and over a thread the same words are a hint (`#hint`) until dismissed on that device
(`localStorage` `wb-chat-hint`, read and written in try/catch: a storage that throws shows it on
each open). Both are the story's `purpose` (*The story*), naming the driver that listens (else the
last that wrote, else "your driver").

### The story

One source for every sentence the chat, the web app and the docs tell the user about where the
driver lives and what the chat is for (#1355; the owner's rule, 2026-11-24: the terminal is where
the driver lives and a prompt it raises is answered there; most work can still run from the chat,
more so with permissions granted; the web app's Settings are the source of truth). They had
drifted: the page said "Run Claude" to an OpenCode user, and the docs called the chat off by
default after 2.0 turned it on.
- **`workbench/story.py`**: `DRIVERS` (`claude-code`, `opencode`, `any`: each one's `who`, `app`,
  `listen`, `grant`, `reply`: how it answers in the chat, `prompts`: the prompts it raises), `TEXTS`
  (each sentence once, a template: `{field}` from the driver and the
  caller, `{Field}` capitalized), `ONLY` (the drivers a key is said for: `next.grant` names a
  command only Claude Code and OpenCode have; a `refusal.*`, `skill.*` or `tasks.pickup` is a host's, `HOSTS`, and
  `refusal.plan` Claude Code's alone: OpenCode has no plan dialog), `PAGE` (the keys the web app
  reads), `HOST` (the keys the hosts' module carries), `DOCS` (the doc
  blocks). `text(key, driver, **fields)`, `fill(t, fields, partial)`, `driver_of(tool)`. Keys:
  `purpose`, `rule.terminal`, `rule.chat`, `rule.settings`, `state.*` and `next.*` (`none`, `idle`,
  `working`, `waiting`, `next.grant`), `wait.*` (`permission`, `question`, `plan`, `elicitation`,
  `consent`: what `state.waiting`'s `{what}` is), `note.waiting` and `note.grant` (the notice row's
  bytes, `chat.WAITING`, `WAITING_GRANT`), `receipt.blocked`, `prompts` and `lane` (Settings cards), `doc.rule`;
  `link.where` (wb setup's last line: where the web app's link is) and `link.reach` (`wb chat on`'s
  and doctor's: `wb chat reach tailnet`), read by cli.py; `moved.deepmode` (`wb deepmode --moved`'s
  line, both hosts' toast, #1507); `refusal.question`, `refusal.plan`,
  `refusal.consent` (the mod's `AWAY_QUESTION`, `AWAY_PLAN`, `CONSENT_WAITING`, the plugin's
  `AWAY_QUESTION` naming `workbench_chat_reply`); `skill.rule` (SKILL.md's terminal-primary
  paragraph) and `skill.prompts` (reference/driving.md's: prompts are answered in the terminal, and
  the line the chat shows while one waits); `tasks.pickup` (the open-tasks context block's last line,
  the mod's `workbench` block and the plugin's `TASKS_NOTE`: `wb wait <name>` to follow a task, #1515).
- **`scripts/gen_story.py`** writes `chat_static/src/story.ts` (`STORY_DRIVERS`, `STORY_TEXTS` for
  `PAGE`'s keys, `storyFill`, `storyText`; a plain script, loaded before app.js, built into
  `story.js` by `scripts/web.py`), `mod/hooks/story.ts` (`CLAUDE_CODE` and `OPENCODE`, `as const`
  tables of `HOST`'s keys filled for each host, pure data: `register.tsx` imports it as `SAY`,
  `opencode-plugin/chat.ts`, `skill.ts` and `upkeep.ts` as their own; in the plugin's shared files,
  `patches.PLUGIN_SHARED`, and the root package.json's `files`) and fills each doc block,
  `<!-- story:KEY[:driver] -->` … `<!-- /story -->` (README.md's `doc.rule`; SKILL.md's
  `skill.rule` and reference/driving.md's `skill.prompts`, both Claude Code's text);
  `--check` writes nothing and names each copy that
  differs. `tests/test_story.py` runs the check, so CI holds the copies to the source.
- **The skill's blocks on OpenCode**: `opencode-plugin/skill.ts`'s `STORY_BLOCKS`, first in
  `HOST_LINES`, puts the same key's `OPENCODE` text in each `<!-- story:<key>:claude-code -->`
  block's place, markers and all, so a reword in story.py reaches both hosts and no host line can
  fall behind it (the two host lines that rewrote driving.md's prompts passage went with it).
- **The page**: an element with `data-story="<key>"` (the intro and hint, the Settings cards *How
  the chat works* and *While away*) says that sentence for the driver (`drawStory`), its backticks as
  `code`; the HTML's own text is `any`'s, so the page reads right before a state arrives
  (`test_story` checks it). `receipt.blocked` is a message's line while the driver waits on a prompt.
- **No words in the kernel** (amends #1356's draft): a decision returns a key and facts, and a
  wording patch needs no PureScript toolchain; `test_story` fails on a string of four or more words
  in hand-written `kernel/src`.

### The driver's state line

`chat.driver_state(lst, rows)`, the snapshot's `driver` (#1355): `{state, driver, who, where?,
waiting?, line, next, grant?}`, from the facts the hosts already write. Waiting beats working beats
idle; no live listener is `none` (named by the newest driver that wrote, else `any`). The wait is
the listener claim's own `waiting` (`{kind, tool, since, what?}`, `chat.WAIT_KINDS`), else the
oldest open notice row under `ASK_STALE` (the one the turn is stuck on). `line` and `next` are the
story's `state.*` and `next.*`, `{what}` its `wait.<kind>`; `grant` (`next.grant` and the command)
only for a permission, on a known driver (`claude --permission-mode auto`, `opencode --auto`): a
question or a plan waits however the driver runs. The page (`drawState`, `#driver-state`,
`role="status"`) shows it under the header while it asks something of the user, waiting or none:
the line, the command waiting, what to do, and for a permission the grant with Copy, its one
button (nothing answers a prompt from the phone, #1350); the header's presence says `waiting for
you in the terminal`. A notice is no thread row any more: the state line says it, and its push
still goes as before. `WAITING_AFTER` (2 s) is the hosts' filter for the claim's `waiting`: a
dialog answered sooner (an auto-accept) is never written.

**Keeping it up.** One `chat._Server` per bound address, binding without HTTPServer's host-name
lookup (it stalled macOS, #236). `systemd/wb-chat.service`: a user unit, `Restart=always`, no start
limit, `RestartSteps` 10 s to 5 min (retrying is what brings it up when an address arrives late; a
start limit gave up for good), stopping only on exit 78 (`RestartPreventExitStatus`: bin/wb's
Python and Windows guards, and `chat.ConfigError`, #534). Rebinding and a code reload re-exec in
place, so the unit sees no exit (#200). Where logind's `KillUserProcesses=yes` would kill what wb
leaves running (`cli.kills_sessions`, via `loginctl show-session`), each runner, the bench driver
(`bench.start`), `wb optimize` (`optimize.start`) and the server `wb chat on` starts (`chat.start`)
runs in its own scope (`cli.detach`, `cli.runner_scope`: `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet
--collect`, which execs, so the pid is the command's; #531). So does all `cli.detach` starts from
a service's own cgroup (`cli.in_service`, `/proc/self/cgroup` ending in `.service`; not
`INVOCATION_ID`, which terminals pass on): the web app's Measure now ran `wb optimize` in
wb-chat.service's, and wb setup's restart of the unit killed it (#1407); `wb doctor` warns when that scope
can't be had (`cli.logout_stops`), and `wb chat on`/`wb doctor` say when logind reports
`Linger=no`. macOS: `launchd/workbench.chat.plist` (`RunAtLoad`, `KeepAlive`, `exec
"$HOME/.local/bin/wb" chat serve` through `/bin/sh`, Homebrew's `python3` first, `/usr/sbin:/sbin`
for macOS's system tools, #1305; it retries even
exit 78; unchecked on a Mac, #449). Messages name the OS's service (`chat.service_name`,
`service_hint`, #756). `wb setup` installs the service (*Up by default*, below); without one,
`chat.ensure` starts a server of wb's own. `wb chat url` prints `http://localhost:<port>/#token=…` (the port from `chat/port.json`,
else `chat/serve.pid`, whose `port` stays when `wb chat off` stops its server and drops its pid, else 1337; `--port`, #349; the fragment never leaves the browser).

- **The path of a message.** The page posts it to `chat/messages.jsonl`; the listening session's
  mod submits `[web chat] <the user's words>` and nothing more (plus `(about <task>, step <s>,
  screenshots <n>)`, `(about task <task>)` from the task sheet, `(keeps take <n> of the shortlist: <path>)`, and per file `[attached: <path>
  (<size>, <type>)]`, `attachedLines`): into the running turn (`session.send`) or as the next
  prompt; a receipt (`wb chat ack`) shows at once. Claude answers with `wb chat reply` (the skill).
- **Attachments, each uploaded once** (#623). Each file gets its id on the page when picked and is
  uploaded by it before Send (`PUT /api/upload/<id>`, after `GET` says it isn't there); the server
  stores an id once (`chat.save_upload`), so a retry, reload or second tab never makes a copy. The
  body goes to `.part-<hex>` and becomes the file only whole. A message names files by id; an
  unknown id is 400; one file per sha256 per message. Limits, read per request: `upload_mb` (25),
  `upload_message_mb` (50), `UPLOAD_FILES` 10; refused (413) before the body is read, then read on a
  moment (`_linger`) so the page gets the answer, not a reset. Saved as `chat/uploads/<id>/<name>`
  (0700/0600) through directory fds `O_NOFOLLOW`, files `O_EXCL`: a link in the way is 409. A
  path-like name (`/`, `\`, `.`, `..`) is 400; others lose unprintables and leading dots and are cut
  to `UPLOAD_NAME` 140 bytes of UTF-8 (eCryptfs: 143), keeping the extension, never splitting a
  character (#742). A disk error is 507 (`ENOSPC`/`EDQUOT`) or 500, `{error: "not saved: …"}`,
  `final: true` for `FINAL_ERRNOS`; the page stops on `final` or the `SERVER_TRIES`-th (3) 5xx,
  else backs off (it re-sent forever, #742). `wb gc` drops uploads past `--days` whose message has
  a receipt (expired too, #741) or that no deliverable message names (`chat.drop_old_uploads`).
- **Dictation** (#1203). A voice memo attached reached Claude as audio it can't hear. The state's
  `dictate` (`chat.dictate_ready`: `audio.dictation`, the first listener in audio.json when its
  entry can run, a url not probed; read for every state, so a page shows a new listener's mic at
  its next state) shows a mic beside the attach button; none without a listener, so nothing is
  added by default. The clip is uploaded as an attachment (by its id, once), then
  `POST /api/transcribe/<id>` (`chat.transcribe_upload`): an upload of type `audio/*`, `video/*` or
  `application/octet-stream` (else 415; none, 404), copied to a temp `clip.<ext>` (the user's file
  name never reaches the listener's argv or the form), then `audio.hear`. The words, `{text}`, are
  kept in `uploads/<id>/.transcript.txt` (a leading dot: no upload is named so), so a retry or a
  reload never runs the listener twice; one clip at a time (`_dictate_lock`). The page puts them
  in the box for the user to edit and send: Claude only ever gets text, so the agents, OpenCode and
  the mod don't change. 409 `{error, busy: true, why}` when the GPU is a task's: a GPU listener
  takes its turn with `wait` False and gives way, never queues behind a round; a `gpu: false` one
  runs beside tasks. 503 `{error: "the listener isn't answering: …", retry: true}` for
  `audio.Down` (a url listener's server restarting). 404 `dictation is off: …` without a listener;
  502 `the listener failed: …` (also in serve.log), nothing kept, so the next try runs it again.
  The page keeps a clip (wb-chat-dictate, its bytes in IndexedDB) through a 409, a 503, a 5xx
  that isn't the chat server's (a proxy's, no JSON `error`: `tailscale serve` while the server
  restarts), a 408/425/429 or a 200 without `text`, and asks again on `BACKOFF` (a state's flush
  only once the step is up, `hearAt`), its mic saying `Waiting for the GPU…` or `Waiting for the
  listener…`; only a 4xx or the listener's own 502 drops it, its reason on the banner. A 409 had
  dropped the clip, so the user said it all again once the task let the GPU go. An agent's token is 403 (outside `AGENT_MAY`; `AGENT_CANT`'s wording, a prefix entry). The clip's upload
  is a draft no message names, so `wb gc` drops it in time. Realtime voice isn't built: Claude
  Code's turns aren't a realtime loop, and its own voice covers the terminal.
- **The switch.** `chat/switch.json` `{on, v}` (absent: on, `chat.is_on`; `{"on": false}` only after
  `wb chat off`, and the user's off stays off; `v`, `chat.SWITCH_V`, marks 2.0's writes: a bare
  `{"on": false}` with no `chat/port.json` is an older wb's failed `wb chat on`, read as never set
  and removed once, #1405). `on` turns it on and runs `chat.ensure`; when that
  ends neither `up` nor `started` the switch goes back as it was (`web chat left off: …` from off,
  `web chat not up: …` from on: left on when it died, the pane read On and pinned a dead link,
  #690). `chat.start` runs `bin/wb chat serve --port <port>` detached (`chat/serve.log`,
  `chat/serve.pid` `{pid, port, start}`) in an environment without `chat.CLAUDE_VARS`
  (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and an OpenCode driver's `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`, #1309):
  started from a Claude session (the mod's `wb chat url`) or an OpenCode driver's tool or shell, the server must never
  run wb as the model (#1281). A wildcard is probed at its
  family's loopback (`chat._probe`, #450); `chat.wait_up` waits `START_WAIT` 10 s (an exit fails
  at once with serve.log's last line, #200). `chat.who_answers`: a response whose
  `X-Workbench-Chat` (`chat.MARK`, on every response) equals `chat.identity(token)` (HMAC-SHA256 of
  a fixed string keyed by the token) is ours; anything else is "other" (`chat.blocked_why`, #554).
  `chat.running` is `who_answers == "workbench"`. Off: nobody listens or relays, no link, away ends,
  `listener.json` removed; a running server stays up; `off` stops only the process wb started
  (`chat.stop_started`, by pid and command line).
- **Up by default** (#449, #1281). `chat.ensure(port)` returns `{url, state, why?}`: `off` (the
  switch), `up` (ours answers), `blocked` (something else answers; `why`: `chat.blocked_why`);
  else, for `chat.PORT` (the unit's) when a service keeps it (`chat._unit_keeps_it`: `systemctl
  --user is-enabled`, on macOS `launchctl print`, #756), it starts the unit (`chat._start_unit`:
  `systemctl --user start wb-chat`, `launchctl kickstart gui/<uid>/workbench.chat`), else
  `chat.start` (unless serve.pid's server is still starting), then `wait_up`: `started`, or
  `failed` (`why`: serve.log's last line). A unit that doesn't answer is followed by `chat.start`
  once (#1343: one that exits 78, stopped for good, left the app down, as only the unit was ever
  started again): `started` with `why` naming the unit, or `failed`. One at a time
  (`chat/ensure.lock`). `wb chat url` runs it and prints the link alone (the mod reads it whole);
  `wb chat url --json` prints the dict, exit 0, for the mod. **`wb setup`** installs the service
  (`cli.install_service`; `--no-service` skips it): on Linux, where `systemctl --user
  show-environment` answers with this HOME, it links `systemd/wb-chat.service` into
  `~/.config/systemd/user/` (a unit there of the user's own is kept and used; `--force` replaces a
  link elsewhere) and writes the drop-in `wb-chat.service.d/10-wb-setup.conf` (`cli.SERVICE_DROPIN`)
  with `cli.service_env`: `PATH` (the directory of the Python running setup, then setup's PATH,
  then the manager's) and each set `store.PATH_VARS`, made absolute. The manager's PATH has none
  of the shell's, so a pyenv, conda or uv Python 3.11+ was missing and the unit exited 78 (#1343),
  and OpenCode in `~/.opencode/bin` or probe in `~/.local/bin` were missing, so the web Settings
  said OpenCode isn't installed (#1342); a `systemctl --user edit` override.conf sorts after it
  and wins. It stops the server `wb chat on` started (`chat.stop_started`, so the unit gets the
  port), then `daemon-reload`, `enable wb-chat` and `start` (`restart` when the drop-in changed).
  On macOS it writes the plist into `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` with `EnvironmentVariables` from
  `service_env` and a comment carrying `cli.SERVICE_MARK` (an absent copy, the shipped file's
  plain copy, an earlier release's (`cli.SHIPPED_PLISTS`, sha256s: 1.91's, which its comment said
  to copy by hand, ran on without the PATH and WB_* variables, #1406) or one with the mark is
  rewritten; any other is the user's, kept, and the line says `, yours`), boots out a
  loaded agent whose plist changed, and `launchctl bootstrap`s it. Then the service's chat must
  answer on `chat.PORT` within `START_WAIT` (`cli._came_up`): `enable --now` and `bootstrap`
  succeed when the server exits at once, and setup said `ok` over an app left down. One that
  doesn't is stopped (`systemctl --user disable --now wb-chat`, `launchctl bootout`), wb's own
  server started (`chat.ensure`), and the line is `--  web app service: <service> didn't answer
  within 10 s, so setup stopped it (…) and wb started its own server instead; <journalctl --user
  -u wb-chat | launchctl print …> says why, then wb setup again`. One line: `ok
  web app kept up by systemd's wb-chat (<link> → <unit>)`, a `--` line for a failed step, `--  web
  app off: no service installed (wb chat on, then wb setup)` with the switch off, nothing where
  neither manager serves this HOME (WSL without systemd, a container, a test's or sudo's HOME):
  the mod's `wb chat url` covers those. Safe to run again. **`wb doctor`** (`cli.chat_line`, only
  looking, never the token, never making one: no token file is `no server answers on port <port>`,
  since no server of this account's ran, #1281's review): `ok  web app answers on localhost:<port> (<chat.service_name> or
  started by wb)`, `--  web app off (wb chat on)`, or `BAD web app down: <why> (wb chat on)`. The
  bind stays loopback (`chat.plan`) and the link `chat.url`.
- **One listener.** A session listens while workbench mode and the chat are on; with several, the
  first live claim on `chat/listener.json` (its `wb events` pid and start). The user's message
  answering another session's row is that session's (#1096): `wb chat reply` stamps the session that
  wrote it, and that session's mod takes it, listening or not. On OpenCode (#1319) the listener is
  the OpenCode server whose plugin holds the claim (its pid and heartbeat), for the root session
  the user last typed in there; first live claim wins across both drivers, with no handoff between
  them (#1340: *The web chat on OpenCode*, under *The OpenCode plugin*).
- **Claude knows where the user is.** A web message has a typed message's authority, with a note:
  reply there, briefly; a yes there answers only a question asked there; nothing hard to undo on an
  ambiguous OK; while away, report there what finishes or needs them.
- **Away is the device the user last used** (#959). Away once they use the chat after last typing
  in the terminal (a web message, or a page shown, focused and in use on its Chat view: `POST
  /api/active`; never a click in Stats or Settings, or a tap on the nav leaving the chat, and a
  request whose Host is localhost, 127.* or ::1, the modeline's link on this machine, writes
  `page.json` alone: the web app is the desk's admin too, #1374; told by the Host, never the peer,
  since `tailscale serve` proxies a phone from loopback under its tailnet name), until
  they type or answer a dialog in the terminal (answering counts: a tapped notice made the user away
  and the answer submitted no prompt); at most 6 h after that use, longer while one of this
  session's tasks is open (#110; `--backlog` ones alone until #1402: one long task asked for from
  the phone was then reported in the terminal only). `chat/away.json` holds it, the user's, not one
  session's (#688).
- **Claude Code's dialogs are answered in the terminal** (#1350, from #1340's decision on the
  owner's bottom line: the terminal, local or ssh and tmux, is where things get done; the chat is
  for a message in a pinch). Nothing is answered on the phone, on either driver: a permission, a
  question (AskUserQuestion), a plan (ExitPlanMode) or an MCP server's form (an elicitation) waits
  in the terminal, and the page shows one line while it does, a `notice` (`wb chat notice`): `Claude
  is waiting for you in the terminal.` (OpenCode's: `OpenCode is waiting for you in the terminal.`,
  #1319), a permission's adding `Run it with permissions granted to
  work from the chat.` (`chat.WAITING`, `WAITING_GRANT`, the story's `note.*`); the page draws it as
  the driver's state line (*The driver's state line*), not a thread row: the driver's own permission modes and
  rules are the one permission policy, and run with them granted most work goes on from the chat
  (#1350's comment). No buttons; every kind, away or not, an agent's turn too; pushed as Claude's
  messages; at the terminal only for one still up after `NOTICE_AFTER_MS` 30 s, while away at once;
  one open per session. The dialog settled (its call went on, the form answered, the turn ended)
  clears the line (`chat.notice_done`: the thread leaves it out, it is never pushed late, the #959
  review) and counts as the user being back. Only for a chat user (a page used within
  `PAGE_RECENT`, a day, or push on). The answer cards, and the away setting that allowed an away
  user's permissions, went with the relay.
- **While away, a question or a plan goes to the chat, never a dialog** (#1351, #1340 B and C):
  with no card on the phone it would block the turn in a terminal nobody watches, the phone's
  messages queued behind it. The mod refuses AskUserQuestion with ``The user is away: ask in the
  web chat (`wb chat reply`) and end your turn.`` (`AWAY_QUESTION`) and ExitPlanMode with `Post the
  plan in the web chat and end your turn; approval is at the terminal.` (`AWAY_PLAN`); at the
  terminal both are ordinary dialogs. On the OpenCode path (#1319) the plugin refuses OpenCode's
  `question` tool from `execute.before` (a `permission.hook` deny loses the text) with ``The user is
  away: ask in the web chat (the workbench_chat_reply tool) and end your turn.`` (`chat.ts`
  `AWAY_QUESTION`, naming its tool by `REPLY_ID`); a plan has no dialog there (Plan is an agent). The
  words are the story's `refusal.*`, through the generated `mod/hooks/story.ts` both hosts import
  (*The story*, #1355). The mod's side: *The web chat
  listener*, under *The mod*; the plugin's: *The web chat on OpenCode*.

**Other agents** (#1042). The API is documented for other clients in `docs/chat-api.md` (every
endpoint, the stream, the agent flow with curl; `test_docs` fails on a path in `chat.py` it doesn't
name) and, machine-readable, in `docs/chat-api.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1, #1138: below), and `skill/agents/ask-workbench/` is a portable skill (agentskills.io: SKILL.md, and
`scripts/ask_workbench.py`, standard library only) the user points another agent at. The page is one
client; the server needs no browser.
- **Either driver** (#1366, for 2.2). The agent hands work to whichever driver listens, Claude
  Code or OpenCode, over the same API, and the skill, the doc and the API say which: the skill
  was `claude-workbench` with `ask_claude.py`, its every line "Claude". It is `ask-workbench`
  now (SKILL.md `name`), with `ask_workbench.py`, the MCP tool `ask_workbench` and the variables
  `WORKBENCH_URL`/`WORKBENCH_TOKEN` (`URL_VARS`, `TOKEN_VARS`: `CLAUDE_WB_URL`/`CLAUDE_WB_TOKEN`
  still read after them); `skill/agents/claude-workbench/` stays as a pointer (a SKILL.md saying
  it moved, and `ask_claude.py` and `mcp_server.py` that `runpy` the new scripts by path, so an
  install or MCP config made before 2.2 still runs; `ask_claude` still reaches `ask_workbench`,
  `ALIASES`, unlisted). The driver is `{tool: "claude"|"opencode", model?}` (`chat.DRIVER_TOOLS`,
  the tools of task.json's `driver` and `store.caller_kind`): `chat.listener_driver` reads a
  claim's (its own `driver`, a name or that object; else `opencode` when a live heartbeat,
  `store.heartbeats`, lists its `session`, with that session's model; else `claude`, as only the
  mod claimed before 2.2, and a claim with `parent` is the mod's at once, no beat read);
  `chat.listener_view` adds it to the listener every API answer carries (`/api/state` and the
  stream, `/api/wait`, `/api/send`), and `/api/health` says `driver` while one listens (not when
  none does: `{api, listening}` as before). `chat.send` stamps each of Claude's rows with its
  writer, `driver` (`chat.writer_driver`: `claude` under `CLAUDECODE`, `opencode` with
  `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` and its session's model from the live beat, `store.driver_server`; none for
  a terminal or an agent's shell); `from` stays `"claude"` (the API's name, any driver's).
  `ask_workbench.py` prints `[answered by Claude Code]` or `[answered by OpenCode (<model>)]` on
  stderr as a reply comes (`who`: the reply's `driver`, else the listener's), once and again on a
  change; the MCP server says the listener in `ask_workbench`'s answer (`driver`), and
  `get_reply` names who answered (`answered by …`, `driver` on the result and each reply).
- **Tokens.** `wb chat token add <name>` (`chat.agent_add`: `AGENT_NAME` `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`, not
  `AGENT_RESERVED`, one per name) prints `wba-` + `token_urlsafe(32)` once and keeps its sha256 in
  `chat-agents.json` beside the token file (`chat.agents_path`, 0600, under `chat-agents.lock`);
  `list`, `revoke` (`chat.agent_revoke`). `Handler._authed` returns `"user"` or `"agent <name>"`
  (`chat.agent_for`, constant time, the file read per request so a revoke is at once) and sets
  `Handler.agent`; an agent token from a peer that isn't this machine (`Handler._from_this_machine`: `127.*`, `::1`, or the very address it connected to, `Handler._local`: an agent here reaching a chat bound only to the tailnet or LAN IP comes from that IP, and was refused, #1274) is 403 `not_local` (``agent tokens work only from this machine, at the address `wb chat url` prints``) whatever the bind, as agents are this machine's own (owner, 2026-11-23), while the user's token still works from the tailnet or LAN; a held wait or open stream checks again at every wake (`Handler._revoked`:
  both went on reading its replies after a revoke, the #1042 review). An agent's token is on an
  allow-list, `AGENT_MAY` (`(method, path)` pairs, a trailing `/` matching by prefix: GET `/api/health`,
  `/api/wait`, `/api/state`, `/api/stream`, `/api/upload/`, `/api/file/`; PUT `/api/upload/`; POST
  `/api/send`; `chat.agent_may`), checked for every `/api/` request before its path's own handler
  (`Handler._gate`: the token's 401, then 403 `agent_forbidden`), so an endpoint added later is the user's alone until
  named there (#1280: the deny-lists it replaced, `AGENT_DENIED` and `AGENT_UNREAD`, left every new
  one open to agents). Every other path is 403 `agent tokens can't use <path>` (`chat.agent_refusal`),
  or the old wording where there was one (`AGENT_CANT`, wording only: `/api/push`, `/api/active`,
  `/api/seen`, `/api/latest`, `/api/shot`, `/api/audio`, `/api/transcribe/` (#1203), `/api/task` (#1201)); an unknown `/api/` path (off `chat.ROUTES`, #1138) is 401 without a token, 403 with an agent's, 404 with the user's. And 429 `{error, code: rate_limited, retry_after}` past
  `AGENT_SENDS_PER_MIN` 30 sends in any 60 s (`chat.RateLimit`, per agent, in the server's memory).
  No switch of its own: answered while the server runs and a token exists. With the chat off no
  session listens, so `/api/health` says `listening: false` and a message waits, unread, until one
  does, or `MESSAGE_EXPIRE` passes (a service keeps the server up through `wb chat off`: "on
  whenever the chat is", the docs said, #1127).
- **Marked.** Its message is `{from: <name>, role: "agent"}` (`chat._inbound`: indexed in
  `open.json`, receipted, expired, listed by `pending` as the user's), reaches Claude as `[agent
  <name>] …` (the mod, *The web chat listener*), never makes the user away, shows on the page with
  its name (`agentMeta`, `.row.agent`; no *send again*), and `wb chat log` says `agent <name>`.
  Claude's reply to agents alone (`to` without `"user"`) is no news for the user on the page either:
  its meta says `Claude to <name>` (`forUser`, as `chat._for_user`; `.row.claude.to-agent`), and it
  never counts in the tab's unread (it read as a reply to the user, counted, #1128). The
  skill: a teammate's request, answered with `wb chat reply --to <id>`, the user's consent gates
  untouched.
- **Send, then wait.** `wb chat reply` writes `re` (`--to`, else `chat.taken` for the listening
  session's own calls, `chat.caller_listens`: its `CLAUDE_PID` is listener.json's `parent`, either
  unknown counting as yes; when an OpenCode session calls or listens, `chat._listens_across`: an
  OpenCode caller (`store.opencode_session`) listens when the claim names its session, else only
  when the claim is OpenCode's (`listener_driver`) and names none, Claude Code's (`CLAUDE_PID`) never while
  OpenCode listens, a caller of neither still yes: with both drivers open the one not listening
  threaded its report onto the listener's message, #1363's matrix, #1366; another session's plain reply is the user's: its report went to the
  agent the listener was answering, pushed to no phone, #1129; the user's alone
  when it holds one of theirs: an agent's message delivered into the user's turn read every plain
  reply to them, the #1042 review; `taken`: the messages whose newest receipt is `now` by the listening session (never `into`: an agent's message the mod delivered into a wake turn, or queued or submitted behind a wake, took that turn's plain report to the away user, sent to the agent alone, pushed to no phone, #1175, #1212), under `MESSAGE_EXPIRE` old, that no
  `turns.jsonl` row lists: a session that died mid-turn left its agent's message taken, and the
  next session's replies went to that agent alone, the #1042 review) and `to`
  (whose: `"user"` or agent names; `chat.reply`; an unknown `--to` exits 1). `GET /api/wait?after=
  <id>&timeout=<0–600, WAIT_DEFAULT 300>&until=done|reply` (`Handler._wait`, `chat.wait_state`)
  returns Claude's rows after `after` `addressed` to the caller (`to` names it; no `to` is the
  user's) and `done`: since the newest of them, else since `after`, a turn has ended (a message to
  Claude: a `turns.jsonl` row lists it; a reply: a row `ended` at or after its `ts`, by its
  `turn_by` when it has one: another session's turn end with no ids, which every mod records once
  messages.jsonl grew in its turn, made the listener's "On it" done, #1303). It holds on
  the `Hub` until a reply, `done` (with `until=done`), nobody listening (at once: `listener:
  null`) or the timeout; at most `MAX_WAITS` 16 at once (503), each looking every `WAIT_LOOK` 1 s
  whether its client hung up (`Handler._gone`: an aborted wait held its slot to its timeout, and
  16 of them refused every wait, the #1042 review). `ask_workbench.py` asks a wait cut short again (a
  reset, or 502 to 504 from a proxy, while the server re-execs; 503: `TRANSIENT`), after a pause
  doubling from `RETRY_FIRST` 1 s to `RETRY_MOST` 15 s, then names `--after`: at its deadline
  (exit 1), or once the chat has been cut `OUTAGE_MOST` 120 s in a row (exit 2: off, asleep or
  out of reach, which a wait to the hour's deadline hid, the #1107 review); it ended at once with
  a bare error and no id (#1107). It also answers `waiting_on_user`
  (`chat.waiting_on_user`: a notice not yet settled, under `ASK_STALE` old), and
  returns when that turns true during the wait (once: true at its start, it holds). `wb chat reply
  --to user` addresses the user's thread whatever the turn took: a consent question during an
  agent's request went to that agent alone, pushed to no phone (the review). `GET /api/health`:
  `{api, listening, driver?}` (`driver` only while one listens, #1366). `/api/state` carries `api` (`API_VERSION` 1). A wait on a message to Claude
  unread past `MESSAGE_EXPIRE`, with no reply, is 410 `expired` at once (`chat.wait_state`'s
  `expired`, read through `chat.expired`): it was held to its timeout again and again, and
  `ask_workbench.py` waited out its whole deadline for an answer that could not come (#1138); the
  client exits 2.
- **Versioned paths, one error shape, retry safety** (#1138, for 2.1). Every `/api/<x>` is also
  `/api/v1/<x>` (`API_V1`): `Handler._versioned` rewrites the path first in `do_GET`, `do_PUT` and
  `do_POST`, so every check after it (`Handler._gate`'s `AGENT_MAY`, `chat.ROUTES`) sees the one
  name; `/api/` stays for the page and older clients, and `ask_workbench.py` keeps it. `chat.ROUTES`
  lists every route by method (one ending in `/` takes an id; `chat.routed`): `do_GET`, `do_PUT`
  and `do_POST` answer 404 for an `/api/` path off it once `_gate` has passed it (so an agent's
  token there is still 403, `agent_forbidden`), and `docs/chat-api.yaml`, the OpenAPI 3.1
  description (the `/api/v1/` paths, bearer auth, the `Error` schema and each status's response,
  the `Idempotency-Key` parameter and `Idempotent-Replayed` header, `x-user-only` on what an agent
  may not call), describes exactly those: `test_docs` reads it with a parser of the YAML subset it
  is written in (`read_yaml`: no PyYAML) and fails on a route in one and not the other, a route in
  `ROUTES` that isn't a branch of its `do_<method>` (or a branch off it), a dangling `$ref`, a
  refusal not answered with `Error`, `Error`'s `code` enum against `ERROR_CODES` and
  `ERRORS_SAID`, or `x-user-only` against every route outside `AGENT_MAY` (`chat.agent_may`). Every error answer is
  `{error, code, …}` (`Handler._json` adds `code` from `ERROR_CODES` by status unless the answer
  names its own: `token_revoked`, `not_local`, `unknown_host`, `agent_forbidden`,
  `bad_idempotency_key`, and `not_audio` for `/api/transcribe/`'s 415 (the upload's type, not the
  request's), `ERRORS_SAID`); `error` stays the text, as `app.ts` and `ask_workbench.py`
  show it as is. `Handler.send_error` answers http.server's own refusals (501 for another method,
  a malformed request line) in that shape: they were HTML. A revoked agent token's sha256 moves to
  `chat-agents.json`'s `revoked` (the newest `REVOKED_KEPT` 200; `chat.token_revoked`), so its
  next request, held wait included (`REVOKED`), is 401 `token_revoked`, not `bad_token`.
  `POST /api/send` with an `Idempotency-Key` (`IDEM_KEY`: 1 to 255 printable ASCII, no spaces;
  else 400 `bad_idempotency_key`) runs under `chat/idempotency.lock` (`Handler._send_once`): the
  key's record (`chat.idem_key`: the caller's name and the key's sha256) within `IDEM_FOR` (a day)
  answers with the message it sent (`chat.message`, from anywhere in messages.jsonl) and
  `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, sending nothing and costing no rate-limit slot (the limit is now
  counted in `Handler._send_message`, after the body is read); another body under it
  (`chat.idem_request`, the JSON with sorted keys) is 422 `idempotency_key_reused`; only a sent
  message is recorded (`chat.idem_record`). An upload needs none: its id is stored once.
  `ask_workbench.py` sends one fresh UUID as both the key and the `cid`, and sends again after a cut
  (a reset, 502 to 504) for up to `OUTAGE_MOST`: it ended at once, exit 1, and a rerun asked
  Claude twice. Still cut then, it exits 2 naming the key (`Unreachable`: it may have landed,
  and exit 1 named nothing to follow, the #1138 review); `--key` reruns the request under it
  (`KEY`: at most 64, as it is the `cid` too), its uploads' ids a `uuid5` of the key and each
  file's sha256, so the rerun's body is the first one's (a random id was a new body: 422).
- **Kept apart.** A `cid` another sender used is 409 (`chat.send`: an agent's send could get the
  user's message back); an agent's stream never makes the oldest give way (503 at once); the mod
  indents an agent's later lines, so none starts as `[web chat]` or `[message …]` (`chatPrompt`).
  An agent's `about` is 400 `agent messages can't carry about` (what a message answers is the
  user's to say).
- **The MCP server** (#1138, for 2.1): `skill/agents/ask-workbench/scripts/mcp_server.py`, a
  stdio MCP server (newline-delimited JSON-RPC, as `ask_mcp.py`: `initialize` with the client's
