message's end, never the engine's timeout, `aborted: still running after …ms`, which is wb hung and
said as a failure, #553) is `aborted`, with no message: not wb failing, so nothing says `could not run wb` (nor `wb status failed`), and a read the pane keeps (the roles,
the chat link) keeps its last value and reads again
(#1142). Growing files
are read by `readTail`: whole up to 1 MiB (events 64 KiB), else `tail -c` from a whole line, since
`$.fs.read` rejects a file over 4 MiB (no wake came again, the 2026-11-16 audit).

**poll()** (re-entrant calls set `again`): `scan` reads every `tasks/*/status.json`, then
`task.json` for the tasks shown (closed ones drop out 30 min after their last update and aren't
read again that load; open ones get their last 4 event lines, `recentEvents`, cached by
size@mtime, #739); the status line; opens the pane once per load for a queued/running/testing task
of the session's or the mode on (unasked only on a wide terminal; one the user closed stays
closed); refreshes the transcript only while the pane shows (#838; `wb watch <task> --json
--last 2000` every `LIVE_EVERY_MS` 5 s while active, #691; `focusOf` sticks to the followed task);
submits one queued turn when idle (a dropped one waits a minute); the boundary compaction; the
weekly check, the update check beside it; then `deliver`, `rewake`, `listen`, `readSwitch` and
`settingsTurns` (*Seeing what the agent does*); `chatLink` runs on its own minute's timer.

**Busy.** `mem.busy` is set by `turn.start` (main loop) and by the model's own main-loop
`tool.call` (`next.origin.plugin === 'engine'`: a module reloaded mid-turn never saw `turn.start`;
not a subagent's or another plugin's, which no `turn.complete` would clear), cleared only by the
main loop's `turn.complete`.

**Waking** (`deliver`; its decisions are the kernel's `noticesDue` and `noticePlan`, *The kernel*,
which the OpenCode plugin's notices follow too). Only when notify.jsonl's size or mtime changed, Claude is busy, or a wake
was held (rows cached in `mem.notifyRows`, #921). Per task, the newest notify row under an hour old
and every question row past `acked`; still true when a check-in and the task is
queued/running/testing, a question while the phase is `asking` and `ask/<id>.json` has no
`<id>.answer`, or the phase equals the kind; a stale one is acked and dropped. A true one is
toasted once (`workbench: <name> <headline>`); a task not `mine` (its `session` among the ids, else
by directory) gets nothing more. Busy: a question goes into the turn (`intoTurn`: `acked` first, put
back if refused, `mem.heldAsks`), anything else waits; a held question whose `<id>.answer` opens
with ask_mcp's NO_ANSWER gets the MISSED_NOTE wake. Else `acked = row.ts` and `wake` submits
`[workbench] Task \`<n>\` <headline>.\n\n<row.text>\n\n<NEXT[kind]>`, plus, while away (each wake and
`intoTurn`: `awayToo`, #540), `\n\n<AWAY_NOTE>` once an away stretch (the `web-chat` block or the first
wake: `mem.awayNoted`, cleared by `back` and once a poll finds the user not away, `awayEnded`) and
`(User away: answer with \`wb chat reply\`.)` (`AWAY_TAIL`) after it; every wake carried the whole
paragraph (#1322). HEADLINE and NEXT are at the top of register.tsx; a question's NEXT is `wb answer
<n> --id <id>`, and only a notice opening `PERMISSION to ` (`PERMISSION`, ask_mcp.notice's openings)
adds the `wb allow` paragraph (#1322: every question carried it). A dropped submit (`{drop}`) puts `acked` back if unchanged, records `mem.dropped`,
toasts once. With `wake` off it is only toasted and `acked` isn't written, so `wb wait` still gets
it. `rewake` (the kernel's `rewakePlan`): idle, wake on, a `mine` task waiting on Claude whose status changed between
60 s and 12 h ago, whose news Claude hasn't had and whose wake wasn't
dropped in the last minute, gets `acked = now` and a prompt with `wb report <n>` and its newest
notice's headline and next step (`headlineOf`, `nextOf`, deliver's; that notice one of a batch:
its own `BATCH_NEXT`; none in `mem.notifyRows`, or of another kind than the phase: `HEADLINE` and
NEXT, #1384). Had the
news: `acked` at or past the later of `mem.noticed` (each task's newest notice in the tail, a
batch's for each task it names) and the task's `noticed` file (the runner's last status write lands
after its notice, so `updated_at` alone woke twice, #844), else past `updated_at`. `cli._ack_all`
stops short of news still true. Wakes are submitted as the plugin, not `asUser`. The state
directory is global, so each session acts only on its own tasks (the 2026-11-16 audit); among a
task's sessions the first to deliver wins (the `acked` write is not locked).

**Workbench mode** (`workbenchMode(on)`, `chat.delegating`). On: the `workbench` skill's prompt
(`skill.prompt`, which opens the pane via `showPane`; again while on with no task, read by
`firstTask` from the skill's "**First task:** \`…\`" line, it returns AGAIN_NOTE instead; with no
task on a fresh install, `freshInstall`: nothing under `tasks/`, `results.jsonl` empty or missing,
no role on API, read from the files so the mod keeps no state, it returns the whole skill with
`FIRSTRUN_NOTE` after it, `[workbench-firstrun] A fresh install: …`, which SKILL.md's *First task*
reads as "run *First run* now", #1190: in the skill's text, since `prompt.context` fires only at a
conversation's first message), or a
Bash call running `wb start|next|feedback|steer|answer|resume` (`delegates`, the kernel's `gateOf` `delegates`; not
`accept` or `takeover`, which a quit's notes ask for). Only a command counts, not text (#409), read
as bash reads it (`simpleCommands`, #560): quotes undone within a word, comments and heredoc
bodies dropped (`$(…)` and backticks in unquoted heredocs and double quotes still run; a `$(…)` in
double quotes ends where bash ends it, `closing`: quotes, comments and heredoc bodies skipped, so a
quoted heredoc's "doesn't (it can't)" or "a)" doesn't close it, #1364's review), a
redirect's file (`>`, `>>`, `>|`, `&>`, `<`; `2>&1` a descriptor) and a here-string no words of the
command (#1364: kept beside it, `Shell`: its stdin, its redirects' files, the command piped into
it), split at `;`, `&`, `|`, newlines, `(`, `)`, `$(`, backticks; the command word past `VAR=x`, the reserved
words and the wrappers with their options (`Kernel.Gate`'s `gateOf`, `at`: `env`, `time`, `nohup`, `exec`, `command`,
`timeout` and its duration, `nice`, `ionice`, `stdbuf`, `sudo`, `doas`, `xargs`) must be `wb` or end in `/wb`. Syntactic:
`true || wb steer` counts. Off: either quit. While on: the `workbench-mode`, `user-notes` (and
`claude-coding`, `dynamic-workflows`) blocks, the idle status line, pane auto-open, chat listening, the boundary
compaction. `mem.delegated` remembers it was on in this load, so a hand-back's compaction still
keeps the state. No `$.ui.invalidate`: rewriting the
first message would cost the prompt cache.

**Commands.** All are `/workbench` (the skill) or start with `workbench-`, so `/workbench` lists
them. `showPane` first closes a pane the engine holds but doesn't show. The quits: *Stopping
everything*. `/workbench-models` records the check as raised (scout.json `offered_at`,
`scoutAsked`) and queues SCOUT_NOTE, the check's only turn. `/workbench-update` runs `wb update` and, when it updated,
`/reload-plugins` (`$.command.run`). A command can't start a turn itself: it pushes onto
`mem.queued`, which the next idle poll submits.

**Context blocks** (`prompt.context`, in this order; computed at the first message and after a
compaction or `/clear`, not every turn): `workbench-mode` while delegating (MODE_NOTE: until a quit,
follow the skill, every plan is a handoff plan, the SKILL.md path); `user-notes` while delegating
with notes; `dynamic-workflows` with Dynamic workflows on, delegating or a task open (*Dynamic workflows*); `web-chat` while away (`awayNow`; AWAY_NOTE: "The user is away from the terminal: they
last used the web chat", reply with `wb chat reply`); `workbench-wake` with `wake` off, delegating
or a `mine` task open (WAKE_OFF_NOTE: no wake will come, tell the user); `workbench` when `wb
status` with `scope()` exits 0 listing open tasks or runs (with no task open, the run lines after `no open tasks`
alone: dropped whole, a run at review was never said, #1491; plus the story's `tasks.pickup`, the OpenCode plugin's
`TASKS_NOTE` line word for word: `wb report`, and `wb wait` to follow one, never `wb watch`, which follows a
task until it closes, so a driver on one at review waited out its shell's timeout, #1515; a failure toasts
once). None without a person.

**The rules said later** (#540). A block can't be added after the first message, so a session that
entered the mode later got no notes, no wake-off note, no coding rule. `mem.said` (`Said`, set by
`prompt.context`) records what was told; `unsaid` returns what is missing and counts it said (the kernel's `tellPlan`, which picks `prompt.context`'s blocks too; the
notes once, the wake-off note once, the coding rule whenever the mode differs; CODING_DECIDE on a
return to "Let Claude decide"; the workflows rule whenever it differs, WORKFLOWS_OFF on a return to off). `/workbench` appends them to its text and sets `mem.skillTurn`, so a
`prompt.context` in that turn leaves them out (a compaction or the turn's end clears it). Every poll runs `sayRules`: unsaid rules go in as a
user-role row (`$.session.append`, no turn), or, refused, a queued `[workbench]` turn. Away isn't
one: it rides on each wake (`awayToo`).

**Compaction.** `session.compact` (main conversation, a `mine` task open, delegating now or in this
load) appends KEEP_ON_COMPACT: keep the user's goals and decisions, the tasks and what each needs,
what was accepted, merged or discarded; drop finished tasks' diffs, reports, transcripts. At a task
boundary in the mode (a task of the last open set gone, Claude idle, none waiting on Claude) it
compacts once usage reaches `WB_COMPACT_AT`% (default half; 0 off) of the auto-compact
threshold (or the window), with no toast of its own (Claude Code shows the compaction, #1322): the
kernel's `compactPlan` judges the boundary and the usage, the mod reads them and compacts.

**Status line and pane.** `⚒ wb · <name> <phase> r<round>` for queued/running/testing, `<name>
asks`, `<N> awaiting review`, `<N> stuck`, `<N> failed` (each counted apart: one review and one stuck
task read `2 awaiting review`, #1048; not parked: `phaseOf`'s `waits`, #541; `mine` only, #693; tallied by the
kernel's `openCounts`, as the pane's group header is), joined by
` · `; `⚒ wb · workbench mode` with nothing listed. The pane: the task list (*The Tasks view*, below);
the followed task's transcript (lines cut to `LINE_CHARS` 2000,
within `HISTORY_CHARS` 60,000: Claude Code drops pane text past 100,000), following the newest
unless scrolled up; the stage (the apprentice as pixels at 20 rows by 40 columns or more, else its
one-line face; text wrapped by `wrapWords`, as Text's own wrapping beside the raster drew empty
rows); the modeline. The modeline and the strip (`AbovePrompt`): *Seeing what the agent does*. The apprentice (`apprentice.ts`): 16×12 pixel art in half blocks into a
`Raster` (cells as little-endian u32 triplets, base64), a pose per state (rest, blink, think, work,
swing, tada, ask, slump, sleep), FACE the one-line faces; the bubble is tasks.ts's `speechOf` (shared with the OpenCode panel, #1312).

**The Tasks view** (#1048; the owner, web chat 2026-11-23: "progress bar indicators or something,
some type of indications showing me everything that's going on while it happens"). `hooks/tasks.ts`
lays the list out (the design study's reference renderer, mock.py, ported rule for rule;
`tasks.test.ts` holds its mockups character for character) and `register.tsx` draws it: `scan` adds
each task's facts (`viewFacts`, from the task.json and status.json it already reads: nothing new is
read), `listRows` asks `taskLines` for the rows and adds a task's `wb coding allow` line after them,
and the render draws one `Text` a row (`wrap="truncate-end"`; none is wider than the pane, so
`pageShape` counts them exactly). One task is at most two rows. Line 1: the glyph (the spinner
running, else ◌ ◐ ? ◆ ▲ ✗ ✓ –: no state told by colour alone), the name (underlined when followed),
the stage (`round 2 · fix 1/2`, `round 3 · self-review`, `waits for the GPU`, `review · tests ✓`…,
from status `round_for` and the runner's `last`: the queued words match the prefixes
`transcript.activity` matches), the place (`GPU`, `GPU 1` from status `cards`, `API DeepSeek`), the
model (an API task's id's last part, a GPU task's label), the role (`complex`, `trivial`,
`writing`), the spend (status `api`: wave 2's `usd`, `plan`, `no price`) and the elapsed time
(`3m ago` for a review). Line 2, `⎿`: what it did last (an asking task's question, a stuck one's
`… · Claude steers it next`) and its meters: `ctx █████▋░░ 71%` (status `live_used` of this
session over `window`, `┊` at `tuned.fresh_at`), `~6m left` or `3m over` against status `typical`
(only with `TYPICAL_MIN` 3 timed tasks), the tool count and `3.9K out` (tokens written: the input
re-reads the context each step). Late is coloured only from the progress checks' own points, 1× and
2× status `late_min` (step A's review: a 4-minute median coloured a 5-minute task late, where no
check comes before `progress.FLOOR_MIN`), and only once the estimate says `over` (an `--after` under
the typical length coloured it beside `~12m left`; no estimate shown, no colour); an API task `hosted.json` doesn't list has no typical and
shows no estimate. A passing review, a parked task and a closed one have no line 2; closed ones fold
into one dim line per block. Tasks of one `--group` (two or more) sit under a header (`▾ hiscore · 3
tasks · 2 running · 1 testing   $0.04  ░░░░░░░░ 0/3 done`, done counting reviews and closed ones;
narrow, it drops the bar, the spend, then `· 3 tasks`, so `· 1 stuck` stays) joined by `├ │ └`; blocks and their tasks keep start order, so nothing jumps. Columns line up within
a block and drop for the whole block until the widest row fits: line 1 the role, the model, the long
stage (`r2`), the long place (`API`), the place; line 2 the tokens, the bar to 5 cells, the tool
count, the bar (`ctx 56%` stays), the estimate. One row a task (`compactWanted`) in a pane under 20
rows (the 14-row box below a ~100-column terminal) or when two would leave the transcript, the
apprentice and the modeline under 12 rows. A press on a task's first row (a `plain` Button
keyed `task-<name>`) follows it (`followTask`, `mem.picked`, which `focusOf` keeps while the task is
listed). While an API task works (running, testing or asking: not one queued for its slot, the
owner's "only while an API task runs"), `API today ≈$0.42 of the $5 day cap  ▉░░░░░░░░░` (no `≈` at the user's prices, #1135) sits above the
modeline (`capRow`: warning from `WARN_SHARE`, half the cap, its own, error at the cap), from `wb route --json` as
`rolesNow` caches it, read again past `ROLES_CACHE_MS` off the render's path (`capNow`).

**The web chat listener** (`listen`: workbench mode, chat on, an events child). Another session's
live claim makes this one stand by (`claimStands`, which `settingsTurns` asks too): its pid alive and, with a `start`, still started then (`alive`,
from `/proc/<pid>/stat` or `ps -o lstart=` as wb reads it, UTC then the local zone, #848; when
neither can say, alive while listener.json is under 15 s old, #700); without a pid, `ts` within
15 s; asked only of another's claim, at most every `PID_CHECK_MS` 30 s (#839); another `machine`'s
always lives (#922; a crashed one there stands until a session on that machine or a quit clears
it). Standing by, it still takes the user's messages that answer its own rows (below). Otherwise it
writes `chat/listener.json` on a change (with `parent`, `mem.claudePid`, #1129) and delivers each
unreceipted message from `open.json` once `wb chat claim <id> --by <key>` grants it (refused:
retried a minute later; two sessions both submitted one, #84): idle → `prompt.submit('[web chat]
<words>', asUser)`, receipt `now` (an agent's behind a prompt submitted this poll, `mem.submitted`: `into`, #1212); busy → `session.send` with WEB_NOTE (an agent's: AGENT_NOTE, receipt `into`, so the turn's plain `wb chat reply` is never its answer, #1175), else a queued prompt
(`queued`, acked `now`, an agent's `into`, when that turn ends: `mem.chatQueued`, `readQueued`; acked `now`, the next wake turn's report went to the agent, #1212); `wb chat ack <id> --by
<key> --how …` once it entered (a dropped prompt is retried a minute later); `chat/away.json` `{at:
now, by: <key>}`. Away is read by every session (`away()`); a typed prompt writes `{at: 0}`
(`back`), as does a terminal dialog settled there (`termDialogDone`). Typed is
`byUser` on the engine's `origin.kind`: `composer`, `bridge`, `sdk`, `auto-continuation`, or an
`unclassified` or unstamped one not `isMeta` (a /loop, another plugin's or a peer's prompt ended away
for everyone, #835). **Whose a message is** (#1096; the page has no reply-to): the user's answers
Claude's last row to the user before it (`answersTo`, from `messages.jsonl`'s last `THREAD_TAIL` 64 KiB,
`claudeRows`, read once a poll and only for a user's message), which names its session (`session`,
`claude_pid`, `claude_start`, `claude_machine`: `cli._chat_writer`, as task.json has them). That session
(in `mem.ids`) takes it, listening or standing by; the listener leaves it to another live session for
`HANDOFF_MS` 30 s (its process judged by `noteClaude`, `mem.deadPids`), then takes it itself with
`ELSEWHERE_NOTE` after `[web chat] `: it follows another session's message; leave that session's task to
it and tell the user to answer at its terminal. When that process is gone the listener takes it at once
and plain: its nearby tasks are the listener's own now (`mine`), and its terminal is gone. A row without a
session (a terminal's reply, an older wb) and an agent's message are the listener's, as before; with
one listener for all, the answer to session B's report reached A, which the skill tells to leave B's
tasks alone. An expired message (claim refuses it) isn't tried again this load
(`mem.chatExpired`; one toast, #536). Quitting stops delivery and empties listener.json if held.

Each message passed on is owed a chat reply (`mem.chatOwed`, `owedAtTurnEnd`, #767: phone
questions were answered in the terminal only for two releases): a `from: claude` row since it was
given, of this Claude Code's to the message's sender (`to`, none: the user; `claude_pid` its own,
or none: an older wb's row; `chat.send` stamps every one, as another session's screenshot still
settled it when only `reply` did, the #1129 review) or answering it (`re` holds its id), or a
typed prompt settles it (any session's row did: another's report kept the reply from going,
#1129). An agent's message (`Owed.agent`, its name) is settled only by a row to it or answering
it, never by a plain reply or the user's return (`userOwedClear`; #1273: a plain `wb chat reply`
went to the user's phone and settled the agent's debt, so its wait heard nothing). The mod's own
`auto` post settles only by `re`: it is always this Claude Code's, so the first of two messages
given in one poll had its answer settle the second's, which never got one (the #1352 review). At
the end of the main turn that had it
(`grace` 1 when it was queued behind a running turn or behind a prompt the mod submitted that
poll, `mem.submitted`, #837) with no reply, the mod posts that turn's own answer (`turn.complete`'s
`answer`, at most `ANSWER_ARGV` 16,000 characters on the command line) with `wb chat reply
--turn-answer --text=<answer> --to=<id>…` (one post per answer and sender, `--to` each message of
that sender's it answers, so an agent's wait gets it, #1042, and never one post to both the user and
an agent, #1273): an `auto` row, cut to `chat.TURN_ANSWER_MAX` 4,000 characters
ending `TURN_ANSWER_CUT` (#1352, from #1340 F). It replaced a nudge turn (`OWED_NOTE` or an agent's
`AGENT_OWED_NOTE`, then the `OWED_POSTED` note, which a regex on Bash, `REPLIES`, settled even when
the post failed): that cost
Claude a turn, and a driver that doesn't follow the skill (OpenCode's, #1296) left the phone with
nothing. A failed post (a toast, once: `chat-owed`), or a turn that said nothing (thinking only, an
interrupt), leaves the message owed: the next turn's end posts again, the failed post's answer
first (`Owed.answer`). `turn.complete` awaits the post; the turn-end record below waits on it.

**Agents' messages and the turn-end record** (#1042). A message with `role: "agent"` and a name
wb makes (`agentOf`: `[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`) is delivered as the user's are but submitted as `[agent
<name>] <words>` (with `about` and attachments as above) and a last line `[message <id>: answer
with wb chat reply --to <id>]` (`chatPrompt`; mid-turn with AGENT_NOTE), toasts `a message from
agent <name>` (the user's own message toasts nothing: they just sent it, #1322), and writes no `away.json` (an agent never makes the user away); a prompt starting
`[agent ` is never the user typing (`prompt.submit`). Each message given to Claude goes into
`mem.chatTurn` with its `grace`, as `mem.chatOwed`; at each main turn's end (`chatTurnEnd`) those
at 0 are recorded with `wb chat ended <ids> --by <key>`, and with none, a turn in which
`chat/messages.jsonl` grew (stat at `turn.start`, `chatTurnStart`, a promise the end awaits: a
turn ending before its stat came back once read the size from the turn before, 2026-11-24; a
reply, maybe a later report) is recorded with no ids. Nothing while the chat is off. The record
is written after the owed reply's post (`chatTurnEnd`'s `after`, #1352: it ran beside the post,
so an agent's wait could end before the answer was in the thread); its start size is taken first.

**A question or a plan while away** (#1351): the `tool.call` hook's `awayRefusal`, before any other
check, denies AskUserQuestion with `AWAY_QUESTION` and ExitPlanMode with `AWAY_PLAN` (`AWAY_REFUSAL`)
while the session delegates with the chat on and the user is away (`away`), so neither dialog
comes up; at the terminal both pass through.

**Dialogs: the waiting line** (#1350). `classic.PermissionRequest` (its `kind` from `DIALOG_KIND`:
ExitPlanMode a `plan`, AskUserQuestion a `question`, else a `permission` with the input's command,
file_path, url, path or pattern, else its JSON, cut at 1500, `askText`) and `classic.Elicitation`
(`elicitation`, its tool `mcp:<server>`, its message) note a dialog (`dialogUp`), unless a settings
hook decided or the session isn't delegating with the chat on: `mem.termDialogs` (`{tool, agent,
input, at, due, kind, text, id}`, `due` at once while away, else `NOTICE_AFTER_MS` 30 s on). The hook
answers nothing: the dialog is the terminal's. `termNotices` (at once while away, else on the poll's
tick) runs `wb chat notice --tool=<t> --kind=<kind> --text=<text>` (each `--opt=value`, so a
leading `-` isn't a flag) for one due while no other line of the session's is open (a failure:
`warnOnce`). The engine's `tool.call` ending (its permission check and its run) settles the oldest
noted dialog of that call in that loop (`agentId`, and `sameCall`: every argument both carry the
same, as ExitPlanMode's empty input matches its dialog's plan; by tool alone a Read allowed by a
rule finishing beside one asking cleared an away user's line and marked them back, the #1042 and
#1350 reviews; in the hook's `finally`),
`classic.ElicitationResult` an elicitation's, and `turn.complete` any left (an interrupt drops a
waiting hook): `termDialogDone` drops it, runs `back` (settling is the user at the terminal, #1350)
and `wb chat notice --done <id>`. In an agent's turn the same (#1042's cards are gone). The relay it
replaced answered the dialog from the page. **The state line** (#1355): `listen` puts
`waitingFact(mem.termDialogs, now)` (`mod/hooks/waiting.ts`: the oldest up `WAITING_AFTER_MS` 2 s or
more) in the claim as `waiting`, left out when none (`mem.waitSaid`, what it last said); the
tick (`POLL_MS`) polls when the fact moved, so the page has it within a tick and not the idle
poll's 30 s. A consent dialog (`consent`: a send, a role change, a coding edit) is one too,
`kind: "consent"`, `tool: "workbench"`, for as long as `$.ui.ask` is up, never a notice row.

**The weekly model check** (`scoutIfDue`): in a session delegating now or in this load, with wakes
on (another project's session spent the offer, #919; such a session leaves scout.json alone), once
`wb events` said hello, Claude idle `SCOUT_QUIET_MS` (a minute) after a main-loop turn (raised at
once, it buried Claude's question), quiet (`quietForJobs`: no task anywhere active, none of this
session's unparked ones waiting on Claude within rewake's 12 hours, `rewakePlan`'s `recent`, #541), once per load, when
scout.json's `done_at` is 7+ days old and no `offered_at` since it fell due: it writes `offered_at` and
toasts `SCOUT_DUE` (`workbench: the weekly model check is due: /workbench-models`), at most once a due
period. It submitted SCOUT_NOTE as a turn of its own, about 650 tokens, again daily until done
(#1322). SCOUT_NOTE (`/workbench-models`): `wb scout` and what it flags, research, recommend
keep/add/retire, ask before downloading or deleting; GPU and API alike, #1024: for roles on API `wb
scout`'s API section, newer or cheaper models from the same providers on their own pages, whether
thinking would pay for significant; it names no model; then `wb scout --done --notes`. The skill
library's and the media licences' steps are `wb scout`'s own lines, printed when they apply.

**The weekly update check**: once a load, after the first main-loop turn once wb runs, beside the
poll (a stalled fetch held every wake): `wb update --check --if-due` (origin fetched at most every `UPDATE_EVERY`, a
week; in between counted locally, else `update.json`'s `behind`); `update available` becomes a toast naming `/workbench-update`, once a
session until installed, and so does `local changes in the marketplace clone` (`LOCAL_CHANGES`, `patches.CHECK_LINE`),
which comes alone when nothing is new upstream (only `update available` was toasted, so the warning reached nobody,
#1005).

**Claude's calls in a worktree** (`callRows`, `noteCall`, in the same `tool.call` hook, after its gates, #1211):
each Bash command that runs in or names a task's directory (`tasksNamed`) and each edit tool's file in a worktree
(`taskOfPath`), from anyone, is written as it begins (`end` null) and again once over (`end`, or `denied`), to
`rules/<task>/claude-calls/` (*Files and formats*), for a task with a task.json; `wb accept` and `wb next` tell
Claude's own files from its builds' output by them, a `wb accept` in the same call as a build by the build's row (#1272) (*The runner, inside*, `runner._claude_built`). Facts for wb, not the mod's state: it never reads them.

**The consent gate** (`sendRefusal`, in the `tool.call` hook every call passes, #1005). Nothing goes to workbench
upstream without the user's yes to that very call, in a dialog: Claude's, a subagent's or another plugin's alike, from
Bash, Monitor (its `command` runs in the same shell) or a GitHub MCP tool. A rule in the skill is advice Claude may
misread; this is the one place every call passes. Outward (the kernel's `gateOf`, its gate `outward`, or `send`; *The kernel*):
`gh pr create|comment|edit|merge|review|close|reopen|ready|update-branch|lock|unlock`,
`gh issue create|comment|edit|close|reopen|delete|lock|unlock|transfer|pin|unpin|develop`,
`gh repo fork|edit|delete|rename|archive|unarchive|sync`, `gh workflow run|enable|disable`, `gh run rerun|cancel|delete`,
`gh release create|edit|delete|upload|delete-asset`, `gh label create|edit|delete|clone` (past
`-R`/`--repo`), `gh api` with a method other than GET or HEAD, or with fields, `git push` (past git's own
options; its `-C` directories, `dirs`), and `wb patch send` (`wb` or a path to it, or Python running `…/wb` or `-m workbench`);
command words lowercased (macOS finds `GIT` as git). Read as bash reads it (`simpleCommands`; the reading, from here to
`upstreamAim`, is `mod/hooks/shell.ts`, which the OpenCode plugin's `upstream.ts` reads lines with too, #1296; the command word
`gateOf`'s `at` as in `delegates`, past `sudo`, `doas`, `xargs` and the other wrappers): echo and heredoc text isn't a command, `$(…)`
and backticks are, and a shell's `-c '…'` (`STDIN_SHELL`: `bash`, `sh`, `zsh`, `dash`, `ksh`, `ash`, `fish`) and
`eval` are read inside; a line naming none of `gh`, `git`, `wb`,
`workbench` isn't parsed. What a program that runs text (`RUNS_CODE`) is handed (`runs`, `codeFed`: a heredoc, a
here-string, the words and stdin of a command piped into it, an interpreter's `-c`/`-e`, a script the line itself
wrote by a redirect, `cat > s.sh <<EOF … EOF` then `bash s.sh`; not another script file) counts by
what runs (#1364): a shell's (`STDIN_SHELL`, `sh -s` too) is read as commands, `bash <<EOF … git push` once went
through, and a send there is asked about as one inside text another program runs (the dialog shows the line);
an interpreter's code is text, an outward command in it (`OUTWARD_TEXT`, as a string or a list: `['git', 'push']`)
counting only when the code runs commands at all (`spawns`: Python's `subprocess`, `os.system`, …, Node's
`child_process`, `execSync(`, …, Perl's, Ruby's and PHP's `system(`, backticks, …). A heredoc or quoted text any other
command gets is its data: a Python heredoc editing an issue body that named `wb patch send` was refused as a send three
times on 2026-11-24, nothing being sent. Aimed at upstream
(`upstreamAim`): `wb patch send` always; another outward command when the line names a gated directory (as written,
through `~`, `$HOME` or `$WB_HOME`: `mentions`) or runs in one (`cd`, `cd --` and `pushd` followed from the session's
directory, git's `-C`; by real path too, a symlinked spelling), or runs in Claude Code's plugins directory in a
checkout whose origin is upstream (a marketplace renamed), or when the line anywhere names the upstream's owner/repo
(`export GH_REPO=<slug> && gh issue create` named it outside the outward command), unless that runs in a developer's own
clone of upstream (`developerClone`: `git -C <dir> remote get-url origin`, 5 s, `originIs`; never a gated directory or
inside the plugins directory), which is no user's Claude. The gated directories (`gateConf`): the patch clone,
`patches.json`'s `source`, else `WB_SOURCE`, else `~/.local/share/workbench/source`; `$WB_HOME/upstream/`; and Claude
Code's own `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude>/plugins/` (and `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`) `marketplaces/workbench` and
`cache/workbench`: the marketplace install's clone has upstream as its origin, and was once exempted as a developer's
(the review of #1005). The upstream: `patches.json`'s `upstream`, else `UPSTREAM` (`a-schaefers/workbench`); the gate matches each of those and the former names in `FORMER_UPSTREAM` (`a-schaefers/claudes-workbench`, renamed 2026-11-24: GitHub redirects it, so a send naming it, or a clone and `patches.json` still saying it, lands upstream and asks first).
A GitHub MCP tool (`GITHUB_MCP`, `mcp__…github…__<name>`) not named `get_`/`list_`/`search_` whose input names the
upstream, or a repository of its name (a fork), asks the same (`mcpAimsUpstream`), its input shown up to `MCP_CHARS`
4000. The question (`askToSend`, through `consent`) is always the terminal's `$.ui.ask`, a dismissed one (an interrupt)
a no; with the user away on the web chat (`away`) the chat gets one line first, `wb chat reply --to=user` with
`CONSENT_WAITING` (`Claude is waiting on a workbench dialog in the terminal: answer it there.`, the story's `refusal.consent`). The owner's rule (#1340,
2026-11-24): consent is answered in the terminal, locally or over ssh and tmux, never relayed to the chat for answering.
It was refused while they were away (`NOT_SENT_AWAY`), a round trip for nothing, and #1322's first cut asked on the chat
page, which cut a long question at `chat.ASK_TEXT` unmarked and left a user back at the terminal with no dialog. The text: `Claude wants to send this to GitHub (<slug>), publicly: <the command>`, the whole line up to
`SHOW_CHARS` 600, a longer one as the outward command in full, then the line's start (`shownCommand`: cut from the
start, a long line hid the gh command and its body); for `wb patch send` its `--title` and the body file's first
`BODY_LINES` 20 lines (`sendQuestion`, `gateOf`'s `send`: the last `--title`/`--body-file` given, as argparse takes them; wb
refuses abbreviations). A send it can't show is refused without asking (`NOT_SHOWN`: no slug, `--title` or
`--body-file`, a `$` or backtick in either, the kernel's `send.lack`: `slug`, `title`, `bodyFile`, `shell`; an unreadable body, or a send inside text another program runs: fed to a
shell, or in an interpreter's code that runs commands). The
options `Send it` and `Don't send`. `Send it` lets that one call through, and for `wb patch send` writes
`$WB_HOME/send-ok.json` (what wb checks under Claude Code: *Sending a patch upstream*); nothing is remembered (a yes to
one pull request is no yes to the next). Anything else, a failed dialog too, denies: `NOT_SENT`, `workbench: not
sent: the user did not approve it in the dialog. Tell them it was not sent; try again only if they ask for it.` (it
once said to show them and ask, and Claude opened a dialog of its own pleading for the yes just refused). A live check
of the gate runs the real gh form with a fake gh on PATH: an `echo` of it is text, never asked about. No `$.state`
atom. A rejected dialog off the terminal also toasts (`askOrNo`, *Surfaces*).

**The roles' dialog** (`routeRefusal`, beside `sendRefusal` in the same hook, #1014; *Roles*). In Bash and Monitor
commands, read as above (`runs`: `simpleCommands`, `bash -c` and `eval` inside; the kernel's `gateOf`: its gates `route`,
`start` and `settings`, and each one's dry-run `args`), each `wb route …` and each
`wb start … --m…` (any abbreviation of `--model`) is a call (`routeCalls`), and each `wb settings set …` (#1287, a
`--settings` call; `settings`' own `--json` before `set` too: the review of #1336); a show (`wb route`, `--json`) and a dry run
change nothing. For each call, one after another (`routeDry`), the mod runs `wb route --dry-run --json <its args>` (a start's as `--start <wb start's
args>`, parsed there by wb start's own parser: the task's name and an abbreviated `--model` as wb takes them; a
Settings row's as `wb settings set <key> <value> --dry-run --json`, `settings.dry_run`: its row's own `wb route` dry
run word for word, a role's selector, API model, thinking or the cap alike (#1336), or nothing gated for a row whose call
isn't a `wb route`), 60 s,
a start's in the directory it runs in (`routeCalls`' `at`: `cd` and `pushd` followed from the session's, with
`gateOf`'s `cd` and its target, as `upstreamAim` reads it; wb start's `--repo` is `.` unless given, and a start after `cd other &&` was judged
local-only, or not, by the session's repo, #1125). A `cd` the mod can't resolve (a word with `$` or a backquote, none,
`-`) and a directory that isn't there (`mkdir x && cd x`) leave the session's: a missing one failed the dry run to
spawn and the call skipped the dialog. A route's runs in the session's (it reads no directory).
A dry run that exits non-zero (wb refuses the change itself), prints nothing gated (a GPU model pin, a GPU `--model`, the Agents switch to GPU)
or can't run lets the call through: wb refuses a gated change under Claude Code without the approval anyway. Else
`consent(<the dry run's change line>, 'Allow', "Don't")`: the terminal's `$.ui.ask`, with the chat's one line while
away, as the send's above. `Allow` writes `$WB_HOME/route-ok.json` (`{...approval, at}`, the dry run's `approval`: `{argv,
change}` or `{start: {task, model}, change}`) and lets the call through; anything else denies (`NOT_CHANGED`:
`workbench: not changed: the user did not approve it in the dialog. Tell them it was not changed; ask again only if
they ask for it.`; a rejected dialog off the terminal toasts too, `askOrNo`). Refused without asking (`ROUTE_OWN`, `run wb route (or wb start --model) as a command of its own`):
a gated call beside another call in one line (calls nothing gates pass together: two ungated Settings rows in one
Bash call were refused before any dry run, the review of #1287), and one inside text another program runs: a call a
shell is fed (a `wb settings set` row too, gated or not: it isn't dry-run), or one in an interpreter's code that runs
commands (`ROUTE_TEXT`, `spawns`); a heredoc that only says `wb route cap 9` or `wb settings set cap 9` is no call
(#1364). The file tools
(`EDIT_FIELDS`: the kernel's `editTools`, Claude Code's rows) on routes.json (`routesPath`: `WB_ROUTES`, else `~/.config/workbench/routes.json`, by real path too) or
`$WB_HOME/route-ok.json` are denied (`routesFileRefusal`, `ROUTES_EDIT`), and so is a command that writes
`$WB_HOME/route-ok.json` (`writesTo`, `ROUTE_OK_OWN`; what a command writes is `gateOf`'s `writes`): a redirect onto it, `tee`, `cp`/`mv`/`install`/`ln`/`rsync`
onto it or into its directory under its name, `dd of=`, a shell's fed commands too (`cd` and `pushd` followed; the
path as written, through `~`, `$HOME` or `$WB_HOME`), or an interpreter's code with a write call (`WRITES_CODE`: Python's
`open(…, 'w')`, its path built inside too, `os.path.join(…)`, `write_text`, Node's `writeFileSync`, …) and the file in a
string that is a path (quotes; backquotes only in JavaScript: in Python's text they are Markdown's), with `WB_HOME` or the
state directory in the code or the call run there. A mention is never a write: a `gh issue create` whose heredoc named
the file was refused as writing it (2026-11-24, #1364), and a `grep` for the name passes; a word the mod can't resolve (another variable, a
glob) lets the call through. A speed bump, not a wall: a command that builds the path gets past it (*Roles*, the gate).

**The roles in the conversation.** `WbSaid.routes` (the `said-3` atom) is the roles' summary as the mod reads
routes.json (`readRoutes`, `routesSummary`, which says what `routes.summary` says: Couplings) and the cap (`. Day cap
$N`: in what is compared, so a cap changed alone is a row too; it once wasn't, 2026-11-23; an OpenRouter role's
`order` as `, backends a, b` after its API model, for the same reason, #1126), '' while every role is
the default and no cap is set (nothing to tell), `routes.json can't be read (wb route says why)` for a file wb wouldn't read
(`routesValid`); read in `wanted` while delegating or with a task open. `unsaid` pushes `[workbench] The roles changed:
<summary>. <ROUTES_RULE>` whenever it differs from what was said (the first time `ROUTES_NOTE`), so any change, the
dialog's, the web app's, a terminal's or a hand edit, reaches the conversation as one row; when the newest stamp a role
records (`by`/`ts`, `gpu_by`/`gpu_ts`) is `web`, the summary ends `(the user, on the web app)` (`readRoutes`' `web`,
#1283). `prompt.context` adds the
`workbench-routes` block (delegating, or a task open, as `wanted` reads) once any role has an API model (a GPU pin alone
adds none): `Roles (the user's, wb route): <summary>. Day cap $5. Never pass --model for an API model or change a role
without the user's yes (the mod asks them in a dialog); recommend only.` (`ROUTES_RULE`; `No day cap yet.` without one).
Roles are settings, and Claude never changes one unasked (the owner's locked rule, 2026-11-24): #1322 tried `Run it when
it is the right call`, and it went back. The `/workbench` skill's text carries it the same way (`unsaid`).

**Tests** (`register.test.tsx`: an in-memory filesystem, a fake `wb events`; `statHeld`, a path
whose stat comes back late; `SURFACES`, the four the kit mounts on: the empty pane, the Tasks tab's
review, stuck and failed rows, Stats, Settings, both consent dialogs on each, a wake after
`session.attach` on desktop and vscode, the unanswered-dialog toast for a desktop surface that
attaches after a surfaceless start, and `findWb`, #1200). Not covered: check-in
wakes, the one-hour cutoff, scrolling, `WB_COMPACT_AT`.

**Troubleshooting.** With `wb` missing from Claude Code's PATH (and no `~/.local/bin/wb`, `findWb`)
or failing, the mod toasts once (`can't run \`wb events\``, `wb status failed`) and runs on from the
task files: set `WB_BIN`, which moves only the mod's calls (Claude's Bash still needs `wb` on PATH);
`wb doctor` says which wb the mod runs (`the mod runs …`, `cli.mod_wb`). `claude plugin validate
mod` lists hooks, calls and env reads; `claude --debug` shows hook errors.

## The kernel

The decisions both hosts (the Claude Code mod; the OpenCode plugin, #1296) must make the same way
are written once in PureScript under `kernel/src` and compiled into one committed ES module,
`mod/hooks/kernel.js` (#1325, its boundary #1356). `kernel/BOUNDARY.md` is the contract: the
entry test, `## Exports` (each export's module, decision, what it `replaces`, its consumers), the
rulings (one gate classifier over a parsed command comes in, by the owner's ruling of 2026-11-25,
with the parsing left to each host, and so do the coding gate's rules; wording, formatting and parsing stay in TypeScript; effects,
rendering, locale and telemetry never go in), `## Budget` (16 exports, 65,536 bytes, 1,200 source lines and 350 per
module with Tables aside, `core.ts` 250 lines), the wire types (`Number`, `String`, `Boolean`,
`Array`, closed records; every field present, `-1` and `""` for none, an unknown tag the safe
answer), the denied imports and the move protocol. Today it holds `tables`, which `register.tsx`
(`ACTIVE`, `NEEDS`, `PARKS`, `CLOSED`, `NO_ANSWER`, `CHAT_STALE_MS`, `WAKE_OPENING`) and `tasks.ts` (`CLOSED`)
read through `core.ts`, their hand copies deleted; `phaseOf` and `openCounts` (#1325's M1: `register.tsx`'s
`RUNNING`/`waitsOnClaude` and `tasks.ts`'s `WORKING`/`COUNTED` deleted); `owns` and `awayNow` (M2:
`register.tsx`'s `parts`, `within`, `spotOf`, `near`, `ranHere` and `AWAY_MS` deleted, its `mine`,
`claim` and `awayNow` adapters gathering the facts); `noticesDue`, `noticePlan` and `rewakePlan`
(M3 and M4: `deliver`'s and `rewake`'s decisions, `REWAKE_MAX_MS` deleted; the host keeps the reads,
`wb ack`, the submits and the words); and by the owner's ruling (2026-11-25) the mode machine,
`tellPlan`, `modesPlan` and `compactPlan` (`unsaid`'s and `prompt.context`'s choice of what to
say, `keepMode`'s record, the boundary compaction: `COMPACT_AT` and `MODES_KEEP_MS` deleted; the
words, `KEEP_ON_COMPACT` among them, and `firstTask`, a parse, stay in the host). `taskParts`
stays out (rendering). The gate classifier `gateOf`, which every Bash and Monitor gate in
`register.tsx` reads (`delegates`, `runs`, `upstreamAim`, `sendQuestion`, `routeCalls`,
`writesTo`), its hand copies deleted (#1325, after #1364); and the coding gate's rules,
`codingGate` and `editTools` (`codingRefusal`, `callRows`). What #1325 planned and the entry test
and the rulings leave out (2026-11-26): the keywords (reading a prompt is parsing: `mod/hooks/keywords.ts`,
one TypeScript module both hosts import, *Deep workflows*); the weekly check's offer (scout timing is wb's,
`cli.scout_offer_due`, which `wb scout --if-due` runs for the OpenCode plugin; the mod's `scoutIfDue` checks
the same two times in scout.json on its quiet polls, a coupling); the web chat's asks (#1350 to #1352 removed
most; what is left matches each host's own delivery); and the chat API's shapes (types, not decisions: #1323's
one shared types module).

- **The membrane**: `mod/hooks/core.ts`, the one importer of `./kernel.js` (with its generated
  `kernel.d.ts`), exports `kernel` (every export by name, untyped, for the goldens: only tests,
  `*.test.*`, and `golden/` import it), the sets `ACTIVE`, `NEEDS`, `PARKS`, `CLOSED`, `NO_ANSWER`,
  `CHAT_STALE_MS`, `WAKE_OPENING`, and `phaseOf`, `openCounts(tasks)`, `owns(facts)`,
  `awayNow(webAt, now, tasks)`, `noticesDue(rows, startedAt, now)`, `noticePlan(facts)`,
  `rewakePlan(facts)`, `tellPlan(facts)`, `modesPlan(modes, ids, now, on)`, `compactPlan(facts)`,
  `gateOf(words, writes = [])` (its `gate` typed `GateName`), `codingGate` (its `verdict` typed) and
  `editFields(host)` (`editTools`' rows for `claude-code` or `opencode`, as a tool-to-field map),
  typed from `kernel.d.ts`. It maps (a phase to a string, a mark to a boolean) and decides nothing.
- **`Kernel.Tables`** (`kernel/src/Kernel/Tables.purs`) is generated by `scripts/kernel.py tables`
  from wb's Python: `sorted()` of `store.ACTIVE`, `NEEDS_CLAUDE`, `PARKS`, `CLOSED`, `WORKING` and
  `STOPPED`, `store.OPEN_ORDER` in its own order (`openOrder`),
  `ask_mcp.NO_ANSWER`'s first sentence, `chat.LISTENING_FOR * 1000`, `spend.WAKE_OPENING` (`[workbench]
  Task`, from which `spend.WAKE` is built). Python stays the source.
- **`phaseOf({phase, parked})`** → `{active, running, working, needsClaude, waits, stopped, done,
  closed}`: `running` is active and not needing Claude (the status line's, `queued` included),
  `working` a round under way (`store.WORKING`: the pane's clock, context bar and estimate),
  `waits` needs Claude and isn't parked, a mark counting only in `PARKS` (`store.parked`, #698),
  `stopped` stuck or failed (`store.STOPPED`), `done` a review or closed; a phase no table names is
  none of them.
- **`openCounts({tasks})`** → `{counts: [{phase, n, waiting, active, stopped}], done}`: a row for
  each open phase that has a task, in `store.OPEN_ORDER`, `waiting` those not parked; `done` the
  tasks done. The pane's group header (`tasks.ts`: `2 running · 1 stuck`, `1/3 done`) and the
  status line (`register.tsx`'s `taskParts`: `<N> awaiting review`, `<N> stuck`) draw from it.
- **`owns({session, ids, driver, host, gone, cwd, repo, subdir, here, home, fold})`** → `{mine,
  claims}`: whose task it is (*Waking Claude, exactly once*), `claims` the same with its session gone (what
  `claim` may `wb adopt`). The host gathers the facts (the mod: `mem.ids`, `mem.deadPids`, its
  directory, `mem.fold`, the task's driver as `store.driver_of` names it); paths compare by whole
  components, lower case under `fold`. Its twin is `cli._scope` (`kernel.owns_twin` patches
  `_owner_gone`, `store.folds_case`, `Path.home`), which stays the lock.
- **`noticesDue({rows, startedAt, now})`** → `{due: [{task, picks}], noticed: [{task, ts}]}`: from
  notify.jsonl's rows (`{task, kind, ts, tasks}`), per task in the order they first come due its
  every question and its newest notice, none older than an hour before the later of the load's
  start and now (`picks`: row indices); `noticed`, each task's newest notice however old, a
  batch's for each task it names (`mem.noticed`, rewake's mark).
- **`noticePlan({kind, hasId, phase, questionOpen, ts, acked, own, wake, busy, toasted, heldAsk})`**
  → `{current, toast, act}`: still true (a check-in while running, queued included; a question
  while asking and, with an id, still open; else the phase its kind names), toasted once, and
  `act`: `skip` (acked), `none` (another session's, or wakes off: the toast only), `steer` (a
  question into the busy turn), `hold` (anything else true while busy), `wake`, `ack` (no longer
  true), `missed` (a held question whose task is open: said if it timed out, #542).
- **`rewakePlan({phase, parked, mine, updatedAt, now, busy, wake, dropped, acked, seen, marked})`**
  → `{recent, candidate, due, kind}`: `recent` this session's waiting on Claude within 12 h (the
  weekly jobs' gate too); `candidate` idle, wakes on, a minute or more since it changed and since a
  dropped wake; `due` a candidate whose `acked` is below its newest notice (`seen` this load, -1
  none; the task's `noticed`, 0 none), or with none below `updated_at`; `kind` a question while it
  asks, else the phase. The host reads `acked` and `noticed` only for a candidate.
- **`tellPlan({first, want, was, known, any, delegating, away})`** → `{say, said}`: what to tell a
  conversation of the rules (`Said`: `{notes, wakeOff, coding, routes, workflows}`). `first` (its
  first message, again after a compaction or /clear): the blocks, in order `mode` (delegating),
  `coding` (not `decide`), `notes`, `workflows` (on), `away`, `wakeOff`, `routes`, leaving out what
  /workbench's message said (`was`, when `known`, #540), and `said` is `want`. Midway: `notes`,
  `wakeOff`, `coding`, `routes` (`routesChanged` once a summary was said), `workflows`, the last
  three only while delegating or with a task open (`any`); notes and the wake-off note once.
- **`modesPlan({modes, ids, now, on})`** → `{kept, modes}`: `$.store`'s `modes` (`[{id, at}]`):
  whether one of this process's ids is in the mode (#689), and the record to write: none 30 days
  old, the process's own dropped, then, turning it on, each id at `now`.
- **`compactPlan({on, was, open, boundary, busy, waiting, percentSet, percent, tokens, window,
  autoCompact, threshold})`** → `{boundary, check, compact}`: a task boundary (one of `was`, the
  session's open tasks at the last look, not in `open`; only in the mode) marked, `check` (read
  the usage now: idle, none waiting on Claude; the mark then cleared), `compact` (the usage read:
  `tokens` at `percent`, `WB_COMPACT_AT`, or half, of the engine's auto-compact `threshold` when
  `autoCompact`, else of `window`; 0 never).
- **`awayNow({webAt, now, tasks})`** → whether the user is away: the web chat used within six hours
  (`webAt` ms, 0 for none), or one of the session's tasks (`mine`) active or waiting on Claude
  unparked since (#110, #1402).
- **`gateOf({words, writes})`** (`Kernel.Gate`): one simple command, as the host's parser read it
  (its words, quotes undone; `writes`, the files its redirects write), → `{at, word, gate, delegates,
  args, dirs, writes, send}`. `at`: the command's own word, past `VAR=x`, the reserved words (`if`,
  `then`, `elif`, `else`, `while`, `until`, `do`, `!`, `{`) and the wrappers with their valued
  options (`env`, `time`, `nohup`, `exec`, `command`, `timeout` and its duration, `nice`, `ionice`,
  `stdbuf`, `sudo`, `doas`, `xargs`); `word`: its name lowercased. `gate`, closed: `cd` (cd or pushd;
  `args`, its target, none for home), `send` (wb patch send; `send`: `slug`, `title`/`titled`,
  `bodyFile`/`filed`, `draft`, `anyway`, and `lack`: `slug`, `title`, `bodyFile`, `shell` or ""),
  `outward` (the gh forms that write, `gh api` with a method other than GET or HEAD or with fields,
  `git push`; `dirs`, git's `-C`), `route`, `start` (with a `--m…`), `settings` (`wb settings set`),
  each with `args` as `wb route --dry-run --json` takes them, or "". `wb` is `wb`, a path to it, or
  Python running `…/wb` or `-m workbench…`. `delegates`: the word as written is `wb` or ends in
  `/wb`, then `start`, `next`, `feedback`, `steer`, `answer` or `resume`. `writes`: the redirects',
  tee's, dd's `of=`, a copy's (`cp`, `mv`, `install`, `ln`, `rsync`) last operand or `-t` directory
  with `names`, its sources. Only words count (#1364): a heredoc's body, a here-string and an
  interpreter's code never arrive as words; reading that code (`spawns`, `OUTWARD_TEXT`,
  `ROUTE_TEXT`, `WRITES_CODE`) is text, and stays in the host, with the parsing, the paths and
  the dialogs. Ported with a seeded parity run against the old hand copies (120,324 cases: every
  command in `register.test.tsx` as the old parser read it, 50,000 seeded word lists, 50,000 more
  from command heads; no disagreement); it also no longer crashes on, or takes for a wrapper, a
  word naming a property of every JavaScript object (`gh constructor`, `toString git push`).
- **`codingGate({mode, allowed})`** (`Kernel.Coding`): the user's `wb coding` mode and the task's
  allowances (`used`, `when`, `started`, each a Boolean) → `{verdict, open}`: `pass` (`decide`, a
  mode wb doesn't know, or an allowance not handed back), `start` (pass, and the host stamps
  `started` on allowance `open`, a one-task exception's first edit, #94), `ask`, `refuse`; `open`,
  the first allowance not handed back, `-1` for none. **`editTools`**: each host's file tools and
  the field naming the file (Claude Code's `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `Write` `file_path` and
  `NotebookEdit` `notebook_path`; OpenCode 2.4.1's `edit` and `write`, `path`).
- **`scripts/kernel.py`** (standard library, 3.11): `fetch` downloads `kernel/toolchain.json`'s
  pins for this platform (Linux or macOS, x64 or arm64): purs 0.15.16 from its GitHub release
  (`sha256`), esbuild 0.28.2 from npm (`sha512`), each archive's one member checked against
  `bin_sha256`, and `kernel/spago.lock`'s packages from `packages.registry.purescript.org`
  (registry 80.2.0, each tarball against its lock `integrity`; unpacked member by member, regular
  files under `<name>-<version>/` only, a link or a path escape refused by name). They go to
  `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/workbench/kernel/<pin>/` (`<pin>`: a digest of both pin files; `--into
  DIR` moves it), shared by every worktree, every later run checking them again offline.
  `build` runs `tables`, copies `kernel/src` and the packages into a temp directory, runs `purs
  compile -g js,docs,corefn -o output` there (always `output`: esbuild writes the path into the
  bundle), lints the corefn, bundles `output/Kernel.Main/index.js` with the pinned esbuild flags
  (`--bundle --format=esm --charset=utf8`), writes `kernel.d.ts` from purs's `docs.json` (a type
  that isn't wire refuses the build, `NotWire`; a decision takes one record) and both files
  atomically, each with the banner `// Generated by scripts/kernel.py from kernel/src: do not
  edit; … inputs sha256:<hex> body sha256:<hex> purs <v> esbuild <v>` (the inputs: the sorted
  `kernel/src/**/*.purs`, `toolchain.json`, `spago.lock`). `lint`: no `foreign import`, no denied
  import (`Effect*`, `Control.Monad.ST*`, `Data.Array.ST*`, `Data.Array.Partial`, `Unsafe.*`,
  `Partial.Unsafe`, `Record.Unsafe`, `Debug.*`), no `localeCompare`, in the source (read whole, so an
  `import` whose module name is on the next line counts, and again with its comments blanked, `kernel.uncommented`,
  so `import {- -} Effect.Unsafe` counts too) and in the corefn of every module compiled from
  `kernel/src` or `kernel/test`, whatever it is named. A failed `purs compile` shows purs's first error (its stdout).
  `props`: `kernel/test/Props.purs` (module `Props`, under the same lint, outside the digest and the
  budget) compiled with `kernel/src` in a temp directory, bundled to `test/props.js` beside a copy
  of `kernel/test/props.test.ts`, and run under Bun (`bun test`, else `BUN_BE_BUN=1 opencode test`;
  neither: refused by name, never skipped): a Park-Miller generator (Schrage's method, Int only),
  seeds `[20261124, 1, 2]`, 1,000 cases each, within 10 s, holding that closed and active share no
  phase, that active and needsClaude share only `asking`, that a parked mark counts only in phases
  needing Claude, that `openOrder` names every open phase once, that `phaseOf` round-trips (each
  flag says which of wb's sets the phase is in; a phase none names, a near miss or a stranger, is
  none of them), that `openCounts` tallies what each task's `phaseOf` says, that `owns` gives a
  session its own id's tasks, never a live session's nor another driver's by directory, nothing in
  `~` or `/` by directory but where `wb start` ran, `/x/ab` never inside `/x/a`, that `awayNow`
  holds for six hours, then while one of the session's tasks is open, that `noticesDue` picks only
  a task's own rows within the hour, in order, its questions and one newest notice, `noticed` never
  behind a notice, that `noticePlan` delivers a notice at most once while it is true (acked: skipped,
  untoasted; only a true one of this session's with wakes on wakes or steers; none mid-turn but a
  question steered), that `rewakePlan` is due only for a candidate, never busy, too soon, past
  12 h or twice, that `tellPlan` is idempotent (told again what it was told, it says nothing and
  the record stands; notes and the wake-off note, once said, stay said; out of the mode with
  nothing open no other rule moves), that `modesPlan` keeps nothing 30 days old and this process's
  ids exactly when on, and that `compactPlan` never checks out of the mode, busy or with a task
  waiting, nor compacts unchecked or off. A failure names its seed and case.
  `check`: the offline checks below, two builds byte-equal to each other and to the commit, the props.
  `relock`: spago 1.0.4 from npm (no install scripts) into the cache re-locks `spago.lock` from
  `spago.yaml` in a scratch copy; only a new package needs it, and npm.
- **Without the toolchain**, `tests/test_kernel.py` (`kernel.offline_errors`) holds the rest: the
  lint, Tables against the Python, the banners' digests (a hand edit, a stale build), the bundle
  free of `import(`, `require(`, `process.`, `globalThis`, clocks, `Math.random`, `console.`,
  timers, `Intl.`, locale calls, `eval(`, `new Function`, `fetch(`, `Bun.`, `Deno.`; one set of
  exports across BOUNDARY.md, the bundle, the d.ts and the goldens; one importer across `mod/`,
  `opencode-plugin/` and `workbench/chat_static/` (every `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.mts`, `.cts`,
  `.cjs` and `.jsx`, `import`, `from` and `require(`); `core.ts`'s untyped `kernel` record taken
  only by tests and goldens (`kernel.core_record_importers`); no `replaces` name still defined; no phase
  literal in `opencode-plugin/`, and no phase set in `mod/hooks` outside its tests and goldens (two
  phases on a line or in one bracketed list: `kernel.phase_literals`; one phase alone is its own
  words or glyph); the budgets. So a change to a value Tables copies fails the
  suite until `python3 scripts/kernel.py build` (the toolchain once, with the network).
- **The goldens** (`mod/hooks/golden/`): one file per module, `export default {module, cases}
  satisfies Golden`, each case `{fn, in, out, why, twin?}` (`in: null`: a value export), listed in
  `golden/index.ts`'s `GOLDENS`; `golden/run.ts`'s `goldenFailures(kernel, GOLDENS)` compares
  canonical JSON and imports nothing, so both hosts run it: `mod/hooks/kernel.test.ts` under
  `claude plugin test mod`, `opencode-plugin/test/kernel.test.ts` under `BUN_BE_BUN=1 opencode
  test opencode-plugin/test` (OpenCode's own Bun; 2.3.0 and 2.4.1 honour it). A case's `twin` names
  the Python that judges the same (`kernel.<name>`: `scripts/kernel.py`'s; `<mod>.<name>`:
  workbench's): `tests/test_kernel.py`'s `Twins` reads the goldens through Bun and calls each twin
  with the case's `in` as keyword arguments (none for a value export), so the goldens and wb agree;
  `tables`' twin is `kernel.tables_values`, `owns`' `kernel.owns_twin` (`cli._scope` on one task). Without Bun (neither `bun` nor `opencode`) Twins skips.
- **`wb patch`**: `.gitattributes` marks `kernel.js` `-merge -diff`, `kernel.d.ts` and
  `Tables.purs` `-merge`, all `linguist-generated`: a rebase that meets one stops with `wb
  update`'s message; take either side, then `build`. `wb patch upstream` names `python3
  scripts/kernel.py check` among a patch's tests when it changes `kernel/`, with the mod's and the
  OpenCode plugin's, which both load the bundle (`patches.SUITES`, #1328).
- **CI**: `check.yml`'s `kernel` job (fetch, `check` with its props) and `opencode-plugin` job (the
  Bun goldens, #1328) are part of the required `check`; the first shard of `nightly.yml`'s `macos` runs `check` too (the same bundle bytes
  on macOS), and `opencode.yml` the Bun goldens on the newest OpenCode (`BUN_BE_BUN` is undocumented).

## Workbench in OpenCode

Two paths, one backend (#1296, 2.2). **Claude Code with Claude's Workbench**: the mod and the
`/workbench` skill, exactly as before 2.2; Claude drives. **OpenCode alone**: `/workbench` in
OpenCode's TUI, and the driver (the model with the final say: review, accept, the bar) is whatever
the session runs on, picked in OpenCode's own `/models`, a GPU model, an API model or Claude through
OpenCode's `claude-agent` provider. Everything below the driver is one copy: `wb`, the runner, the
lanes, the keyhole, routes.json and the roles, the web app, results.jsonl, the skill library. The
supported hosts are the two CLIs (the owner, locked 2026-11-25): OpenCode's TUI and Claude Code's;
OpenCode Desktop, `opencode web` and IDE surfaces are neither built for nor tested, and whatever of
the plugin works there is incidental. How the plugin is built: *The OpenCode plugin*; its rule is the
host-shape decision (https://github.com/a-schaefers/workbench/issues/1296#issuecomment-7158435888):
the same outcomes, OpenCode-native, wb the system of record, the kernel pure decisions only, and
Claude Code's path unchanged by a byte (its tests unedited, SKILL.md its own copy).

**Installing.** One `plugins` entry, either way (a second is a duplicate `wb doctor` names): `opencode plugin add
'github:a-schaefers/workbench#main'` (`ocplugin.ADD`, OpenCode's Git install: the plugin with the wb
it brings, in OpenCode's package cache, which OpenCode updates and replaces: `wb update` leaves it to
OpenCode, `wb setup` and `wb patch` refuse there), or a clone's `bin/wb setup --opencode` (the `~/.local/bin/wb`
link and the plugins entry, a copy of the clone's committed `opencode-plugin/` that `wb update`
refreshes; never Claude Code's skill link, which OpenCode would list too). `wb doctor` names each
install and the wb it runs; on the OpenCode path alone a missing Claude Code item is a `--` line, never BAD. Both
drivers on one machine: *Both drivers on one machine*.

**Each feature and its counterpart.** The same outcome on both, built from each host's own parts:

| Claude Code (the mod, the skill) | OpenCode (the plugin) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `/workbench [request]`: the skill, the mode on, the pane | `/workbench [request]`, a server command: the driver pin applied, the session switched to the Workbench agent, whose prompt is the procedure; the panel opens on that switch, and as a TUI comes to a session already on it (`opencode -s`, a new TUI); run again in a session already on it, it publishes no switch and opens nothing (the footer's `⚒ wb` or the palette does) | `pane.ts`, `agent.ts`, *The driver* |
| `/workbench-quit`, `/workbench-quit-and-hand-back-claude`, `/workbench-models`, `/workbench-update` | `/workbench-quit`, `/workbench-quit-and-hand-back` (switching to Build ends the mode and closes the panel), `/workbench-models`, `/workbench-update` | `commands.ts` |
| SKILL.md and `reference/`, read through the skill link | the same files rendered for OpenCode when the plugin starts (`skill.ts`): the agent's prompt, the `workbench` skill and one `workbench-<name>` skill per reference file, Claude Code's lines replaced by OpenCode's facts | `skill.ts`, `agent.ts` |
| `wb` recipes typed in Bash | typed tools in the `workbench` namespace (`workbench_start`, `_status`, `_diff`, `_feedback`, `_accept`, `_discard`, `_wait`), the shell for the rest | `tools.ts` |
| The pane "Claude's Workbench": Tasks, the modeline, the splash and the apprentice, the `⚒ wb ·` status line, the minimized strip | the panel "Workbench" (beside the session at 108 columns or more, fullscreen narrower), the sidebar section, the footer item; one Tasks view (`mod/hooks/tasks.ts`) and one animation for both | `pane.tsx`, `pane-view.ts`, `spans.ts`, `splash.tsx` |
| Wakes: a `[workbench] Task …` prompt, exactly once (`wb events`, `wb ack`) | `session.synthetic` from the server part's one `wb events`, the same text and ack; an agent's question steers into a running turn | `notices.ts`, *Notices on OpenCode* |
| The context blocks, `KEEP_ON_COMPACT`, compaction at a task boundary | session instruction entries (the `context` hook as fallback), the `compaction` hook | `upkeep.ts` |
| The consent dialog: an API role, an API `--model` start, a role's Settings row, `wb patch send` | a session form asked by the gated tool (`workbench_route`, `workbench_start`, `workbench_settings_set`, `workbench_patch_send`); the shell path to them denied on the permission hook; no TUI, no form: refused | `consent.ts`, `gates.ts` |
| The consent dialog on every other send upstream: a gh write, a `git push`, a GitHub MCP tool's write | the same form, asked from `execute.before` over the line as the mod reads it (`mod/hooks/shell.ts`, one copy for both); no TUI, no form: refused | `upstream.ts` |
| The coding gate (`wb coding`), routes.json and approval-file edits refused, `local_only` | the same rules on the permission hook and `execute.before` | `consent.ts` |
| Whose task: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_PID`, `claude-sessions/` | `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` and the server's heartbeat (`drivers/`), task.json `driver` | *The OpenCode driver: whose task it is* |
| The driver's own edits in `claude-calls/` | `execute.after` writes the same rows | `calls.ts` |
| The driver is Claude Code (fixed) | `/models`, a standing pin (`wb route driver`, the web app's `driver` row), the once-only notes; a GPU driver held beside the agents | *The driver*, *A local driver on the GPU* |
| The web chat: listener, turns, replies, the waiting line | the same over `session.prompt`/`synthetic` and `workbench_chat_reply` | `chat.ts`, *The web chat on OpenCode* |
| The weekly model check, the update check, settings help turns, `wb optimize --if-due` | the same due rules in wb, toasted from the idle hook | `jobs.ts`, *Background jobs on OpenCode* |
| `deepcode`, `deepmode` | the same keywords, the same `wb run` flows | `deep.ts`, *Deep workflows* |
| `wb patch` and its procedure | the same commands; the procedure in OpenCode's facts (below) | *Local patches*, `skill.ts` |

**What differs, and why.**
- **The driver is the user's choice**, and wb can't make a weak model hold the bar, so it says so
  once, never as a refusal (*The driver*'s notes: the driver is the agent's own model; an API driver
  in a `local_only` repo, whose code reaches the API through the driver).
- **A command that asks the user something** (sudo's password, gh's login): Claude Code's `!`
  runs it in the user's terminal; OpenCode's `!` (shell mode, typed at the prompt's start) runs it
  with no terminal (2.4.1's process-daemon: a pipe, stdin closed, a session of its own), so nothing
  can ask. wb's hints and the rendered procedure name OpenCode's terminal pane (`terminal.toggle`,
  ctrl+x t by default: a real terminal, its wb the user's, no `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`) or a terminal
  of the user's own instead (`patches.PANE_OR_TERMINAL`, `skill.ts`'s, #1321's finding 17). Seen
  live on 2.4.1 (2026-11-26): `tty` under `!` says `not a tty`, in the pane `/dev/pts/<n>`, and
  neither sets `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (a wb typed in either is the user's, `store.caller_kind`'s
  `terminal`; only the driver's own shell tool sets it).
- **Sends upstream**: the mod's dialog and the plugin's form hold the same sends (a gh write, a
  `git push`, a GitHub MCP tool's write, `wb patch send`), read and aimed by one copy
  (`mod/hooks/shell.ts`, #1296's row 14); on OpenCode `wb patch send` itself goes only through
  `workbench_patch_send` (the shell's is refused with that tool), whose form shows its title and
  body, and away on the web chat the form waits for the user, as the mod's dialog does.
- **A patch to the plugin**: OpenCode's Git install can't keep one (`wb patch` refuses there and
  names the clone to make); with a clone's wb, the plugin's own code stays the Git install's while
  OpenCode's `plugins` entry names it, so a patch under `opencode-plugin/` needs that entry swapped
  for the clone's (*Local patches*; #1321, finding 7).
- **Claude Code only**: `wb schedule`'s fires (Claude Code headless, `claude -p`), `ultracode` (a
  Claude Code keyword), `/reload-plugins` (OpenCode reloads a plugin by itself), the marketplace
  rescue (met on OpenCode only with Claude Code installed too), and the savings score's Claude fit:
  no cost machinery is built for a non-Claude driver (#1318, closed by the owner); Stats shows what
  OpenCode reports.
- **Claude's own files**: an OpenCode driver reads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when the user has no
  OpenCode `AGENTS.md`, unless the user sets OpenCode's `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT`:
  OpenCode's behaviour in the user's own session (#1296 row 19), while agents never read it
  (*What the agent knows*).

## The OpenCode plugin

Workbench inside OpenCode (#1296, 2.2) is an OpenCode plugin, `opencode-plugin/`, beside `mod/`:
one package whose parts OpenCode loads from one `plugins` entry (OpenCode 2.4.1's docs,
`build/plugins/index.mdx` *Parts* and *Load*; read from its source, `anomalyco/opencode` v2.4.1).
Its driver side is built from OpenCode's own parts (the host-shape decision,
https://github.com/a-schaefers/workbench/issues/1296#issuecomment-7158435888); the agents stay one
laned `opencode run --standalone` per round from the runner. The skeleton (#1311), the web chat
(#1319, `chat.ts`: *The web chat on OpenCode*, below), the Workbench agent and its skills (#1335,
`skill.ts`, `agent.ts`, below), the driver part (#1316), the notices and the background jobs (#1313,
#1334, `notices.ts`, `jobs.ts`: *Notices on OpenCode*, below), the conversation's upkeep and the
user's commands (#1315, `upkeep.ts`, `commands.ts`, below), the consent gates and the driver's call
rows (#1314, #1331: `consent.ts`, `calls.ts` below), the procedure's typed wb tools (#1335, `tools.ts`
below), the pane (#1312, #1332: `/workbench`, the
panel, the sidebar section and the footer item, `pane.ts`, `pane-view.ts`, `pane.tsx`), and the
agents' sessions as the lead's child sessions (#1331: `children.ts`, `children-tui.ts`, below). The chat runs `wb chat` commands only, as the session it acts for
(`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`), its claim in the session's directory; the driver part's (#1316) take no
scope from the cwd (`wb driver beat`, `wb driver --session`, `wb route driver --json`); the
commands, the upkeep (#1315) and the consent tools (#1314) run a task's commands (`wb stop --all`, `wb takeover --all`, `wb
status`) as the session in its own directory (`session.get`'s `location.directory`), where wb takes a
session's scope from (`cli._caller` reads the cwd beside `store.opencode_session`; the heartbeat's
session `dir` is the other source, which the plugin's beats carry since #1316: #1309's review).

- **The package**, in two manifests of one name, `opencode-workbench` (`ocplugin.PACKAGE`),
  `private`, its version unused (a Git install reports its commit), each `exports` `.` and
  `./server` → `server.ts`, `./tui` → `tui.ts`, `./rpc` → `rpc.ts`, the names OpenCode's
  `Host.resolve` asks for (`plugin/src/host.ts`). The repository's root `package.json` is what
  OpenCode's Git install fetches: its `exports` point into `opencode-plugin/`, its `files` bring
  `bin/`, `workbench/`, `agent/`, `skill/`, `opencode-plugin/*.ts`, `opencode-plugin/*.tsx`, the
  Claude Code mod's `mod/hooks/splash.ts` and `mod/hooks/apprentice.ts` (which `spans.ts` imports
  as `../mod/hooks/…`: one animation for both hosts, #1333), the kernel's membrane
  `mod/hooks/core.ts` and the `kernel.js` it imports (which `upkeep.ts`, the notices and the panel
  import, #1315, #1313, #1312; not `kernel.d.ts`, types only), `mod/hooks/tasks.ts` and
  `mod/hooks/modeline.ts` (the panel's: one Tasks view for both hosts, #1312), `mod/hooks/keywords.ts` (`deep.ts`'s,
  #1278), `mod/hooks/waiting.ts` (`chat.ts`'s, #1355), `mod/hooks/story.ts` (`chat.ts`'s and `skill.ts`'s, #1355), `mod/hooks/flows.ts` (`flows.ts`'s, #1295), `mod/hooks/shell.ts` (`upstream.ts`'s, #1296) and `LICENSE` (the plugin and
  the wb it runs; no `opencode-plugin/test`), and `bin` names `bin/wb` (so Arborist keeps it
  executable); no `type` field, so nothing else in the repository changes how it loads. Each
  `mod/` entry is a file the plugin imports, itself or through another mod file, and each file a
  plugin module imports from beside it, and each such mod file in turn, is in `files` (a type-only
  import is erased before it runs and needs none) (`Setup`'s
  `test_every_file_the_opencode_plugin_imports_from_beside_it_comes_with_each_install`).
  Its `files` also bring `mod/hooks/core.ts` and `mod/hooks/kernel.js` (the kernel the gates
  classify commands with, `consent.ts`'s dynamic import of the mod's core, #1314).
  `opencode-plugin/package.json` (`type: module`, `files` the parts and their modules:
  `server.ts`, `tui.ts`, `rpc.ts`, `wb.ts`, `chat.ts`, `driver.ts`, `skill.ts`, `agent.ts`, `notices.ts`,
  `notices-tui.ts`, `jobs.ts`, `spans.ts`, `splash.tsx`, `upkeep.ts`, `commands.ts`, `deep.ts`, `flows.ts`, `consent.ts`, `consent-tui.ts`, `tools.ts`, `gates.ts`, `upstream.ts`, `words.ts`, `calls.ts`,
  `pane.ts`, `pane-view.ts`, `pane.tsx`, `children.ts`, `children-tui.ts`) is the one a clone's
  entry loads (`wb setup --opencode`'s `opencode-plugin/` directory). Each part is TypeScript, run
  as it is by OpenCode's Bun, a package's in `node_modules` too.
  - `server.ts`: `{id: "workbench", setup}` (OpenCode's check is that shape alone,
    `core/src/plugin/module.ts` `Module`). Setup registers the RPC's `status` handler, sets up
    the web chat (`chat.ts`'s `chat(ctx)`), the Workbench agent and its skills (`agent.ts`'s
    `registerAgent`; no `skill/` to read, none, the rest stands), starts the driver part
    (`startDriver`), the consent gates (`consent(ctx)`), the procedure's tools (`tools(ctx)`) and the call rows (`calls(ctx)`), and the notices (`notices.ts`'s `notices(ctx)`, which runs the background jobs
    too), sets up the upkeep (`upkeep`) and the commands (`registerCommands`), each
    skipped on a server without its API, starts the panel's part (`startPane`: its RPC and
    `/workbench`) and the child sessions' RPC (`startChildren`); each part's cleanup joins `stops`, and setup returns one cleanup that runs
    them all, newest first, one that throws not stopping the rest, at its end, so a part
    registered later is never after a `return`; under `WB_TASK` it returns at once (#1363). It
    exports `ID` and `status(options, env)`.
  - `driver.ts` (#1316, *The driver*): `startDriver(host, run, pid, used)` registers the
    `model.request` hook, the `session.model.selected` subscription, the RPC contract
    `WorkbenchDriver` (`id: "workbench-driver"`: `driver` `{sessionID, model?, once?}` → `wb driver
    --session <id> --json [--model <ref>] [--once]`'s object, `model` only when `parseRef` reads it;
    `pin` `{sessionID}` → `{applied, model?, why?}`) and
    the beat timer, and returns the cleanup; `beatOnce`, `beatOf`, `listAll`, `storePath`,
    `parseRef` (OpenCode's `Model.Ref.parse`, as `routes.driver_ref`), `variantOf`, `applyPin`; `wbRunner` runs
    wb (`findWb`, `wbEnv`) with stdin, killed after `WB_TIMEOUT_MS` 30 s.
  - `consent.ts` (#1314): what Claude Code's mod gates, gated in OpenCode, for every model the
    server runs (the driver, a subagent, another plugin's call). Its parts:
    - **The tools**, in the namespace `workbench` (`ctx.tool.transform`; OpenCode names them
      `workbench_<name>`; its one description, `wb.ts`'s `NAMESPACE_DESCRIPTION`, is the chat's too,
      as the last part to declare it wins, `tools.ts` declaring it too): `workbench_route {args}`, `workbench_start`
      (typed by `tools.ts`'s `START_INPUT`, its argv `startCall`'s: `{name, spec | spec_file, repo, role,
      size, test, model, skill[], image[], setup, auto_fix, args[]}`, a value one `--flag=value` word, the
      spec on stdin as `--spec -`, which the dry run doesn't read; `{args}` alone, the tool's first shape
      and what the gates' `VIA_TOOL` refusal names, is that argv as it is),
      `workbench_settings_set {key, value}` and `workbench_patch_send {slug, title, body_file,
      draft?, anyway?}`. Each runs wb (`runner`: the plugin's wb, `findWb`, in the session's
      directory, with `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` the calling session's and `CLAUDECODE`,
      `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `WB_TASK` dropped, stdin a typed start's spec, else closed). Route, start (an
      arg starting `--m`, a `--model`) and settings first run wb's dry run (`wb route --dry-run
      --json …`, `--start …`, `wb settings set k v --dry-run --json`); a `gate: true` answer asks
      the user in a form (`Allow` / `Don't`), and on the yes writes the dry run's `approval` to
      `$WB_HOME/route-ok.<session>.json` (`writeApproval`, `at` now) before the real call, which
      wb takes (`store.approval_name`, `routes.approved`). The send reads the body file, shows
      where it goes (patches.json's `upstream`, default `a-schaefers/workbench`, publicly), a
      personal-patch line when a commit carries the trailer, the title and the body's first
      `BODY_LINES` 20 lines, asks `Send it` / `Don't send`, writes `send-ok.<session>.json`
      (`{slug, title, body_file, body, draft, anyway, at}`, what `patches._approved` checks) and
      runs `wb patch send … --body-file <absolute>`. A no is `NOT_CHANGED` / `NOT_SENT`; no form
      shown is `NO_FORM` (fail closed: the user's own terminal runs the command); a nonzero exit
      is wb's own words, thrown.
    - **The forms**: a server plugin has no form API in 2.4.1, so `Asker` picks the id
      (`frm_workbench…`, OpenCode's `Form.ID` prefix), and the RPC `Consent` (`id:
      "workbench-consent"`) emits `ask {sessionID, formID, title, question, yes, no}` to every
      TUI; `consent-tui.ts` creates the session form with that id
      (`client.session.form.create`, one string field `answer` whose options are `yes` and `no`,
      `metadata.kind: "workbench.consent"`) and calls the `shown` method, a conflict (409: another
      TUI made it first) too, so one form shows in every TUI, the web app and a paired phone. The
      server part is subscribed to the bus (`ctx.event.subscribe`) before it asks; `form.replied`
      with that id and session is the answer, `form.cancelled` a no. No `shown` within `SHOWN_MS`
      10 s (no TUI attached, the TUI part missing) is `none`: the server emits `close` (a late
      TUI cancels the form) and refuses. `--auto` answers permission asks, never forms, so it
      can't say yes for the user. A call stopped while it waits is a no, its form closed.
    - **The permission hook** (`ctx.permission.hook("evaluate")`, the gate every call's
      permission passes, whatever its rules say): a deny with the words, which reach the model.
      `shell`: OpenCode's resources are each simple command's raw text; `simpleWords`
      (`words.ts`: quotes undone, redirects' files apart, a heredoc's body never words) feeds the
      kernel's `gateOf` (commands, not mentions: #1364's rule), and `shellRefusal` denies a write
      onto routes.json or an approval file (`ROUTES_EDIT`, `APPROVAL_OWN`), `wb patch send` (`SEND_VIA_TOOL`), and a live `wb route`, `wb start
      --model` or `wb settings set` whose own dry run (as the session) says gated
      (`VIA_TOOL(<tool>)`). The commands run from the call's `workdir` (the shell tool's input,
      which OpenCode tells the model to set over a cd), else the session's directory, and a `cd`
      or `pushd` moves the next ones' (its word literal; a bare one to `$HOME`; after `cd -`, a
      variable or a `popd` a relative path is unknown). OpenCode's scan leaves a plain `cd`,
      `pushd` or `popd` out of the resources, so `execute.before` keeps each `shell` call's line
      and workdir by call id (the last `CALLS_KEPT` 64; a Code Mode program's call, whose
      permission names the program, by the session's newest line holding every resource) and
      `lineCommands` puts the dropped directory changes back between the resources they sat
