      between (each resource found where a command starts, never inside a cd's words; one not
      found leaves the scan's list) (#1314's lane notes, 2026-11-26). A line OpenCode couldn't split (`metadata.reason`: a heredoc,
      `$(…)`) is left to wb, whose gate refuses it without an approval anyway. `edit` (every file
      tool's): routes.json (`$WB_ROUTES`) and `route-ok`/`send-ok` files, with or without a
      session (`gates.APPROVAL`), denied for every agent; then the coding gate (`codingGate`, on
      `$WB_HOME/coding.json` and the task's own `coding.json`) for a file in a task's worktree:
      `decide` passes, a one-task exception's first edit stamps it `started`, `ask` asks
      (`Let the driver edit <task>'s code now?`, one form per session and task however many
      edits wait) and on the yes runs `wb coding allow <task> --said=…` (`CODING_SAID`), and
      `only` refuses (`ONLY`). Without the kernel beside the plugin (a copy of
      `opencode-plugin/` alone) the shell gate is wb's alone and a closed coding gate stays
      closed (`NO_KERNEL`).
    - **local_only** (`ctx.tool.hook("execute.before")`, which sees the text): an `edit`,
      `write` (the file in `path`, 2.3.2's and 2.4.1's, or 1.x's `filePath`) or `patch` of commands.json (`$WB_COMMANDS`) that drops a repo's `"local_only":
      true` is thrown before it runs (`localOnlyRefusal`, `localOnlyPatchRefusal`: the mod's
      rule); only the user lifts it.
    - **Sends upstream** (`upstream.ts`'s `Upstream`, a second `execute.before` hook after the
      gates', imported at setup as the kernel is; #1296's row 14).
    Nothing runs at import; setup returns a cleanup that ends the bus loop and disposes the RPC.
  - `upstream.ts` (#1296's row 14, 2026-11-26): the mod's consent dialog on the other sends, in
    the same form. On `execute.before` (once a call, before its permission ask, the whole input;
    a throw refuses it): a `shell` call's `command`, from its `workdir` (else the session's
    directory), is read by `mod/hooks/shell.ts`'s `upstreamAim`, the mod's own reading (*The
    consent gate*: `bash -c`, `eval`, a fed shell, an interpreter's code that runs commands, the
    kernel's `gateOf` per simple command), not OpenCode's scan, which hands the common `gh issue
    create --body "$(cat <<'EOF' …)"` over unread, while wb has no refusal of its own behind a gh
    write or a git push; the permission hook would also run again on a pending ask's
    re-evaluation and ask twice. Aimed as the mod aims it: a gated directory (`gatedWhere`: the
    patch clone, patches.json's `source`, else `WB_SOURCE`, else
    `~/.local/share/workbench/source`; `$WB_HOME/upstream/`; Claude Code's marketplace clone and
    cache), by real path too; a plugins directory (Claude Code's, and OpenCode's package caches,
    `packageCaches`: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/opencode/npm`, `~/.cache/opencode/npm`) whose checkout's
    origin is upstream; or the upstream's name (patches.json's `upstream`, `a-schaefers/workbench`,
    the former name) in the line, unless it runs in a developer's own clone of upstream (`git -C
    <dir> remote get-url origin`, never a gated or plugins directory). A `wb patch send` there is
    refused with `SEND_VIA_TOOL`. An MCP tool whose namespace (its server's name) holds `github`
    (`githubTool`; no info: `<server>_<name>`), not `get_`/`list_`/`search_`, whose input names
    the upstream or a repository of its name (`githubAimsUpstream`), asks the same, unless the
    session's directory is a developer's clone. The form (`Asker`, `consent.ts`'s): `The driver
    wants to send this to GitHub (<slug>), publicly: <the command>` (`shownCommand`: the whole
    line up to 600 characters, else the outward command then the line's start; an MCP call's
    input up to 4000, `shownInput`), `Send it` / `Don't send`; the yes lets that one call through,
    nothing remembered; a no or a dismissal is `NOT_SENT`, no TUI in time `NO_FORM_SENT` (fail
    closed); `--auto` never answers a form. `upstream-env.d.ts`: what its tests use beyond the others'
    declarations (`symlinkSync`).
  - `gates.ts`, `words.ts`: the pure rules `consent.ts` applies (paths: `places`, `guarded`,
    `taskOfPath`; `shellRefusal`, `lineCommands`; `codingMode`; the local_only rules; the patch text's files and
    lines) and the shell splitter, each tested alone.
  - `tools.ts` (#1335; the host-shape decision's "tool schemas replace the command recipes"): the
    procedure's everyday wb commands as typed tools in the `workbench` namespace, `codemode: false`
    (direct tools), each one wb command run as the calling session (`runner`: the options' wb,
    `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` the session's, consent's dropped marks, stdin fed, killed on the call's
    signal or its limit) in the session's directory (`sessionDirs`: `session.get`'s location and
    subpath, read once), its fields the flags by name (`SPECS`), its answer wb's report:
    `workbench_status {task?, all?, all_sessions?}`, `workbench_diff {task, stat?, all?, paths?}`,
    `workbench_feedback {task, text, fresh?, keep_context?, spec_gap?, image?}` (the text on stdin,
    `--message -`), `workbench_accept {task, message?, merge?, merge_as?, include?, take_claude_md?,
    no_sign?, spec_gap?}` (`ACCEPT_MS` 10 minutes: a signing key's touch), `workbench_discard {task,
    reason?, spec_gap?, keep_branch?, drop_steps?}` and `workbench_wait {task?, minutes?}` (`wb wait
    --timeout`, `WAIT_MIN` 10 minutes, at most `WAIT_MAX_MIN` 60, its exit 2, timed out or closed,
    an answer, not a failure). A value is one `--flag=value` argv word, so one starting with `-` is
    never a flag (`wb diff`'s flags go first, then `-- <task> <paths>`: argparse takes `--` only
    with no flag after the name). A nonzero exit is wb's words and `(exit N)`, thrown (the
    procedure reads some exits by number: 3, accept's 5). `workbench_start` is `consent.ts`'s (an API
    model asks first), typed by `START_INPUT` and `startCall` from here. No permission rule: OpenCode
    reads a tool's `options.permission` only to hide a denied one (`core/src/tool.ts`). The
    rendering's recipes name them (`skill.ts`); the shell's `wb` still works. `tools-env.d.ts`: the
    runtime only it uses (chat-env.d.ts's rule).
  - `calls.ts` (#1331): the driver's own calls in a task's worktree as `claude-calls/` rows,
    the mod's rule (`callRows`, `tasksNamed`, `callFile`, `rowText`): `execute.before` writes a
    row begun for an `edit`, `write` or `patch` of a file in `tasks/<t>/` or a `shell` command run
    in or naming one, of a task with a task.json; `execute.after` writes it over (`end`), or
    `denied` when the tool's error is a permission's (`Permission.*`: a deny rule, the gates'
    own). A plain decline fires no `execute.after` (2.4.1 turns `Permission.DeclinedError` into a
    defect), so `Declines` reads the bus: `permission.asked` names its call (`source.id`) and a
    `permission.replied` of `reject` writes that call's row `denied`. `wb accept` reads them as

    is its hand (committed with `--include`) and what a build its `shell` ran there wrote is left

    `test_wb_accept_tells_an_opencode_drivers_write_in_the_worktree_from_the_build_it_ran_there`,
    #1331's live acceptance, 2026-11-26).
  - `notices.ts`, `jobs.ts` (#1313, #1334): *Notices on OpenCode*, below; `notices-env.d.ts`, the
    runtime only they use (chat-env.d.ts's rule). `notices-tui.ts`: the TUI part's side, its toasts.
  - `rpc.ts`: the contract `Workbench` (`id: "workbench"`), JSON Schema, no validator package:

    /api/rpc/workbench/status` with `{"input": {}}` (`protocol/src/groups/rpc.ts`), by the TUI
    part as `ctx.client.rpc(Workbench).status({})`.
  - `tui.ts`: `{id: "workbench", setup}`. OpenCode's TUI loads it only for a server plugin that is
    active (`tui/src/plugin/context.tsx`, `serverTuiPlugins`). It asks `status` (`askStatus`: again

    `rpc.unavailable`, the location for `$HOME` booting on it and loading its plugins only after
    answering: once the whole TUI went without its panel, footer and palette entry, #1488, the
    owner's own machine, 2026-11-26) after setup has returned, never awaited in it (the TUI
    activates its plugins one after another, and `ui.panel.open` works only once setup returned),
    and, when no wb was found, shows one warning toast titled `Workbench` (`wb isn't at <path>, which the

  - `spans.ts` (#1333, slice 4c of #1296; pure, no OpenTUI or Solid, so Bun tests it bare): the

    a new size from the same frame and ending, and ends it where `splashFont` gives none;
    `step()` to the next frame, false and `done` after the last; `frame()` the spans; `end()`.
    `restTarget(rows)`: with no page to say where, the apprentice ends at the bottom left and the
    words rise away (no modeline row is known, so no bar). `splashOn(read)`: splash.json as the
    mod's `splashOn` reads it.
  - `splash.tsx`: the OpenTUI views, `<text>` rows of `<span>`s. `Spans`, `Apprentice({theme,
    pose})`, `Splash({theme, target, onDone})` (filling its box: `onSizeChange` fits the `Play`, a

    named as the `workbench-models` skill) as a turn. `/workbench-update` (`UPDATE`): `wb update`
    (`UPDATE_MS` 600 s; the rest `RUN_MS` 120 s), its output posted without a turn (OpenCode reloads
    the plugin once `wb update` moved its entry), a failure the command's error.
  - `flows.ts` (#1295): each flow's own slash command (*Deep workflows*), server commands as `commands.ts`'s
    (`registerFlows`, one `wb run flows --json` at setup, awaited: a transform added after setup
    returned was never listed in the TUI, seen live on 2.4.1; `flowDefinitions`), each posting
    `mod/hooks/flows.ts`'s `FLOW_NOTE` with the line typed (`prompt.text`) as a `synthetic` turn (`resume:
    true`: the user's ask), which has the driver run `wb run start --flow <flow> --args '<line>'`. No flow
    with a command (or no wb) registers nothing; the root package.json's `files` brings `mod/hooks/flows.ts`.
  - `upkeep-env.d.ts`: the runtime `upkeep.ts` and `commands.ts` use beyond the others'
    (`writeFileSync`), in a file of its own as `chat-env.d.ts` is.
  - `chat.ts`: the web chat (*The web chat on OpenCode*, below); `chat-env.d.ts`, the runtime only
    it uses (timers, `AbortController`, `node:child_process`'s `execFile`, `readFileSync`), in a
    file of its own so parts built at once each add theirs; its OpenCode API shapes
    (`ChatContext`) are its own, from the sources each names.
  - `env.d.ts`, `host.d.ts`: the runtime (`process`, `URL`, `import.meta.url`, `node:fs`,
    `node:path`, `node:url`, `bun:test`, `AbortController`) and the
    subset of OpenCode's plugin API the parts use, declared from OpenCode's source (each shape
    names its file), so the package imports nothing from `@opencode/*` and type-checks with
    nothing installed. A new use adds its declaration; a session hook is a key of
    `SessionHooks` (`session.hook` is keyed by it, as OpenCode's `Hooks<Spec>` is), declared
    there or from its own module (`declare module './host.d.ts'`).
- **No import-time side effects**, for every part: OpenCode imports a module to learn its id
  before it applies removals, so a disabled plugin is still imported.
- **Off inside agents.** The user's global `plugins` load in every `opencode run` the runner
  starts (a canary plugin there runs in the agent's lane: `RealOpenCodeRun`). `context.layer`
  writes `"plugins": ["-workbench"]` (`context.PLUGIN_OFF`, `ocplugin.PLUGIN_OFF`), OpenCode's
  remove-by-id entry (`plugins.mdx` *Control*; `core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts`, `remove`), which
  holds because the layer (`OPENCODE_CONFIG`) loads after the global files and a later add would
  re-enable it (`core/src/config.ts`: `globalSupplementary` below `explicit`). `runner.rules_env`
  says it again in the content, after the user's own content `plugins` (kept, in order), since the
  content loads after the layer. Removed, the plugin's setup never runs and its TUI part never
  loads; `WB_TASK` is the second fence.
- **Installing it.** OpenCode's own mechanism first (#1357's decision):
  `opencode plugin add 'github:a-schaefers/workbench#main'` (`ocplugin.ADD`, `GIT_SPEC`): this
  repository as a Git package, which OpenCode installs into its package cache
  (`<cache>/npm/git-workbench-<12 hex of the spec's sha256>/<generation>/node_modules/opencode-workbench`,
  `ocplugin._git_key`, `copy_of`) and adds to the global config's `plugins`
  (`cli/src/commands/handlers/plugin/add.ts`); following `#main`, OpenCode checks it at start and
  daily and installs a newer commit (`plugins.mdx` *Manage*). It brings wb with the plugin (the
  root `package.json`'s `files`), and without options the plugin runs that wb: the whole install,
  no clone. #1311's review (2026-11-25) found the first form,
  `…#main::path:opencode-plugin` (npm's subdirectory selector, `ocplugin.SUBDIR`), fetched
  `opencode-plugin/` alone, a plugin that could do nothing without a clone; such an entry is still
  recognised (`ocplugin.ours`, `brings_wb`) and runs wb by name from PATH. So is any Git spec
  whose package OpenCode put in its cache is this one (`copy_of`: a fork, a `git+file://` clone),
  which doctor called not installed (#1311's live check). `wb setup --opencode`
  (`ocplugin.install`, *Every `wb` command*) is the fallback, from a clone: it writes the entry
  through `models.own_config` with `options` `{wb: <clone>/bin/wb, env: {<each WB_* of
  store.PATH_VARS set there, absolute>}}` (OpenCode's background service starts without the
  user's shell, so the paths ride in the entry), and after `opencode plugin add` gives that entry
  the options, so it runs the clone's wb. The entry names a copy of the clone's
  `opencode-plugin/` as committed at HEAD, never the live directory: OpenCode watches a configured
  local plugin and reloads it on every change (`core/src/config/plugin/source.ts`), so each save
  ran uncommitted, a patch under test with it (#1321's finding 16). `ocplugin.make_copy`: one copy
  per tree, `~/.local/share/workbench/opencode-plugin/<12 hex of the tree>/opencode-plugin` (the
  tree, `ocplugin.head_tree`'s key and `copy.json`'s `tree`: `opencode-plugin/`'s git tree, or with
  mod files a sha1 of it and their blobs, so a commit changing only `splash.ts`, or a kernel rebuilt
  alone, makes a new copy)
  (`ocplugin.copies_dir`; its tests left out), the mod files the root `package.json`'s `files` name
  under `mod/` beside it at `<12 hex>/mod/hooks/…`, where `spans.ts`'s and the notices' imports look
  (`ocplugin.shared_files`, read at the copied commit; #1333: a copy of `opencode-plugin/` alone
  left them unresolved), with `copy.json` beside it (`commit`, `tree`,
  `clone`, `ocplugin.copy_info`), out of every lane's writable places and readable there (the
  agent's OpenCode imports it to learn its id); off git the live directory, said. Setup says `ok
  OpenCode loads a copy of <clone>/opencode-plugin as committed at <sha>, not the live directory it
  reloads on every change: wb update refreshes it`, and `--  opencode-plugin/ has uncommitted
  changes, which the copy leaves out: …` when it has. `wb update` on a clone, or on Claude Code's
  marketplace clone (#1479: it ran on a user's clone only, and that copy stayed at the setup commit),
  moves an entry on a copy of it (or its live directory) to HEAD's copy when the tree changed (`ocplugin.refresh`,
  silent otherwise: a rewrite reloads OpenCode's plugins); the copies no entry loads go but the
  one the file named before (a running OpenCode may still hold it). Setup records the clone as
  patches.json's `source` (*Local patches*), and `wb patch init` from a marketplace clone the
  plugin loaded from runs the new clone's `wb setup --opencode` (#1321's finding N2). `wb update` updates that clone
  without Claude Code's steps when Claude Code doesn't have workbench (*Every `wb` command*). The package and its wb land in OpenCode's package cache,
  which the lane keeps out once they are there or about to be (`ocplugin.in_cache`,
  `context.plugin_caches`, *What the agent knows*): an agent can't rewrite what the user's
  OpenCode imports and runs. The Git install's wb runs from its generation's directory: a new
  commit is a new directory, and OpenCode removes a generation only when two newer ones exist
  and it is over a week old (`npm.ts` `collect`). That wb knows it is OpenCode's install, no clone
  (`ocplugin.runs_from_cache`, `cli._install_kind`'s `opencode`): `wb update --check` says
  `OpenCode's install at <dir>: OpenCode updates it (it follows <spec>, checked at its start and
  daily)` (`ocplugin.updated_by`: the `plugins` entry whose package in the cache this is, else
  `github:a-schaefers/workbench#main`), `wb update` `wb update leaves
  OpenCode's install at <dir> to OpenCode: …`, both exit 0 with nothing stopped, `wb doctor` `ok
  install: OpenCode's, at <dir>: …`, and `wb patch` refuses, naming a clone and `bin/wb setup
  --opencode` there; each said git's error before (#1311's third review). `wb setup` (with
  `--opencode` too) links nothing there, `--  wb setup links nothing to OpenCode's install at <dir>:
  …` (links, a service unit or options naming a generation OpenCode replaces would outlive it and
  pin the plugin to an old wb), then prints `first run:` (`cli.first_run(host="opencode")`, its API
  keys line too) and `next: wb doctor`, exit 0, changing nothing: refused before the checklist,
  First run's step 1 failed on the main OpenCode install (#1496).
- **Never in wb's own OpenCode calls.** `models.plugin_off` puts `"-workbench"` last in
  `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, after the user's own content `plugins` (kept; content that doesn't
  parse is left for OpenCode to refuse), in every one of them: through `models._opencode_env`,
  `model_list`'s `opencode serve --stdio` (`_list_catalog`), `_opencode_json`'s commands,
  `models._exported_key`'s `auth export <pid> --standalone` (wb start, doctor, route) and
  `keyhole._opencode`'s `auth export` and `auth list` (every API task's start); directly,
  `transcript.export`'s `session export` and `find_session`'s `session list` (2.4.1's session
  commands run no plugin's setup; said anyway). Each starts a private server that loads the
  user's global plugins, and `model_list` waits for them (#1311's reviews). Not `opencode
  --version` (no server), and not the agent's `opencode run`, whose layer removes it.
- **What `wb doctor` says** (`ocplugin.doctor_lines`, after the Claude Code mod's line): one line
  per install, in OpenCode's load order (the copies in OpenCode's global `plugin/` and `plugins/` directories,
  `ocplugin.DISCOVERED`, both of which it loads, `core/src/plugin/source-directory.ts`; then each config
  file's entries, then `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`'s): `ok  the OpenCode plugin <spec> (<how>, in
  <file>) runs <wb>` where `<how>` is `OpenCode's own install, from Git`, `… from npm`, `this
  clone's opencode-plugin/`, `this clone` (an entry naming the clone itself), `a copy of this
  clone's opencode-plugin/ as committed at <sha>` (or `of <clone>'s`), `another copy's: <dir>`
  or `found in OpenCode's plugins directory`,
  and `<wb>` the options' path, `the wb it brings, <path>` (`ocplugin.brought_wb`: `../bin/wb` from
  the server part's file as the copy's `package.json` `exports` name it, links resolved as Bun
  resolves them, so `<clone>/bin/wb` for an entry naming the clone or a link to it in `plugins/`;
  `d.parent/bin/wb` named the wrong one for both, #1311's third review; or the Git
  install's in the package cache), or `wb by name from OpenCode's PATH (<which wb>'s here; the
  background service's may differ: wb setup --opencode names it)`; `--` for a Git entry OpenCode
  hasn't fetched yet (`isn't in OpenCode's package cache yet: OpenCode installs it, with its wb,
  at its next start`); `BAD` for an options' `wb`
  that isn't there (`… it isn't there; wb setup --opencode from your Workbench clone`), a
  directory that holds no copy (`… which holds no copy of it`), or an install that brings no wb
  when none is on PATH (`brings no wb and finds none on PATH: <ocplugin.GET_WB>`); `--` for each
  `"-workbench"` (`turns the OpenCode plugin off`); none installed is a `--` line (`opencode
  plugin add '…' (it brings its wb), or wb setup --opencode from this clone`), as the plugin is
  optional. After an install's line, `--  the OpenCode plugin's copy is as of <sha>, older than
  <clone>'s opencode-plugin/ at <sha>: wb update (or wb setup --opencode there) refreshes it`, or,
  for an entry on a clone's live directory, `--  the OpenCode plugin loads <dir> as it is, reloaded
  on every change there (#1321): wb setup --opencode loads a copy of what is committed`. An OpenCode config that can't be read is said, never a traceback
  (`ocplugin.installs`' RuntimeError; a top level that isn't an object is `models._layers`'
  `doesn't parse`). With the plugin installed (or wb run from OpenCode's install) and the Claude
  Code mod not listed, the missing Claude Code skill link is `--  /workbench isn't in <dir>: Claude
  Code's path only (wb setup links it)`, and wb off PATH `--  wb isn't on this shell's PATH:
  OpenCode's plugin runs its own …`, neither `BAD` (#1321's finding 26).

  `test_with_landlock_an_agent_cant_write_opencodes_package_cache_holding_the_plugin`. Checked by
  hand on 2.4.1 (2026-11-25): `opencode plugin add` of the repository's Git spec installs it and
  its wb from the package cache, and the TUI's `/plugins` lists it under TUI and Server; #1335's
  (2026-11-25, a scratch HOME and XDG dirs): `run --agent workbench` with a reply calling the
  `skill` tool on `workbench-spec` gets the part's text back. The
  splash checked by hand on 2.4.1 (2026-11-25, tmux at 150x46, 130x40 mid-play, 100x30 and 70x24,
  a scratch config and state; a scratch plugin opened the panel, as #1312's `/workbench` will):

- **Live checks #1311 owns**, each run by hand in a real OpenCode by the slice that first builds

  2026-11-26 with `--standalone`'s private server, above; the background service's is the same

  resent once only (#1313, the notices: checked on 2.4.1, 2026-11-25, by `RealOpenCodePlugin`'s

### Notices on OpenCode

`opencode-plugin/notices.ts` (#1313; the host-shape decision: a singleton `wb events` in the server
part, `synthetic` ids bound to task, kind and sequence, one `experimental.idle` re-wake per unacked
notice with a timer fallback). The same outcomes as the mod's deliver and rewake (*A task, start to
finish*, the notices), OpenCode-native; the decisions are the kernel's (`noticesDue`, `noticePlan`,
`rewakePlan`, `owns`, imported from `../mod/hooks/core.ts`, the membrane), and wb stays the system of
record: the plugin reads `notify.jsonl` (its last `NOTIFY_TAIL` 1 MiB), each task's `task.json`,
`status.json`, `acked`, `noticed` and `ask/<id>.{json,answer}`, and writes only through `wb ack`.
- **One lane per server process** (`lanes()`, on `globalThis`, as the chat's): one `wb events`
  child (`ears`: its hello sets `earsOk`, every line a look; respawned `EARS_RETRY_MS` 2 s after it
  ends, doubling to a minute until a hello; with no wb found, a minute), one `SCAN_MS` 15 s timer
  (the fallback), and per setup instance its session API, its `experimental.idle` and `prompt`
  hooks, its event feed (`session.execution.started`/`succeeded`/`failed`/`interrupted`, taken once
  by id) and its `workbench-notices` RPC registration. A server without the session or event
  domains (an older one, a test's ctx) gets none of it.
- **Whose.** A task is delivered to the root of its `session` (a subagent that ran `wb start`
  reports to its driver) when its `driver.tool` is `opencode` and this server's store holds the
  session (`session.get`), judged by `owns`; another server's, Claude Code's or no session's task
  is left alone, unacked and untoasted (its own host, or `wb wait`, delivers it). Adoption by
  directory stays `wb adopt`'s.
- **Delivery** (each due notice's `noticePlan`, `busy` the session's execution under way): `wake`:
  `wb ack <task> <ts>` (exit 3: another server or `wb wait` took it; any other failure: tried again
  at the next look), then `session.synthetic` `{sessionID, id: noticeId(task, kind, ts), text,
  description: "Workbench: <task> <headline>", metadata: {source: "workbench.notice", task, kind,
  ts, title}, delivery: "queue"}`, which opens a turn on an idle session; refused, `wb ack <task>
  <prev> --if <ts>` puts the mark back and the net tries again after a minute (`dropped`). `steer`
  (a question mid-turn, its agent blocked): the same with `delivery: "steer"` and `MIDTURN_NOTE`;
  refused, held. `hold`: nothing until the turn ends (its execution's end, the idle hook, the
  timer), which looks again. `ack`: acknowledged in silence; `missed` too, and a question that timed
  out unanswered while held (`NO_ANSWER`) is said in a queued turn. `none` (wakes off): the toast
  only. The text is the mod's (`[workbench] Task \`<n>\` <headline>.`, the notice, the next step:
  `HEADLINE`, `NEXT`, `BATCH_NEXT`, `SPEND_NEXT` (routes.json's `day_usd` read only for a `spend`
  stop: `routesPath`), `AGENTS_NEXT`, the provider's, local-only and outside-the-step stops,
  `headlineOf`, `nextOf`, `wakeText`), said to an OpenCode driver, and while `wb chat away` says
  `away`, `AWAY_TAIL` (answer with `workbench_chat_reply`).
- **The id** (`noticeId`): OpenCode's own shape, `msg_`, 12 hex of the notice's ts in ms as
  `schema/src/identifier.ts` makes it (counter 2; chat.ts's `inboxId` is 1), then `wn` and 12 hex
  of an FNV-1a over the task, kind and ts. Every try, from this server after a restart or another
  on the store, sends the same id, and OpenCode's inbox gives back the first admission
  (`session/inbox.ts` `reconcile`): a resend is idempotent and silent, never an error. `wb ack`
  stays the once-only guarantee.
- **A run's own notices** (#1278's S9, `deliverRuns`, `parseRunLines`: rows with `run` and no `task`):
  delivered to the session here that ran `wb run start` (run.json `session` with `session_kind`
  `opencode`, judged as a task's), by core.ts's `runNoticesDue` (each run's newest however old, #1491) and
  `runNoticePlan` (still true while the run is in the row's `phase`), `wb ack <run> <ts> --run`, then a queued synthetic, `noticeId("run:<run>",
  kind, ts)`, its text the row's whole, the toast `run <run> <RUN_HEADLINE>`; refused, `wb ack <run> <prev>
  --run --if <ts>` and the next look tries again (no net for a run). *Deep workflows* has the row.
- **The net** (`rewake`, the kernel's `rewakePlan`): a task of a session here waiting on its driver
  a minute after its last status change, its news never had (`acked` below its newest notice,
  this load's or its `noticed` mark, or with none below its change), wakes the idle session once:
  `wb ack <task> <now>`, then a queued synthetic (`noticeId(task, "rewake", <its change>)`) naming
  `wb report <task>`, the headline and next step of its newest notice of the phase's kind
  (`[workbench] Task \`<n>\` is ready for review, 61s ago, and no notice reached you. …`). Once a
  change (`rewoken`). Looked at by the idle hook (`experimental.idle`: what it admits runs in the
  same execution), each execution's end and the timer.
- **Wakes off**: the config entry's options `wake: "off"` (the mod's option): toasts only, no
  synthetic, no rewake, no settings offer turn; the upkeep's `workbench-wake` entry tells the
  driver so (`upkeep.ts`, #1315).
- **Toasts** go to the TUI part over the RPC `WorkbenchNotices` (`id: "workbench-notices"`, no
  methods, the event `toast` `{key, title, message, variant, sessionID, notify}`), emitted from every
  instance's registration; `notices-tui.ts`'s `noticesTui` subscribes (`client.rpc(...).events.on`)
  and shows each key once (`shown`, the last `SEEN_KEEP` 200): `ui.toast.show` with the task's
  session (a session not on screen gets OpenCode's offer to open it) and, for a review, question,
  stuck or failed notice (`WAKE_KINDS`, `ALERT`'s keys: a stuck or failed one a warning), a desktop notification through OpenCode's own attention
  settings while the terminal isn't focused (`attention.notify`, `when: "blurred"`).

### Background jobs on OpenCode

`opencode-plugin/jobs.ts` (#1334; the host-shape decision: the due rules live in wb behind
`--if-due`, the idle hook checks them and shows a toast). `Jobs.tick` runs at the end of each of the
notices' looks once a turn ended here (`sawTurn`) and `wb events` said hello; "quiet" is no task
anywhere active and none of this server's waiting on its driver within rewake's 12 hours
(`rewakePlan`'s `recent`: the mod's `quietForJobs`). Each job's wb call has `JOB_MS` (two minutes,
the mod's `runWb`), not the lane's `RUN_MS` 15 s: `wb update --check` fetches, and its `checked_at`
is written before the fetch, so a killed check lost the week's (the 2026-11-26 review).
- `wb update --check --if-due`, once a load: `update available …` and the marketplace clone's
  local changes (`LOCAL_CHANGES`, patches.CHECK_LINE's opening) toasted as wb says them.
- `wb optimize start --if-due`, once a load, quiet: `measuring …` toasted.
- `wb deepmode --moved`, once a load while workflows.json holds 2.1's `mode: on` and no `deepmode`:
  its one line (the story's `moved.deepmode`) toasted, as the mod's `deepmodeMoved` does (#1507).
- `wb scout --if-due`, once a load, in a server that owned a task in this load (`delegated`), wakes
  on, quiet, every session idle and `QUIET_MS` (a minute) after a turn: wb's offer line toasted
  (`cli.scout_offer_due`, the mod's `scoutIfDue` rule moved into wb; scout.json `offered_at`).
- `wb settings offers --if-due --json` once settings-changes.jsonl grew, as the session the web chat
  listens to here (chat/listener.json's, this server's pid), else the root session the user last
  typed in here (the `prompt` hook, unmarked), never while another listener's live claim stands
  (Claude Code's mod or another server says them) and not before a session is there (the rows wait):
  each offer toasted and, wakes on, a queued synthetic turn (`[workbench] The user changed …\n<help>\n
  Offer to help with it, and install or change nothing without their yes.`, its id `noticeId(
  "settings:<key>", "offer", ts)`); the other rows one synthetic steer with `resume: false`:
  OpenCode publishes pending steers with the next turn's own (the user's prompt), so that turn reads
  it, with no turn of its own (a queued one is promoted alone after it, 2.4.1's inbox `promote`).

### The web chat on OpenCode

`opencode-plugin/chat.ts` (#1319, #1340; the host-shape decision: in-process turns and a
`chat_reply` tool, `workbench_chat_reply` to the model, the listener the server and its heartbeat). The same outcomes as the Claude
Code mod's *The web chat listener*, OpenCode-native, with #1340's simplifications; wb stays the
system of record: every write is a `wb chat` command (`runner`: the options' wb and `WB_*` paths,
`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` the session it acts for, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_PID`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `WB_TASK` dropped, `RUN_MS` 15 s), and it reads only
`chat/open.json`, `chat/listener.json` and `messages.jsonl`'s size.
- **One lane per server process** (`lane()`, on `globalThis`): OpenCode may set the plugin up per
  location; each setup adds its session API, its `prompt` and `execute.before` hooks and its event
  feed, and events are taken once by id (`seen`). Setup registers the tool and the hooks only; the
  poll (`POLL_MS` 2 s, a file read) and the event feed (`EVENTS`: `session.execution.*`,
  `session.inbox.delivered`/`cancelled`, `session.text.ended`, `session.revert.*`,
  `permission.asked`/`replied`, `form.created`/`replied`/`cancelled`) start once a session here
  listens (`activate`), so wb's own `--standalone` servers, which remove the plugin anyway
  (`models.plugin_off`), never start or claim the chat. The last cleanup drops the claim.
- **Who listens.** A prompt the user typed (the `prompt` hook: a root session, unmarked metadata,
  not `[web chat] ` or `[agent `; automations, `/goal` and our own deliveries carry metadata) makes
  that session the listener: `wb chat url --json` (on or off, every `CHECK_MS` 60 s, which brings
  the server up as the mod's link does), `wb chat back`, and `wb chat listener <session> --pid
  <server pid>` (`chat.hold`: refused while another live claim stands, a Claude Code session's or
  another server's; the same server moves it between its sessions). `busy` follows the session's
  executions. A claim found emptied (`wb chat off`, then on) is taken again at once; a refused one
  at the next check. A server restarted listens again once the user types in it.
- **Delivery.** Each message `open.json` holds (the user's, or an agent's: `agentOf`), oldest first,
  once `wb chat claim <id> --by <session>` grants it (refused: `RETRY_MS` 60 s later; expired:
  never), goes in as `session.prompt` with `delivery: "steer"` (it enters a running turn at its
  next step, or opens one), `metadata: {source: "workbench.chat", chat: <id>}` (`SOURCE`), and the
  inbox id `inboxId(<id>)`: OpenCode's own shape (`msg_`, 12 hex of the message's own ms time as
  `schema/src/identifier.ts` makes it, then `wb` and the id's hex twice), so it sorts as a prompt
  typed then would (another shape sorted wrong on a revert, #1340) and a retry gets the first
  admission back; a conflict (that id in another session) is delivered there. The text is the
  mod's `chatPrompt` (`[web chat] <words>`, an agent's `[agent <name>] …` with its lines indented
  and `[message <id>: answer with workbench_chat_reply, to <id>]`, `about`, attachments), then
  `WEB_NOTE` or `AGENT_NOTE` (answer with the `workbench_chat_reply` tool: every text names
  `REPLY_ID`). Nothing while a revert is staged in the
  session (a prompt commits it: `session.revert.staged` until `cleared`/`committed`). On
  `session.inbox.delivered`: `wb chat ack <id> --by <session> --how now` (an agent's into a running
  turn `into`, #1175) and, for the user's, `--away`. On `session.inbox.cancelled` (only
  `Session.cancelInbox` publishes it: the user cancelled the pending item in the TUI or the app)
  the message is dismissed, never sent again: `wb chat ack <id> --by <session> --how now`, not
  owed, and for the user's `wb chat back` (a retry under the same inbox id came back after every
  cancel for six hours: the chat-path review, 2026-11-25).
- **The turn's answer** (#1340 F). Each delivered message is owed a reply by the session it went
  to (`turns`, by session: the listener may move since); the turn's answer is the
  last assistant message's text (`session.text.ended`, its parts joined). At the session's
  execution end (succeeded, failed or interrupted), one `wb chat reply --turn-answer --if-owed
  --text=<answer> --to=<id>…` per sender (#1273), which posts only where the session still owes one
  (`chat.owed`: no `from: claude` row since the message's receipt answers it by `re`, or is the
  session's own, `opencode_session`, not an `auto` post, to its sender); a turn that said nothing
  leaves it owed for the next. Then `wb chat ended <ids> --by <session>` (the messages that turn
  took, or none when `messages.jsonl` grew), after the post (#1352). A typed prompt settles what
  the user is owed, never an agent's.
- **`chat_reply`** (the tool, namespace `workbench` (`NAMESPACE`), so OpenCode's id for it, the one
  the model sees, is `workbench_chat_reply`, `REPLY_ID`: `effectiveName` in core/src/tool/runtime.ts;
  `{text, to?}`): `wb chat reply --text … --to …`
  as the calling session's root (a subagent's reply is its driver's), so `chat.caller_listens`
  (by `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`, the listener's `session`) threads it onto the messages that session
  took; wb's refusal is the tool's error.
- **The waiting line** (#1340 E). `permission.asked` and `form.created` (`formKind`: OpenCode's
  question tool's `question`, any other form `elicitation`) in the listening session or a child of
  it get `wb chat notice --tool --kind --text` after `NOTICE_AFTER_MS` 30 s, at once while away
  (`wb chat away`), one open at a time, in OpenCode's words (`OpenCode is waiting for you in the
  terminal.`); `permission.replied` and `form.replied` are the user back (`wb chat back`) and clear
  it (`wb chat notice --done`), as does `form.cancelled` or the turn's end, without `back`. A
  dialog answered within `BACK_AFTER_MS` 2 s of asking was answered by OpenCode itself (the TUI's
  autoaccept, `--auto`), so it clears without `back`. No
  dialog is answered from the phone (#1340: the relay through `permission.list`/`reply` is struck).
  The page's state line (#1355): `hold` passes `--waiting <json>` (`mod/hooks/waiting.ts`'s
  `waitingFact` over `dialogs`, the mod's one), and the poll (`POLL_MS` 2 s) holds again when that
  moved (`waitSaid`), so a dialog up 2 s shows within a poll and one answered sooner never does.
- **A question while away** (#1340 B): `execute.before` refuses the `question` tool in the listening
  session's tree with `AWAY_QUESTION` while `wb chat away` says `away`.

## Both drivers on one machine

Claude Code with the mod and OpenCode with the plugin, both installed, `/workbench` open in each
(#1363, decided 2026-11-25). Every fact two sessions share is a file under one `$WB_HOME`, locked
without regard to the driver, so most cases just work; what didn't was the three below, each
fixed, and nothing here adds a lock (no case lost work or gave a wrong result without one).

- **The plugin inside agents and wb's helpers** (refused, #1310, #1311): a global OpenCode plugin
  loads into every `opencode run` (no `OPENCODE_DISABLE_*` stops it). The layer's `"-workbench"`
  (`context.PLUGIN_OFF`, restated by `runner.rules_env`), `models.plugin_off` in wb's own OpenCode
  calls, and the `WB_TASK` no-op in both parts keep it out (*The OpenCode plugin*, *Off inside
  agents*; the real round in `RealOpenCodeRun`). The user's other plugins still load.
- **Whose task it is** (#1309): `store.caller_kind` ranks `WB_TASK`, `CLAUDECODE`, then
  `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`; a task records its driver's `session` and `driver` (an OpenCode one its
  server's pid, never `claude_pid`), so `mine`, `cli._caller` and the wakes go to the session that
  started it, and a Claude session in the same directory isn't woken for an OpenCode task.
  `chat.caller_listens` (`_listens_across`) lets only the listening driver thread a phone reply.
- **One-shot approvals** (#1314): `store.take_approval` renames the file away whether it matches
  or not, so either driver's gated call within seconds spent the other's yes unused. An OpenCode
  driver's yes is its session's own file, `route-ok.<session>.json` / `send-ok.<session>.json`
  (`store.approval_name`, the plugin's `writeApproval`), which only that session's call takes;
  Claude Code's stays `route-ok.json` / `send-ok.json`. Per session, not per pid: one OpenCode
  server runs many sessions, and the plugin's wb child carries its caller's session id.
- **Just works, traced**: a notice once, to its owner (`claim_ack` under the ack lock); accept,
  discard or feedback from the other driver (naming a task is the user's intent; listings name
  the others' apart); the GPU and the provider slots (`GpuLease`, `API_PARALLEL`, first come); the
  day cap (the keyhole's `spend-api.jsonl`, per task, counted once); away and back (`chat/away.json`
  is the user's: a prompt in either ends it); background jobs (machine-wide state, `--if-due`); the
  skill library (one lock); the pane and the modeline (the same task files); two sessions of one
  driver; sleep, `wb update` mid-task, a driver killed mid-turn (the runner is detached; `wb
  adopt`); a repo open in both.
- **Installs**: `wb doctor` names each install, Claude Code's mod and each OpenCode entry, and the
  wb each runs (*The OpenCode plugin*, *What `wb doctor` says*); uninstalling one leaves the other
  working (OpenCode's Git install runs its own wb), and `wb setup` in the clone that stays
  relinks a `~/.local/bin/wb` that pointed into the removed one.
- **Claude Code's own calls in a worktree and the OpenCode driver's** both reach `claude-calls/`
  (the mod's rows, the plugin's `calls.ts`, #1331), so `wb accept` tells either driver's hand from
  its builds.

## Waiting without polling

`workbench/watch.py`. Anything that waits for a file or a process sleeps in the kernel.

- **`Watcher(*dirs, recursive=False, skip=())`**: inotify through ctypes (`inotify_init1`,
  `inotify_add_watch` from `CDLL(None)`, so musl works) for modify, attribute, close-write, create,
  delete, moves. An overflow or a vanished directory reports every watched directory changed;
  recursive, an overflow first rewalks each root (`add(root, again=True)`, #472). `recursive` adds
  new subdirectories, never through a link, and leaves out one it can't list (#439); `skip` matches
  patterns against the path below the root. `wait(timeout, settle=0.02)` returns changed paths raw
  (duplicates, temp and lock files). A directory past `max_user_watches` is stat-polled every
  `POLL_S` 0.25 s. Without inotify (macOS, or `inotify_init1` failing) `wait` returns within a second
  whatever the timeout, so every caller loops and re-checks: callers use `wait()`, not the
  descriptor; the chat `Hub`, which selects on it beside a pidfd, switches to `wait()` when any
  directory is polled.
- **`wait_exit(pid, timeout)`**: `pidfd_open` and `select`; without pidfd (macOS, kernels before
  5.3) `kill(pid, 0)` every 0.1 s.
- Writers help: `store.write_json` renames a dot-temp file, `read_jsonl` stops at the last newline
  (a half-written row waits), `append_jsonl` holds a lock file.

Every waiter and its bounded wake (a timeout to re-check what the kernel can't signal):

| Caller | Waits on | Re-checks every |
|---|---|---|
| `wb events` | `$WB_HOME`, recursive, skipping `EVENT_SKIP` (`tasks/*/worktree`, `tasks/*/tree`, `tasks/*/rounds`, `rules`, `imports`, `images`, `audio`, `archive`, `chat/audio`, `bench/.?*`, `bench/runs`, `chat/uploads`, `bench/cases`, and `SCRATCH`: `.?*`, `wb-index-*`, `wb-merge-*`, neither watched nor reported: they took 2 watches to 605, #373, and 1,209 of 1,211, #439) and the tasks already closed when it starts | 10 s (exits when its parent changes); every minute it reaps dead runners |
| `wb wait` | the state directory and the named task's directory | 60 s (a dead runner: `reap`) |
| `wb log -f` | the task directory | 30 s |
| `wb watch` | the task directory | 1.5 s on a terminal while the task is live, 30 s otherwise; the session exported again only on a change or every 30 s while live (#555) |
| the runner's steer bell | the task directory (`steer.jsonl`) and `ask/` | 5 s, while OpenCode runs |
| `ask_reviewer` | `ask/` | 30 s (`STEP_SECS`), until the ask timeout |
| the chat `Hub` | `chat/` and the listener's pidfd (without inotify: `kill 0` each second) | 60 s |
| `wb stop` / `takeover` | `wait_exit(pid, 15)` | |
| `wb top` | `select` on its nvidia-smi stream and, on a terminal, the keys | each tick (`--every`), when it also checks its parent |

`wb events` prints `{"hello": <its pid>, "start": <its start>, "parent": <its parent's pid>,
"parent_start": …, "machine": <store.machine()>}` (the listener's identity and its Claude Code
process, #687, #922), then `{"changed": [paths relative to $WB_HOME]}` per batch, dropping names
ending `.lock`, `.tmp`, `runner.log` and dotfiles; it creates `tasks/` and `chat/`, and exits on a
broken pipe or when its parent process changes.

## Deep workflows

`deepcode <request>`, or a substantive request with deepmode on (*Dynamic workflows (deepmode)*), runs as a
**flow** of the user's agents (#1278): Claude picks or writes the flow, says it in at most three lines, runs
`wb run start` once and is woken only at checkpoints and the end. Each item is a wb task, with its lane, its
role's model, the keyhole, the meter and the day cap; OpenCode's `subagent` tool stays denied (`context.py`).
Claude has the final say (the owner's rule on #1278): every flow ends at a `final` stage, Claude's; what a
`keep` filters stays in the report; code waits at review.

**The pieces.** `schema.py` (a JSON Schema subset, checked outside the lane: `check`, `valid` refusing a keyword
it can't check, `last_object`), `cards.py` (role cards), `runs.py` (flows, runs, the driver, `wb run`, the
keywords' reference). Shipped: cards `agent/roles/` find, verify, judge (tools none), review, choose, critic, build,
fix; schemas `agent/schemas/` findings (`maxItems` 12), verdict, judgments, review, choice, triage; flows
`agent/flows/` build, audit, fix, fix-escalate, best-of, lenses, triage. The user's own come first: `$WB_ROLES`
(`~/.config/workbench/roles/`, its `schemas/`), `$WB_FLOWS` (`~/.config/workbench/flows/`). A repo's
`.workbench/flows/` is listed (`wb run flows`) as "read it first"; `--flow` never takes it, `--plan` does.
**Shadowed shipped ones** (#1295): a user's card, schema or flow with a shipped name wins (`cards.card_path`,
`runs.flow_names`), so `wb card copy|reset <name> [--schema]` and `wb flow copy|reset <name>` make the copy (its
`from` the shipped file's git blob sha, `cards.blob_sha`, computed without git) and set it aside (`.bak`, never
deleted); `wb card list` and `wb run flows` mark a copy `shadows shipped`, and `; shipped changed since` once a `wb
update` moved the shipped blob (`cards.shadow_mark`), so an improved shipped one is never lost unseen behind an
older copy (Goose's prompt templates' customized and reset).

**Report tasks** (`wb start --report`, a report card, or a run's report stage). Read-only: the lane leaves the
worktree out of `context.writable` (still readable as part of the task dir; `external_rules` allows it), the
layer's last rule denies every edit (`context.report_rules`), and `tools none` denies every tool but
`workbench_*` and `doom_loop`. With no lane the runner's check is what holds it: a report whose worktree
changed is void (`runner.REPORT_CHANGED`). The prompt is `cli.REPORT_PROTOCOL` (PROTOCOL's fold and `Lesson:`
kept), the handbook a report card's text or `context.REPORT_HANDBOOK` (`context.handbook_text`); no tests, no
auto-fix, no self-review, no diff in the notice. The object: `submit_result` (an MCP tool on the ask server,
its inputSchema the task's `rules/<task>/schema.json`; `ask_mcp.submit` checks it and writes `ask/result.json`;
OpenCode hands a tool's argument errors back to the model), else the last object in `final.md`
(`schema.last_object`: DeepSeek ended with it after prose in 31 of 31 rounds of #1278's study, and the report's
2,500-character cut lost it in 13). `runner.report_end` checks it again outside the lane: valid, it goes to
`tasks/<task>/result.json` and the review notice carries it (up to `RESULT_SHOWN` 24,000 characters) with its
source; else one repair round (`runner.SCHEMA_FIX`, a new opening: `rejected: <errors>. Resend the whole
object: …`) in the same session, even one OpenCode compacted (`fresh_reason`, #1478), then `failed`. A report
has no explore guard (the calls-without-an-edit count, which only its reading would fill: #1489); the repeat
and error guards, the wall, silence and think limits hold, the think nudge `runner.REPORT_NUDGE` (finish and
send the result, never "make the next edit"). `wb accept` takes no `-m`, commits nothing, deletes the branch while still at the
base, and records `outcome: reported`, `report: true` (`_accept_report`); `store.results()` keeps such rows
from the router, the slices and tuning.

**Role cards** are OpenCode agent Markdown (`cards.parse`, a frontmatter subset): `cards.KEYS` `description`,
`tools` (read, none, code; `readonly` is read), `schema`, `steps`, `skills`, `ask`, `role`, `est` `{in, out,
min}`. `permissions` and `model` are dropped and said (`cards.said_dropped`). The text is at most
`cards.BODY_MAX` 3,000 bytes. A report card's text stands in HANDBOOK.md's place; a code card's goes after it
under `## Your role` (`cards.handbook`). `steps` go on the task's own `wb-code` agent entry (`runner.rules_env`),
so the layer's denies still come last. task.json `card` fixes the card at start.

**Flows** (`runs.validate`; `runs.FLOW_KEYS`, `STAGE_KEYS`, `PLACES`; the format in
`skill/workbench/reference/deep.md`): `v` 1, params typed (`runs.PARAM_TYPES`, `parse_params`: a bare type, or
an object of `runs.PARAM_KEYS` `{type, description, default, choices, optional}` as Goose's recipe parameters,
#1295: a param left out takes its `default`, or stays absent when `optional`; `choices` for a string or int),
`command` (below), `from` (a copy's), stages
`items` or `from` (+ `split`), `keep`, `flow` pipeline|barrier, `batch`, `attempts`, `refix`, `on_failure`,
`max_items` (`MAX_ITEMS` 200, the rest `not_run`, named), `claude`, `final`, and `prompt` (the item's spec, by
default `{item}`; `runs.render` only substitutes, an object as fenced JSON, each place cut at `runs.CUTS`, said).
Over a code stage (`runs.CODE_PLACES`) a report's prompt may carry `{diff}` and `{report}`: the reviewed round's
report (`store.Task.report`: the coder's summary and test line, `runs._code_report`), so a review after a refix
reads the coder's "done, or declined with why" (the shipped build, fix and best-of reviews carry it; #1134's
study found reasoned declines asked again until `max` ran out). **A batch** (`batch` N): each member is
`runs.member`, its key as `id` (an object's own `id` replaced, anything else under `item`), and its schema
`runs.batch_schema`: the answer list (`runs.answers_key`, the first top-level array of objects requiring `id`)
exactly N long, each `id` one of the batch's, written to `runs/<run>/schemas/<stage>-<n>.json` and passed as
`--schema`, so an invented, missing or extra id gets the one repair round. A member still unanswered (a
duplicate in its place) goes under `not_run` as `unjudged` (`runs.unanswered`); a batch's trail lists its
members as its judge was given them, and a null batch names them (`members`). Before, lenses' and triage's
judgments reached Claude without what they judged, by ids the judge invented, a skipped one gone.
**A compare stage** (`compare: true`, a report over a code stage with `attempts` of 2 or more; no split,
batch, attempts or refix): one item per item of the code stage, once all its attempts ended, its members the
attempts that reached review (fewer than two: `not_run`, nothing to compare). Its prompt's `{diffs}`
(`runs._diffs_of`) carries each attempt's diff as `### a<k> (task <t>; tests passed|failed|no tests)`, each
cut to its share of `CUTS['diff']`; only the green ones when two or more are, the rest named
(`runs._attempts`); its schema `runs.compare_schema`: `best` and `ranking` one of the labels shown. The
shipped best-of is code → review → choose (the `choose` card, `choice` schema `{best, ranking, why}`) →
Claude, whose final row carries the pick and, as its trail, every attempt's task: nothing is discarded on
the chooser's word (#1134's study: Claude read every review and most diffs, N times the handoff; SWE-agent's
Chooser).
**Escalation** (`escalate: [roles]` on a code stage, 1 to `ESCALATE_MAX` 3 distinct `routes.ROLES`): an item
that ends null (stuck, failed, discarded), or whose review's asks are left once refix's `max` is spent (`_take`
journals `escalate` {stage, key, task, why} and supersedes that review: `escalated: …`; the attempt's task
stays at review for Claude), is tried again from the base as `<key>#e<k>` on the k-th role (`runs.escalation`,
`escalation_key`, `item_role`: `wb start --role`; `stage_model(stage, it)` for its room, budget and
`request_floor`), its start journalled `escalated` {key, after, role}; a stuck code item checkpoints Claude only
when it was the last role's, and `wb run start` refuses an escalate API role with no day cap as it does the
stage's, its line `<stage> <role> (GPU|API), then <roles>`. Shipped: `fix-escalate` (fix on trivial, then
significant). An escalated item past `max_items` still runs (its item counted once).
**A `files` param** (#1295) is a pathspec (or several, comma separated), matched by git's own rules against the
files committed at the run's base (`gitops.files_at`: `ls-files` over a scratch index read from the commit,
outside the lane, in the run's repo only; never the user's index or an uncommitted file), each match an item
`{file, name, stem, dir}` (`runs.file_item`; `dir` `.` at the root), at most `runs.FILES_MAX` 1,000 (refused past
it: narrow it; the stage's `max_items` cut still names the rest). **`unless_exists`**, on a stage whose `items`
is a files param only, is a path template of `{item.<file|name|stem|dir>}` and the params (`runs.unless_errors`):
the paths that exist at the base are found once at the start (`runs.existing`, one `gitops.paths_at`; run.json
`exists`), and each such item is `not_run`, `exists at base: <path>`, counted to no `max_items` and priced at
nothing; no new state. **A dry run** (`wb run start … --dry-run`, `runs.dry_run`) validates, parses the params,
checks the caps and the budget, and prints each stage, each items stage's first spec (`DRY_SPEC_CUT` 1,500) and
the estimate, writing and starting nothing: the estimate Claude says before a start (SKILL.md *Deep workflows*).
**A flow's slash command** (#1295): `command`, one lowercase word (`runs.COMMAND_RE`), never `workbench*`, wb's
`deepmode` or a host's built-in (`runs.RESERVED_COMMANDS`, Claude Code's and OpenCode's TUI's), nor another flow's
of another name (`runs.command_errors`, over `_commands_on_disk`), and only on the user's and shipped flows: `wb
run flows --json` (`runs.flow_rows`) gives a repo's none, nor one a flow `validate` refuses. Both hosts register
each as `/<command>` at a session's or server's start (a flow saved later: the next start or reload) and answer it
with a `[workbench]` turn (`mod/hooks/flows.ts`'s `FLOW_NOTE`, both hosts' one copy): start `wb run start <run>
--flow <flow> --args '<the line as typed>'`. The line is parsed once, in Python (`runs.parse_args`, held to
`tests/fixtures/flow_args.json`): a flow with one param takes it whole (a leading `<k>=` dropped), else `k=v`
words, shell quoted. Goose's required/optional rule doesn't apply: a param's own `default` and `optional` decide.
Refused: an unknown key or placeholder, a last stage that isn't `final`, and after a code stage anything but a
report over its `{diff}`. Run names `runs.RUN_RE` (24), stage ids `STAGE_RE` (8): `<run>-<stage>-<n>` fits a task
name, and the run a `--group`. A run and a task never share a name (`runs.taken`, `cmd_start`).

**The driver** (`runs.drive`, `python -X utf8 -m workbench.runs drive <run>`, detached by `cli.detach` as
bench's, under its `drive` lock; `runs.spawn`). Each pass (`runs.tick`, woken by its run directory, at most
`TICK_S` 30 s; its counts and spend go to `status.json` only when one changed, `_write_status`: a write every
pass woke the driver itself, 20 passes a second while an item ran): it takes its items' notices (`_ack_items`: an open run's item, its driver alive
(`runs.item_open`), notifies `runs/<run>/notify.jsonl` with its `noticed` mark, `store.Task.notify`, and the
driver claims each ack up to it, so neither the mod's wake nor its idle net wakes Claude for one; with the driver
dead an item's notice is Claude's, a task's as any), refuses an item's open ask at once (`runs.RUN_REFUSED`,
`ask_mcp.answer_once`, as the bench's `REFUSED`: nobody is told of it, and a finder's ask for a path held the GPU its
20-minute `ask_timeout` in the real GPU audit, 2026-11-26), reaps dead runners, resumes an item stopped from outside
its step whose cause passes or is the user's to lift (`_held`, `runs._outside`: `cli._interrupted`, a restart, a
killed runner, a shutdown's signal, an update, or `cli.stopped_outside` in `runs.held_infra`: the day cap in a
round, a provider's rate limit, outage or refusal, a repo made local-only, `wb stop --all`; `wb resume`, journal
`resumed` `by: driver`). The rest of `cli.stopped_outside`'s, a model that failed, a setup, a crash, a full disk,
the repo gone, OpenCode unusable, end the item as its own failure (its stage's `on_failure`, `null` by default),
as `wb resume --all` leaves them (`cli.INTERRUPTED`). A resume refused with exit 3
(the cap, local-only, Agents on the GPU) holds the item (journal `held`) and pauses the run, or under
`--overnight` with the cap's `meter.RESETS` is tried again each pass, so past midnight it goes on; any other
refusal is its null. A second stop from outside after the driver's resume (a spend stop aside) is a checkpoint,
Claude's, its work kept; while the run isn't `running` the item waits for `wb run resume`. It takes each report item that ended (`_take`: its object to `outputs/`,
through `keep`, then `wb accept`; a refix `wb feedback --text` with the `must_fix` list, at most `max`, the review
`superseded`; a failed one discarded, `null`), raises a checkpoint for a code item stuck or failed, then starts
what is ready (`runs.state`, rebuilt
each pass from the flow, the journal and the tasks: a pipeline item once its input is in, a barrier's once all
are) and has room (`_room`: `IN_FLIGHT` 6 items; an API stage's provider slots, `cli._api_slots_free`, and none
while a task of the user's waits for one, `cli._api_pending`; on the GPU one waiting item per stage). Each start
is `wb start <run>-<stage>-<n> --spec specs/… --role R --queue --group <run> --run --stage --item --checkin 0`,
a report's with `--report --card --schema --tools --ask-budget 0 --no-self-review --no-base-check --setup ''`
(`runs._start`), a subprocess, so refusals are the user's: an exit 3 that is the day cap's own (`meter.RESETS`,
"it resets at local midnight", anywhere in what wb start said) pauses the run, or under `--overnight` is tried
again each tick (journal `retry`); any other exit 3 (no cap, no price, an unreadable routes.json, which say "day
cap" too and never clear) is `not_run`; a start that timed out (124) once its task exists is the item's,
running (a runner that never came is reaped, a stop from outside); else `null`. The journal row comes first, so a
crash adopts the item.

**Budgets.** Dollars: `--budget-usd`, else the flow's, else today's cap left (said at start); the cap itself
still checks every start. Before each API start `meter.run_total` (one pass over the ledger for the run's tasks)
plus `meter.request_floor` past the budget pauses the run (`run_paused`); plan and free models count $0. GPU
minutes: `--budget-min`, the items' `active_s`. `--overnight` (needs `--budget-usd`) keeps trying past the day
cap's midnight instead of pausing. A stage on an API role with no cap refuses the start (`meter.no_cap`).
The run's budgets are checked before each start only: items already running finish their rounds, so a run can
end past `--budget-usd` by what they spend (the day cap still stops every one).
The estimate: each card's `est` × `meter.price` for the stages whose items are known (`runs.estimate`).

**Notices** (`runs.Run.notify`; *Waking Claude, exactly once*): `run_checkpoint`, `run_done`, `run_paused`,
`run_stopped`, `run_failed`, each text the wake whole, opening `[workbench] Run `<run>` <headline>:`
(`runs.HEADLINE`; the opening `spend.RUN_WAKE_OPENING`), which `spend.RUN_WAKE` charges to the run's tasks (its journal's, `runs.tasks_of`, archived
too; never by the name's prefix, which charged a user's own `<run>-x`). Each row is `{ts, run, kind, phase,
text}`, no `task`: `phase` (`runs.NOTICE_PHASE`) is the run's phase it was raised in, and a notice is still true
only while the run is in it (a pause since resumed, a checkpoint since fed, is acknowledged unsaid). Both hosts
deliver them (#1278's S9) as a task's, to the session the run is `mine` to (run.json's `session` and
`session_kind`, else by directory: a scheduled run's is the session near its repo; the kernel's `owns`), once,
while still true, however old (a run has no rewake, so the hour a task's notice is due within left a run done
overnight unsaid, #1491): core.ts's `runNoticesDue` (the kernel's `noticesDue` over the run rows, keyed by run:
each run's newest, `noticed`) and
`runNoticePlan` (`noticePlan`, its kind the raised-in phase), the mod's `deliverRuns` (register.tsx) and the
plugin's `NoticeLane.deliverRuns` (notices.ts), held through a busy turn, the text the wake whole, a toast
`workbench: run <run> <RUN_HEADLINE>`. The claim is `wb ack <run> <ts> --run` (`Run.claim_ack`, the
compare-and-set `wb wait` shares), and a dropped wake's rollback `wb ack <run> <prev> --run --if <ts>`
(`Run.release_ack`); with no rewake for a run, the mod reads notify.jsonl again at its next poll. `wb wait <run>`
and `wb wait` take them too (`runs.due`, skipping one no longer true): the skill's wait without the mod (or with
the plugin's `wake` off), as `wb run start`'s last line says. The web app's Stop (`wb run stop` under
`WB_ACTOR=web`, the Settings run row) stops the run as `runs.WEB_STOP` and raises a `run_stopped` for its
session; Claude's own `wb run stop` raises none. A driver that died with the run open (a reboot, a kill) is found by `wb status`, `wb
run status` or `wb wait` (`runs.reap`, after a 5 s grace): `stopped`, one `run_stopped`. A restart's or `wb update
--stop`'s batch notice (`cli._restart_notice`, `_stop_for_update`) holds a run's items apart from the user's own
tasks (`cli._batch_key`: the owner, and the run): one batch led by a run item went to the run and acknowledged
the user's tasks with it. A run batch's text names `wb run resume <run>`; its dead driver's run is stopped with
it, quietly (`runs.reap(quiet=True)`, journal `reaped`), the items' notice the one wake; `wb update --stop` stops
the drivers of the runs whose items it stops first (`runs.stop`, `items=False`).

**Resume** goes on from the journal by stage and item: valid outputs kept, live runners adopted, and the items a
stop or an interruption left (`runs._resume_items`, `_resumable`: `wb run stop`'s, journal `stopped`, and not
Claude's own `wb stop <item>`, which leaves the same `last`; and those failed or stuck from outside, `_outside`;
a live runner reaped first, quietly) `wb resume`d, journal `resumed` `by:
resume`: by the new driver as it starts, alive so their notices are its, or by `_resume` under a live one. A
closed run, or one at `review`, never goes on (`runs._ended`; `wb run feed` asks before it writes the inbox).
**Close** refuses while a code item is open. `wb stop --all` and `wb takeover --all` (the hand-back) stop runs' drivers (#1471); while a run is open, a code item Claude took over (status `taken_over`) is `not_run` (`runs.TAKEN_OVER`, `runs._live`), never done, so no next stage reviews, refixes or approves the diff Claude is editing; once the run has ended, its report keeps the item as it was. `wb gc` archives closed runs.
`wb top --json`'s `runs` (`runs.snapshot`) is the pane's and the web's seam. **A slash command as a flow**: `wb
flow import X.md` (`runs.import_command`) writes a flow of yours (`$WB_FLOWS/<name>.json`, or `--out`): one stage
over the list param `items` (a code stage, or `--card`'s), its prompt the command's body with `$ARGUMENTS` as
`{item}` (appended when absent) and its own braces kept as text, `description` from the frontmatter; a positional
`$1` is refused. **The host side**: the keywords, `/deepmode` and the flows' own slash commands are in both hosts (*The keywords*, under
*Dynamic workflows (deepmode)*; the mod's `registerFlows`, the plugin's `flows.ts`), and so are the run notices'
wake (above). The web app has the runs strip over the thread (`chat.open_runs` in the state, *The web chat*) and
the Settings group `workflows` (*The admin table (settings.py)*): deepmode, a row per run not closed with its Stop
and its Summary, and the flows. `runs.keywords`, `tests/fixtures/keywords.json`, `runs.DEEPCODE_RULE` (`wb
deepmode --rule`), the run rows and `wb top --json`'s `runs` are the hosts' seam.

## Every `wb` command

`workbench/cli.py` is argparse: one subparser per command, `set_defaults(f=cmd_<name>)`, dispatched
as `a.f(a)`; a new command is a parser block plus a `cmd_*`. `die(msg, code=1)` prints `wb: <msg>`
on stderr. Exit codes: 1 an error; 2 a usage error, or `wait` on a closed task, with no open task
or at a timeout; 3 no model can run (`start`); 4 is no longer used (a start the GPU or a
provider's slots can't take yet queues, #1322); 5 an accept whose merge failed; `scout --due` 0 when due, 1 when not;
`doctor` 0/1. Errors wb raises (`RuntimeError`, a config that doesn't parse, an unreadable file:
`wb: <path>: No such file or directory`) print as a message, never a traceback. Any other exception is a bug:
its traceback, then `wb crashed: a bug in workbench. Claude can fix it for you as a local patch (wb patch) and offer it
upstream (<root>/CONTRIBUTING.md)` (`OpenCode's model` for `Claude` from an OpenCode driver: `patches.driver_name`, #1321), exit 1 (*Local patches*); in-process (`main(argv)`, the tests) it propagates, as
a crash caught as `SystemExit` passed ~160 refusal tests (#1005). `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` pass through. cli writes
notify.jsonl only in `reap` (`_restart_notice`) and `wb update --stop` (`_stop_for_update`); the
runner writes the rest (#882). `wb --version`: `workbench.__version__`.

**Acknowledging.** `_ack_all(task)` moves the task's `acked` mark, never back, under the task's `ack`
lock (the one `claim_ack` takes; unlocked, a `wb ack` between read and write was written over and a
question delivered twice, #786). With an unacked notice of the kind the phase stands for
(`question` while `asking`, `checkin` while queued/running/testing, else the phase name), it stops
just before the oldest, so unseen news stays deliverable (else to now) (a `wb note` once swallowed a failure for
an hour). Called by feedback, rewind, next, answer, allow, note, resume, takeover, accept, discard, stop;
not by steer, `skill hand|take`, diff, report, log. `upto=t` (answer, allow answering a request,
feedback, next, resume) moves it to when the command acted, still stopping before another open
question (`ask_mcp.is_open`). `feedback`, `next` and `resume` act on a task one at a time
(`one_at_a_time`), refuse a gone worktree (`_need_worktree`: `wb discard <task> --keep-branch`), and
mark notes the last runner never delivered as taken (`_stale_notes`, *Notes*).

### Running tasks
| Command | Flags (defaults) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `wb start <task> --spec <file\|->` | `--repo` (.), `--role significant\|trivial\|writing` (from `--size`: trivial, else significant), `--size trivial\|significant` (from `--role`: trivial for the trivial role, else significant; both given, the role picks the model and the size the slice and the GPU router's size), `--model <id or fragment>`, `--test <cmd>` (granted to the shell too: `context.test_allowances`; after the repo's commands.json `test`, `context.with_repo_test`: `<repo's> && <--test>`, a part a shell would split otherwise (`;`, a newline, `||`, a lone `&`) in parentheses, one already in `--test` not twice, the whole one command task.json `test_cmd` and the start line's `tests`; a report task runs none; #1295), `--auto-fix N` (2 on the GPU, 1 on API: `cli.AUTO_FIX`, `cli.auto_fix`; a given value is kept and the start line prints the one used, #1017), `--self-review`/`--no-self-review` (the `self_review` knob), `--checkin MIN` (0 off), `--ask-budget N` (2), `--ask-timeout S` (1200), `--round-timeout S`, `--silence-timeout S` (unset or 0: measured budgets), `--think-timeout S` (0 off), `--test-timeout S` (900), `--unload-for-tests` (task.json `unload_for_tests`: every model on the GPU but `keep_loaded` let go before each test run, the GPU held meanwhile, the GPU held from other tasks while tests run, a remote model's tests too, #428, #943, its device nodes in the lane, `context.gpu_nodes`), `--no-sign` (task.json `sign: false`; without it `gitops.sign_problem` and `gitops.presence_signer` are said at start), `--no-base-check` (`no_base_check`; else `--test` runs once on the base first, *The base check*), `--base REF` (HEAD), `--skill NAME…` (and the repo's commands.json `skills` after them; one not in the library `note: commands.json "repos" skills <names>: not in the library (wb skill list), left out`, #1295), `--allow PATTERN…`, `--allow-path DIR…`, `--allow-port N…` (grants `ports`: a port the lane refuses, *What TCP reaches*; the bench's replays, a case's `ports`), `--setup CMD`, `--setup-timeout S` (1800, `setup_timeout`), `--copy PATH…`, `--sibling PATH…` (*Setting the worktree up*), `--force` (queue a `--model` that can't run now), `--queue` (accepted, a no-op: a start queues by default, #1322), `--trial`, `--local-only` (task.json `local_only`: an API model is refused for this task, as for a repo commands.json marks local-only, *Privacy for API roles*), `--backlog NAME` (task.json `backlog`; a finished batch's name, its newest start `BACKLOG_GAP` 6 h old, is refused with a dated one, `cli._backlog_done`, #880), `--after HH:MM` (`cli.after_time`: the next such local time, today's while ahead, else tomorrow's; task.json `not_before`, epoch seconds; implies `--queue`, and skips the bench preemption, the busy opt-in's move and the GPU's and slots' notes, the room now saying nothing of then; *Scheduled runs*, #1204), `--group NAME` (task.json `group`: one request's fan-out, *Dynamic workflows*; `cli.GROUP_RE`, a task name's characters up to 32, else refused before anything is made, `cli._check_group`, #1048), `--image PATH` (repeatable, at most `cli.IMAGE_MAX` 4: an image the agent sees, #1199; | `wb accept <task> -m "…"` (a report task: no `-m`, *Deep workflows*) | `--include`, `--no-sign`, `--merge`, `--merge-as merge\|ff\|squash` (implies `--merge`; commands.json `repos` `merge` sets the default, without implying it), `--force` (any open phase; stops a live runner), `--spec-gap`, `--take-claude-md` | Reaps; a moved repo refused first (#498). Review only; a closed one only when status `unrecorded` (`_finish_record`, #88). A live task with nothing changed on its first step is refused before its runner stops; past the base, nothing changed since the last commit (`cli._to_commit`: git's changes, ignored files written, edits in a filled submodule, #1307) accepts that commit, its `accepted` line ending `(-m unused: nothing changed since <commit>)` unless a squash took the message (`closing`'s `message`, #1393); a failed commit leaves it `stuck`, not live with no runner. Commits `<m>` + "Delegated to <label> via OpenCode: R round(s), F automatic test-fix, V review round(s)." + `Workbench-Task:` + `OpenCode-Session:` (no AI co-author line); the step is measured from where it began (`gitops.step_base`: a retry past accept's commit, #879, or past an interrupted wb next's, #1302), and a retry puts `delegate/<task>` on that commit (`gitops.put_on_branch`, refused when the branch holds commits it lacks, #417). Ignored files changed since the agent stopped, or by its shell (#1210), that the commit leaves out are copied to `left-out/` first and named (`cli._keep_left`, #1179's review). Removes the worktree and runtime dir, records `tip`, keeps base..tip in `steps.bundle` (`gitops.bundle_steps`; `refs/workbench/accepted/<task>`, `gitops.keep_accepted`, only if it fails, #799, deleted once a merge lands the tip, else by gc). `--merge`: *Git, commits and projects* (`gitops.merge_lock`; failure: the accept stands, exit 5 `NOT_MERGED`, #247). A retry resumes from status `closing` (#246) while the worktree is gone or clean (`cli._gained_work`); meanwhile (`cli._accepting`) discard, feedback, next, resume and takeover refuse it (#878: discard recorded committed work as discarded); a merge already made is found by ancestry (`gitops.contains`), a squash by `closing`'s `merge_from` (#432); what a SIGKILLed merge left in the checkout is quit or backed out first (`gitops.clear_killed_merge`, #1231), once that try's signing git, if still waiting, is ended (`closing`'s `merge_git`, #1246). Writes the row, drops the rules and the review trees' refs (`_closed`); prints `the repo has no CLAUDE.md: write one (wb init)` when it has none (nor a committed AGENTS.md, #1513) and, for an API task, what it paid at the end of its `accepted` line (`savings.paid`: `· paid ≈$0.12`), nothing else (#1322). Under `WB_SCHEDULE` (a scheduled run's headless Claude) `--merge` and `--merge-as` are refused before anything (*Scheduled runs*, #1204). |
| `wb relocate <task> --repo <dir>` | | Refuses a repo without the base or a linked worktree; refuses a `.git` naming another git dir; repairs the link (`git worktree repair`), rewrites `gitdir.json`, task.json `repo`, `git_common`, `cwd`, `submodules.json` (`gitops.relocate`, #498, #682). |
| `wb discard <task>` | `--reason "…"`, `--spec-gap`, `--keep-branch`, `--drop-steps` | Stops, records, removes worktree, runtime dir, rules and review refs (`_closed`) and branch (`deleted (was <sha>)`, status `tip`, in the repo `gitops.repo_of` finds), not with `--keep-branch`, a moved repo, or committed steps unless `--drop-steps` (#494; then accept's merge line for them, #1174); a cut-short checkout's only while `branch_made` holds (#416). A run's compare attempt another attempt beat (accepted first) is recorded `not_chosen` (#1473). Closed: refused unless `unrecorded`. An API task's `paid` ends its line, as accept's. |

|---|---|---|
