Writes `workbench-patch-<slug or short sha>-<UTC %Y%m%d>[-n].zip` (`-2`, `-3`… beside one already there) in `~/Downloads` when that directory exists, else `$WB_HOME/patches/out/` (`patches.zip_out`), through a `.part` file renamed into place: a folder of that name holding one `git format-patch --no-signature` file per commit (`DIFF_PLAIN`, `0001-…`) and `README.txt` (`ZIP_README`: the commits' subjects, the base, `merge-base local local@{u}`, `git switch -c` and `git am <this folder>/*.patch`, `UPSTREAM_CONTACT`, and that the From: lines name the authors). Prints `wrote <path>: N patch(es) on upstream's <base>`, `email it to adam.schaefers@icloud.com, or send it any way you like; nothing was sent`, and `the patch files name the commit author (<name> <email>[, …]); edit them before sending if you'd rather not`. Not an outward command: the mod's gate doesn't ask (the kernel's `gateOf` gives it no gate, neither `outward` nor `send`). No abbreviated flags. |
| `wb driver [beat]` | `--session ID` (that session's, the plugin's RPC; else the caller's `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`, else every live one), `--model REF` (the model the session runs on next, `provider/id#variant`, over its beat's: the TUI's selection, `driver.selected`; a session's only, exit 1 without one or for a ref that isn't one), `--once` (each note said once, `drivers/said.json`), `--json` | *The driver*: `driver: <id> (GPU\|API) · session <id>` and a `note:` line each; from a terminal every session that drove in `DRIVER_HOLD` and the `pin:` line; under Claude Code `driver: Claude Code (fixed)`. `beat` (no flag): the plugin's heartbeat on stdin, written by `driver.write_beat` (exit 1 `no heartbeat written: …`) |
| `wb doctor` | | `ok`/`BAD` set the exit code, `--` informs: opencode (`runner.OPENCODE_TESTED`), git (`gitops.GIT_FLOOR` 2.34), models (an Ollama cloud one: `--  <id> is an Ollama cloud model, an API model now: set a role to use it`, #1013), `limit.context`, the roles (`BAD <path> can't be read (…)`, else `--  roles: <summary> (wb route)` once any is set, #1014; then each role on API, `ok  <role> role: <id> ready` or `BAD` with wb start's own refusal, `routes.resolve` and `routes.cant_run`: no key, a key wb can't hold, gone from the catalog, out of credit, no price, the day cap, `cli._api_role_lines`, #1067; with a role on API, the keys, `cli.api_key_lines`); with every role on API, no local model and no OpenCode config read `--` (`--  0 local model(s): every role runs on API`), not `BAD`, `optimize.advice`, `router.thinking_stall`, the state dir (2 GB, `store.host_drive`), `idle_line` (`IDLE_DAYS` 3), `models.unheld_loaded`, the lane (`context.interop_gap`, `context.home_gap`: doctor's alone, #1322; `lane.gaps`, what the lane breaks for the agent's tools; from ABI 4 `_tcp_refused`'s `local daemons' TCP ports are out of the lane (N ports)`, *What TCP reaches*), commands.json, each MCP server it names (`ok  MCP server <name> (commands.json): the agents of every task|<repos>`, else `BAD` with wb start's refusal, `cli._mcp_named`, #1202; `--  MCP server '<name>' names <path>, in the repo …` for one whose command names a path in a repo its tasks run in, `context.mcp_checkout_notes`, with a lane on), what the agents get (`cli.setup_lines` over `context.agent_setup` and `setup_said`, *What reaches the agent, listed*, #1295: `--  agents get <each source that reaches, its size; a plugin's tools>: about NK tokens with OpenCode's own, before a task's project files and spec (wb start counts those)` and `--  kept from agents: N skills denied by name (Claude's, ~/.agents', `workbench`), <each dropped or denied source>`), `context.TOOLCHAINS`, `wb` on PATH (the plugin's launcher, `cli.plugin_launcher`, said as such and never as another copy; not on PATH with the mod installed, a `--` line for the user's own terminal, not BAD, #1190; nor on the OpenCode path alone, the mod not listed and the OpenCode plugin installed or wb run from OpenCode's install, `--  wb isn't on this shell's PATH: OpenCode's plugin runs its own (its line below says which); for your own terminal, …` (a clone's and `bin/wb setup --opencode` from OpenCode's install, else `wb setup --opencode`'s link), #1321's finding 26) and which wb the mod runs (`the mod runs WB_BIN=…`, `it by name` with `, else ~/.local/bin/wb where its PATH has no wb` when that link is there, or off PATH `~/.local/bin/wb (wb setup's link)`: `cli.mod_wb`, #1200), `cli.logout_stops`, the web app (`cli.chat_line`: `ok`, `--` off, or `BAD web app down: …`, *The web chat*; after its `ok`, with a `tailscale` on PATH and the web app on this machine alone, `--  ` + the story's `link.reach`, #1355), each schedule (`schedule.doctor_lines`: `ok  schedule <name> (<when>): last <its last run>`, `BAD` with claude (a backlog's: a flow's needs none, `schedule.needs`, #1295) or opencode not on the unit's PATH, the wb its unit runs gone (`schedule.newest_wb`: `its wb is gone (<path>): wb schedule rm <name>, then add`, the unit's and not this wb's, #1497) or its unit gone, #1204; on WSL with a schedule or the web app on, `--  ` + `schedule.WSL_IDLE`, #1511), `cli.awake_line`, `webpush.has_cas` (with push subscriptions or any API role: the keyhole's context is `webpush.tls()`, #1080), the mod (`cli._mod_behind`; #1061's note on Claude's own files went, #1322: the release notes carry it), each install of the OpenCode plugin and the wb it runs (`ocplugin.doctor_lines`, *The OpenCode plugin*; with the plugin, or wb run from OpenCode's install, and no Claude Code mod, a missing `skills/workbench` is a `--` line, not BAD), then `patches.doctor_lines` (from OpenCode's install instead `ok  install: OpenCode's, at P: OpenCode updates it (…)`, `ocplugin.updated_by`): `ok  install: marketplace at P`, `your own clone at P, branch B (wb patch init)` (on `local`, or patches.json's `source`) or `developer clone at P, branch B`; `--  local patches: N (scopes)` (a clone on `local`; on `local` tracking nothing, `--  local patches: branch local tracks no upstream: git -C P branch -u origin/main local (wb update sets it)`, #1327; a marketplace clone: its local changes and `wb patch init`); `gh: ready as L over P` (`ok`) or `--  gh: <state>: <hint>`, asked only with patches or a `wb patch upstream` branch that hasn't landed upstream (`held`, `_landed_pr`, by the local refs alone); none sets the exit code. Then each experiment. |

## Files and formats

```
$WB_HOME (~/.local/state/workbench)
  notify.jsonl                   notices that need Claude, all tasks (the runner writes them)
  notify.old.jsonl               handled notices older than ARCHIVE_DAYS, moved by gc (_rotate_notices); past NOTIFY_OLD_MAX its newest half kept
  claude-sessions/<pid>          "<ts> <session id>" lines after a "start <its start>" line (#787): sessions a Claude Code process ran wb in (spend.sessions, cli._caller)
  drivers/opencode-<machine_tag>-<pid>.json   one per OpenCode server, the workbench plugin's server part's every 30 s through wb driver beat (#1309, #1316, driver.write_beat): {tool: "opencode", pid, machine?, store?, ts, sessions: {<id>: {model?, variant?, dir?, used?}}}, `model` the session's last primary request's or its selection, `used` that request's time (epoch s; store.driver_models, #1317), `store` the server's database, `sessions` every session in it when the listing began (`ts`), no `store` when it can't list them all (*The heartbeat*); store.beat_path, read by store.heartbeats (which removes this machine's files whose pid exited), store.driver_server
  drivers/said.json              {<note key>: ts}: the driver's notes said once (wb driver --once, driver.once; the newest SAID_KEEP 400, *The driver*)
  gc.json                        the last gc: {at, archived, notices, rules, runtime, scratch, starts, uploads, branches, refs, …}
  archive/<task>/                a task closed and untouched for ARCHIVE_DAYS (30), moved by gc
  coding.json                    {mode: only|ask|decide, ts}; none: decide
  settings-changes.jsonl  .lock  a Settings change that went through (settings.record, from cli.main's one log writer for every caller, #1355; the web app's since #1280, wb settings set's since #1287):
                                 {ts, key, label, from, to, said, help?, by: "web"|"claude"|"opencode"|"agent"|"terminal"}; `help` the note asking Claude to
                                 offer to set it up (settings.HELP); the mod tells Claude of the web's (#1283)
  experiments.json  .lock        wb experiment: {<name>: "on"|"off"}; probe's old levels adaptable|moderate|aggressive, or true: on; else off
  probe-languages.json           {probe (real path), version, languages, at} from `probe search --help`; re-read when path or version differs (context.probe_languages)
  progress.json                  progress checks' opt-in: {on, after?, ts}; none: off
  splash.json                    the pane's opening (wb splash): {on, ts}; on unless "on": false
  workflows.json                 Dynamic workflows (deepmode; wb deepmode, wb workflows, #1041, #1278): {deepmode: on|off, ts}; none: off; 2.1's {mode, ts} read as off (#1507)

                                 session? (Claude Code's, or an OpenCode driver's with session_kind: opencode, #1309), claude_pid?, claude_start?, skip?}; status.json {phase running|checkpoint|paused|stopped|review|closed|failed,
                                 why, pid, start, machine, spawned, stages {<id>: {done, running, null, filtered, not_run}}, spent_usd, gpu_min,
                                 budget_usd, budget_min, updated_at}; journal.jsonl ({ts, kind start|item|retry|output|null|not_run|refix|escalate|escalated|fed|amend|notice|resumed|reaped,
                                 stage?, key?, n?, task?, state?, why?, src?, round?, by? (resumed: driver|resume), ok?}); inbox/<stage>-feed (wb run feed's list); outputs/<stage>-<n>.json
                                 {key, input, result, task}; specs/<stage>-<n>.md (each item's spec); schemas/<stage>-<n>.json (a batch's schema, runs.batch_schema); notify.jsonl (its items' notices, the driver's);
                                 result.json (runs.report_of at the end); acked (its notices taken); driver.log

  speed-api.json  speed-api.lock each API model's write speeds and times to first token (the account's, #1017)
```
